#49365 18 2005-02-05T08:03:52Z Teedle
You get the bug by doing THIS:

(Unless my memory fails me....)

Basically, you do what you normally do to make a teleporter (super- charged jump pad). As in, you change the number at the end (or second from the end) to a higher number than it is. (as in: 0,-1 goes to 0,-5)

Then you change the number at the very beginning, right after the !, the one that signifies that it's a launch pad, to the one that signifies that the object is a Ninja. The object that signifies a Ninja is, I think, 5... but I may be wrong.

You can also fiddle with tiles- change them to lower case for some interesting effects. Or, you can fiddle with zap drones by, for example, putting a 7 as their second last digit (e.g. 3,0,0,2 --> 3,0,7,2) so that they dissapear, and all you can see is the eye moving around the course. And the first paragraph explains how to make super- charged launch pads- you can do the same thing, but with decimals (As in 0,-0.2) to make little bouncy thingies.

And you can also make thwumps electrocute you on wierd sides (as in, sides that aren't where the blue strips are) except that I've forgotten how... just involves some messing around with code.

Oh yeah- if you want to find an object, the last object you placed is the last object in the script.

Have I forgotten anything...... ?????????

#2382 1 2005-04-01T13:17:41Z Teedle
Well, here is my idea for a new competition... I hope ya enjoy it.

RULES
1. All DDAs must use provided tilest
2. No tiles may be changed- except for those blocked by a one way
3. The one ways may not be deleted- unless being replaced by a block
4. 1 entry per person. If you create a totally kickass one after submitting your first, you may post that as a replacement.
5. The ninja must end on the door (and complete the thingo)
5. The judges (aka my decision) is final.

SCORING

Part 1
{No. of frames (multiplied by) y} / deaths in 6 runs
Total + bonuses = grand total

So... X is relevant to the amount of enemies you place. Enemies must be activated and/ or used (with exception to, obviously, mines.) So, a level layerd with inactive thwumps around the edge or rockets, lasers and gauss turrets behind locked/ trapped doors shall not score high. Scoring for enemies is as folows:
1 point for gauss turrets
1 point for thwumps
1.5 points for non- homing zap drones
2 points for lasers
2 points for rockets
2.5 points for homing zap drones
4 points for Chain Guns
0.2 points for mines
0.2 points for bouncy blocks
Please do not spam mines, or layer any of the above items

I will test each level 6 times, and out of that I shall divide your score up to this point by the number of times, in those runs, N dies before reaching the exit. If he dies 5 out of 6 (or more) you are automatically disqualified.

And, for bonuses,
+ 400 for each instance (as in, groups) of using doors as propulsion
+ 1000 for each time N gets hit by an enemy, but survives. (Only applicable once per enemy.)
+ 2500 if N survives (permanently) after completing a level
+ (Up to my discretion) for using many alternate methods of propulsion
- (Up to my discretion) for EXCESSIVE (also my discretion) gold delay
- (Up to my discretion) for DDAs that, basically, are boring and/ or just generally suck. (See Brickmans post.)




THE END DECISION

A few of the highest rating courses will be judged for overall coolness and fun by a panel of volunteers, (if nobody joins in- just myself) and award a winner and runner up. These will not necessarilly be the two people with the highest points.

DEADLINE

Probably April 15... may be extened or cut short...




Yeah, well go knock yourselves out.

Oh yeah- I almost forgot- the level is in the attatchment...

#59409 18 2005-04-10T09:56:09Z Teedle
Some more rules- (well, they bug me, anyway.)
*spamming floor drones is pointless, as they all merge together before long.
*Gold delay in an action map is usually frowned upon
*Go easy on placing objects after pressing 'z' in debug mode. Really. No one likes crappy drawings made out of gold, with the pieces scattered unartistically and randomly. Rather use 'c' for any drawing purposes.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Hmmmmmm... I might add some stuff in way of DDA creation...

You should always, always place enemies first. These lag up the most, so having them out of the way is always helpfull. Also, keeping a stack of doors, thwumps, one ways and whatnot stored someplace in the rock is DEFINATELY worthwhile... you can go and delete them as you add the same objects into the actual level. This, again, stops lag and random deaths...

There are plenty of different ways to propel N- slopes, launch pads, thwumps, and trap doors (and possibly more.) If you want to use trap doors, press 'c' in debug mode, and place the trap door switches 3/4 of a tile away from the actual door. This will propel N, and fast.

If you want N to survive a collision with a rocket, thwump, drone or floorguard, make him hit a launch pad at the exact FRAME of collision. (To see frames, turn CAPSLOCK off and click to cycle through the frames one by one.) This effect is usually cool.

Other than this, lots of enemies are usually good, and the longer the DDA (provided there are some close calls) the better.

Death DDAs are rarely rated well- if you make them, never use mines, they are totally and utterly random. Making N splatter on a downwards moving thwump looks totally and utterly cool. You can also slide him across normal doors or impale him on them- this, too, looks quite wicked.

Rocket DDAs are quite cool. Try to make sure the passageways the rocket goes through are very tight, to make it look more impressive.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

GLITCHES: I may make a bug map without any code editing, and list the glitches there. I'll link this place one I'm done, but it might be a while- I'm in the middle of making a few maps at the moment.

I really really REALLY don't want to do this again- I had some horrible nightmares lately, BUT- the cincher- I had cheese the night before, and I mean at like 12PM right before going to cheese. (Usually brie, jahrsburg or maybe marinated fetta...) I had no idea it was relevant. But it might be.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

I've had some really disturbing and strange dreams. Some realistic, some surreal. One I had ages ago I remember really well was when my friends and I were on a ship, and it crashed on a tropical island. And then, we all had fun and built huts and then there was a castle nearby! Cool! We raided it and it was so cool, like so many of the adventure books I'd been reading and imaginary games I'd been having (they were awsome... they'd sometimes go as long as a month, fighting through strange and exotic loctaions. This was years ago, though- like, up to grade 4, maybe 5?) And then, we rode out to fight there armies! And it was all cool, and we were nieve, and then.... we died. Slowly. Horribly. We were going to rescue these strange magic crystal things, but instead all of my friends were slowly killed, and I was left alone, and one drowned, and I was run through with a sword, stood up again, was kicked down, and was slowly, ever so slowly stabbed to death...

--------------------------------------------------------

My latest one (cheese related) was really disturbing, because it was both surreal and almost realistic...
A guy walked into my old choir camp dorms- really small, really tight- ang it was modern times, and I was with my school. Anyway, he came and bit a friend of mine. He was then shooed off by the teachers- the man, not my good mate- and, vola, my friends arm got all infected, and it started hurting him- but he was sent back to bed. Later on, he turned- surprise surprise- into a zombie. Not that scary, I suppose, but it was disturbing. And he was in the bunk below me, coming up to get me...
I panicked, and he just stratched me, and didn't get through my skin, and I got away with a friend of mine while the zombie bit everyone, who kept on biting other people. Anyway, about 100 of us escaped. I'll spare you the long details of the flight, and mention a few 'memorable' scenes...
Somebody within us turning into a zombie, right in the midst of our protective bunch, trying to escape.
Losing people one by one.
Being trapped, escaping by smashing glass, and running again.
Getting more and more tired, just not wanting to go on, but not being able to stop.
Schools, kids, running, screaming...
Getting caught in the rush, losing friends, not stopping, 'betraying' people who got bitten- only to run on and leave them to die. Alone. At the fate of the zombies.

The one moving thing, though, was one place, when we- and by now, I mean a huge group of thousands of peopple- were running down a stairway to get to a subway. I'd been with my best mate this entire time- and then a zombie was next to me, and I hate jump over the rail and go down more stairs. I called for him to do the same, but we were caught up in the rush, and I just wanted to get away, and I just acted like a coward and ran- jump down a few metres at a time, down the gap where the handrails were, rushing to the bottom, passing groups of terrified, injured, and frightened people, and a few zombies- and I made it into the actual station doors, which were then bombarded, right before we left- and left my friend, knowing he'd never, ever, ever escape.

On the station, we grouped together- strangers- those of us who had lost friends and lives, often sacrificing others to survive themselves. We were all broken, and haggard, and horrible. Then we were boarding, and we realised someone in our group may have been bitten. And we spotted one girl- maybe 13, maybe 14- beautiful and innocent, cluthing her arm and crying. And we just took her, and sort of handled her out of the train... her weeping, me feeling horrible but knowing thee was no alternative. We then just left her there, the doos slammed, and we moved on. To keep on running at the other station, because the zombie invasion ended up right behind us- we'd barely gotten any headstart... The thing with the girl was the worst of the dream...

And then, just a blur of escapes, running, climbing, and escaping, as one by one we drop off. Finally, a group of people- maybe only 10 altogether- made it to the final barrier. I was the youngest and least equipped of all of them. There were millions of others, but these people were ruthless, and there was one last set of impenatrable doors seperating us from the rest of the world- like, a door leading to absolute safety and a new land, where we could escape. One person came running desperately up to us, gesturing for us to wait, but we just shut him out. And I stood there, the despicable coward who didn't help my friends, and cried. One of the men had a gun. He saw me crying. Then he saw the slight scratch on my arm. It was tinged ever so slightly yellow. He raised an eyebrow, and in slow motion- raised the gun barrel and pulled the trigger.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Shit- did I really just write that much?

But, yeah, the worst bit was- this was when I woke up- then I fell back asleep, and it started again. AGAIN. And I knew it. And it played all over again, with a few differences. Except this time there was no end. At all. Horrible.

When I woke up I didn't know if I was really awake or not, and I just panicked when my mum came into the room, and cowered in my blankets. So, yeah. I guess I'm a coward, really. No deffence- I just lay there, waiting for her to kill me, so it could be over and done with, and I could just give up. It didn't seem worth fighting over.

Anyway, as you can probably tell, she wasn't actually a zombie, so it's all good.

So, yes. This may have been becaus of the cheese. I don't really want to try again. It revealed too many things about my personality I wish I didn't know.

#68309 90 2005-05-21T13:53:45Z Teedle
Righto... bugs....

'There are several bugs in the game of N. Many of these can be used succesfully- if used in the right context.

NANs
First of all, the bugs that are worst, and affect gameplay the most, are NaN'd bugs- these are achieved by pressing, for example, 'l' in the level code textbox. These NANs can tatally stuff up your map data.

Concerning doors
Doors can be used incredibly badly, if done correctly. (Or is that wrongly?) Layering trap doors and openable doors can result in you being able to go through the trap door. Layering normal doors can prevent you from
a) Having to get all of the switches to get through the door, which appears closed
Being able to get through the door- even when it looks open
Normal, 'slidy' doors when placed over opened openable doors prevents N from falling down.
When a floor guard is on a path of normal doors, it will continue on its path even when the doors are opened. This can, on occasion, work well and add to the gameplay.

Concerning thwumps
Thwumps can be made, with difficulty, to go in just one direction, through anything- including tiles- in its way. This can be done easily to the right- simply place a thwump facing left, halfway in a wall. This can sometimes work- for example, in Lucidiums 'pressed for time'... however, the idea stales after a while.
Thwumps can also go through walls, on occasion- for example, when places in a '5' tile and facing downwards. Don't do this. Just don't.

Concerning launch pads
The frame N hits a launch pad, he is invincible. Problem is, this doesn't work when the map is added to the 'user levels' list- so, you should probably steer clear of this effect in the majority of cases.
Launch pads can also bring N back to gameplay after he reaches the exit door of a level. This doesn't work outside of debug mode, so try to steer clear of this too.

Code editing
The most common, and best, example of code editing to help a level is this- super (or minute) powered launch pads. But please- these can get tacky. Use them in moderation.
To change the speed and direction of a launch pad, first find the bit of program that denotes that it is a launch pad.
(For example, 2^372,324,-1,0)
The last two digits are what you want to focus on- changing these changes the speed N gets propelled on the x and the y axis. (as in, up and down.) Just fiddle a bit- you'll get the hang of it.

Hiding things
Try to avoid 'hiding' objects beneath bouncy blocks. This is usually annoying, and rarely works well in a level- with a few exceptions. You can also hide many other things in many other ways- door triggers half- in walls, half out whilst being covered by a one way platform is another example. Or hiding enemies inside walls, and guiding them through a level using normal slidy doors. Or even beneath thwumps. These hiding tricks can rarely be used well- but, then again, rarely is not 'never'.

Concerning one- ways
Downwards facing one way doors can be easily thwarted, so they really aren't the best for puzzle maps.
One way doors facing to a side on a level surface (for example, a row of one ways or in a tunnel) can be incredibly annoying, as they can be hard to pass.
Also, no matter how fast N is flying upwards or sidewards, one way doors can stop him without him dieing.

For demonstration of these bugs, please have a look at the 'bugs, bugs, bugs' series by Formica/ The Daily Llama.

[/B]Meh. I still think that there should be compulsory voting in order to submit maps. You know.... 4 votes and you can submit a map. They can build up into 'credit', if you will. And that way the vast majority- if not pretty much all- of the maps since the credits system takes place would be voted. As for the idea this thread was about? I can't say I really like it- it's just asking for stupid comments. And less votes. And far too few maps are getting rated at the moment anyway.

Personally, I'd like voting disabled, but I won't go so far as to ask for that.

Anyway... here are my views on a number of suggestions for NUMA...

Compulsory voting- vote 4, submit 1 map

PROS
-reduces spam, and threads of hundreds of maps that bounce the newest page into oblivion
-the vast majority (presumably over 80%...) of maps would be voted.
-it's fairness- you want people to rate your maps? You rate other peoples maps!

CONS
-could result in some dumb votes on maps people haven't even played. Of course, MODS _could_ help prevent that...
-Well, more work for our beloved arachnid.

NUMA mods

PROS
-well, I suggested it
-helps against maps like THIS
-would actually be helpful for Arachnid, not always having everybody asking everything on him

CONS
-tension over who gets to be a mod
-possible irresponsible mods

Compusory comments with rating

PROS
-Well, you'd get more comments
-Less downrating, as you'd have to provide a reason.

CONS
-Less rating whatsoever
-Plenty of rubbish comments for the MODS (if they come) to clean up
-Revenge votes at people who rate down maps
-Anarchy and the end of the world...

My PRO and CONS may, I admit, be slightly currupted by my opinions.

#3093 1 2005-05-30T11:55:44Z Teedle
Just curious how this has spread through cyber space....

When did I first get addicted? For me, I was at a concert hall, waiting in the audiance stands for our time, aproximately 4 hours away, to stand up and rehearse for about 4 minutes...

And I didn't bring my laptop, as- well- why should I have? As if we'd get a powerpoint, and I was out of batterries.

And there were a grand total of 2 powerpoints in the wall. My best friend, next to me, got it. And he started fiddling through games... eventually, partly through, he came to N. He played one level for a bit... (01- 0), got sick of it (short attention span) and loaded some other random .dos game. I can't remember what. I had fallen in love with N, and nothing else mattered.

So, anywho, I got it off him a few days later at school, but was busy and didn't play it for ages. Then some stuff happened in my personal life- it was a big thing at the time- bassically, a girl (this was in year 9) that I had liked since I had first seen her at the begginning of year 7- she started going out with a friend of mine. An arrogant friend of mine. Who was hitting on a female friend of mine, and also dating somebody else from a random 3rd party. Which is all very very very pointless information, but still.

I was pretty- no, very (somewhat unreasonably) upset, and felt like ****, and went into my room, booted up my laptop, and tried not to think about anything. So, I found N in my game folders, and played it from straight after school untill about 2 in the morning, while my brain tried to deal with its adolescent teenage boy- related issues. I made probably- (shame) only about 4/7 of the game (with 5 columns) at the time. And I still felt like ****, and N felt repulsive, but I was hooked anyway. And I played it again, in small amounts, often- and then, I deleted it from my computer to help me concentrate in class. But, I couldn't live without it, and loaded it up on my home computer again. And that's where I discovered NED.

So, from that day on, I've been hooked- though I try to play N in moderation. And my love life is just fine right now, thank you very much.

Well, you _could_ easily cut it down a lot.... to the bare 'we're so sick of hearing this!' suggestions.

As in, something like...

***Weapons in N- it won't be implemented, as it would go against the whole style of gameplay. It won't be implemented, and that is that.
***N as a console version- doubtfull, but it is a possibility. However, this is already in the pipeline, so do not suggest this again.
***New tiles- now that N has been developted as far and much as it has, adding new tiles would involve a huge amount of effort, and the whole collision- detection system would go out of whack. It's not a bad idea, but it _won't_ happen.
***New drones and items- go ahead and post your ideas, but there is quite a good chance that it has been suggested before. Search around a bit, first. And if an object in the game could already fullfill that role, don't bother. (e.g. 'spike traps' in the floor: A mine could achieve the same effect.)
***Speed changer- don't suggest this. Really. You'll eventually find out why....
***Multiplayer- if you're thinking about 2 N's running around the screen shooting at eachother,give up now. Really.
***NED from the menu- been discussed several times before, unfortunately it's too hard to implement.
***A level editor- one is allready in the game, please read your help files.
***New time trial mode (gold does not count)- This won't work, as there are many levels where you could just simply run to the left/ right, and win like that.... the highscores would never change.
***Inertia, when on a thwump _it_ pulls you- nope, that'd stuff up the highscores. Sorry!

Anything that would require stuffing up the highscores will NOT be implemented- as in, changes to existing physics and existing objects.

... there... but I missed some, I'm sure. Anything else critical need to be added? Ones that come up all the time, perhaps?

We're... well, not much happens down here. We follow Americas example in many things, which I hate. It's the only reason I'm against us becoming a republic (no offence)- still being commited, even if it is only very, very slightly- to England seems to me as the last thing between now and being completely controlled by America.

I mean, look at it- in WW2, it was 'The mothercountry has gone to war, and thus we must follow'. Now- 'Bush is leading the country to a war nobody approves of, in his country or ours, so lets just go and send people there too.'

Other than this... well, we don't have Deep Fried Marsbars, cereals with marshmellows in them, or any of the other (apparantly) distinctly American forms of fast food. We have, on average, aproximantely- what was it- 124% of our ideal body weight (if that makes sense) which is high, but lower than your (I think) 157%. (On average, this is, of course.) We're all sorta clumped around the shores, have proper cities, but there are a few people in the vast interior. Strangely enough, there's quite a large population in Alice Springs, which is slap bang in the centre of Australia, away from absoultely anywhere else whatsoever... which is slightly odd.

Other than this, well, I live about 1 and a half hours from Phillip Island, which has some great beaches. We're not particularly ignorant about stuff, and we're being led by John Howard, who bassically sucks up to Bush in every way imaginable.

Oh, and we have- for the most part- your music, though there are some Australian bands and artists that pretty much nobody out of the country knows about. For example, Missy Higgins, who has probably the strongest Australian accent out of anybody I know or have heard.

Our accent isn't particularly pronounced, and it's nothing like what I imagine most Americans would assume it to be. The Kagaroo population is under threat from over-culling encouraged by our wonderfull government, and many, many Australians have never seen one- nor a wombat, or a platapus, or... an emu? (I've seen Kangarroos, wallabies, wombats and I THINK a platapus in the wild before...) And platapus's are pretty much endangered.

There aren't many snakes- scrap that, ANY snakes in the city, and we don't seem to have too many other pests- such as, Rats- in huge amounts either. The wilderness is being wrecked by Rabbits introduced by some random English bloke a couple hundred years ago.

And, thanks to Howard, the Old Growth forests of Tasmania (absolutely beautiful) are being recklessly destroyed.

We have plenty of poisonous snakes here, too, but most people I know have never seen one. We once had one in our holiday home in the country, which was... a bit unsettling... Oh yeah, we get snow here too, up in the mountains. Our holiday home in the country is about 3/4 of an hour away from the ski and snowboard resort 'mount bulla'.

Other than this, we're invaded by McDonalds, Hungry Jacks, KFC and other facelesss, evil corporations like the rest of the world. I live next to a nature reserve- the 100 acres. Around here, there's absolutely nothing like the stereotypical image of Australia, though there probably are pockets where you get the Crocodile- dundee type Australians, but it's really, really rare, as far as I know.

#3451 1 2005-06-25T13:56:03Z Teedle
Lately I've worked a bit on my 'single song challange' tileset series. I've done about 10 or so, these are my favourites.

Basically, I've listened to a song- sometimes once, sometimes one- and- a half times, but at absolute maximum twice, then build a tileset in N while listening to it. And I can't have any previous ideas for the tileset- it needs to be influenced almost entirely by the music.

And it can't take longer than the song twice. The design needs to be done on the first hearing, and you just do some minor polishing during the second.

Here are my 5 best so far, forming an 'episode' so far. Go on and join me making these- they only take 3 or 4 minutes, which is the entire idea.

Most of you won't have heard many of these songs, but even for those of you who have, it'll be hard to tell how the tileset was influenced by them- but it WAS, and that was the whole idea. Enjoy!

Hey guys. Just thought I'd say goodbye before I left.

In case any of you are actually going to mind my absence, don't worry, I won't be gone far. I'll still come here, occassionally- just not every single day. I'm aiming for maybe once a week or something like that, but maybe that won't work. Anyway.

Ya know, these forums have been sucking a ton out of me. No- the entire internet, the computer, in fact, has been taking a ton out of my life. I've just been feeling drained lately, fighting about things I don't feel passionate about, and gradually drifting away from everyday life.

It all sounds very melodramatic and whatnot, but really, this isn't a bit reason whatsoever. It's nothing like the grand scope of Kabblizzy and Maximo's leaves- it's just me not feeling like this anymore. Or, more specifically, feeling overall like crap, and realising that this isn't helping.

It's not really bringing me all that much joy, which was sorta what Kabblizzy was saying.

And, not to sound like an echo of our beloved Blizz, but I _shall_ be staying round a bit, seeing the (probably small) fuss this topic may cause, and even after that I'll come here once in a while, to post in small amounts, every now and then. Especially if I need help for, say, an upcoming debate.

I haven't really reached any real hights on this forum, and I may come back to reclaim my ubernerd status eventually, and maybe get someplace. But at the moment, this forum is draining it from me.

I'll stick around tonight, maybe a bit tommorow, rest of this week- then I'll sorta be off, but like Kabblizzy, I'll come back and post a bit. I'll probably post in Atramentis- style amounts, or maybe a bit less.

How about N? Am I done with that? Sadly, yes. 88-4 has totally and utterly defeated me, and I'm tired of trying it again and again and again and getting more and more frustrated. Actually, all of this has been kinda frustrating to me of late- not majorly, but a bit. Having said that, I'll probably download future versions when (if) they come, and leave some positive remarks for M & R. (Speaking of which, you guys rock.)

And NUMA? Well, I'll stick around. But not as much. I'm planning on not going on it more than, perhaps, once a day at first then every coupla days. I'm going to tone my map- making down, but by no means stop together. However, I probably won't be rating and commenting quite as much as before. It's all sorta straining everything a bit.

Well, what else can I say.

Ooo- I know! Electric chickens taste better in the winter!

...

So, to just sorta wrap things up, sorry for those of you I arrogantly argued against, often with totally incorrect convictions. Sorry to Kablizzy- it's a real regret of mine, acting in the hot- tempered way I did. Well done to you, nevermore, may your 'tattletale' remain in the top 10 indefinately. Sorry for being an ass (yay... donkies are cool) about my ratings, and whatnot.

Anyway, twas fun, and I'll still most certainly be around, but nowhere near as much. I've sorta moved on. And this is all shadowing Kabblizzy, which I'm sorry about, because- well- it's just sorta awkward.

And all of this has been affected by this absolutely crazy, helplessly pathetically horrible and disturbing night I had last night- not just dreams, because I only got them when I actually got to sleep at, oh, 5 am or so? So, who knows, I may just get over it.

But, I really want to focus more on 'real life' with 'real people'. Do some really productive stuff- improve, hopefully, my school marks somewhat again, paint, write, compose, and all of that.

I wish all of you forum- dwelling creatures all the best, really. Every last one of you. It's been great. But I'm sorta sick of this. I feel sick, inside, and almost literally- I'm still not entirely over a really bad ilness I had a while ago. And, well, you know- I've been feeling like absolute crap lately. Which doesn't really affect all that much, and isn't a reason, but that's probably why this is all coming out a lot more serious than it really is.

After all, what am I doing, exactly? Not storming out of a forum, just promising to cut down on it. Not leaving, quite, but sorta. It's nothing particularly great, so don't feel like it is.

And I feel sick, and I'm just leaving. The addictive thought of this forum has slowly, somehow, become repulsive to me. But I've always been slightly odd.

Best of luck to all of you, which I'm probably going to continue saying as I drop in to visit this forum for the rest of this year, at least. Ah, good 'ol melodrama.

There a bit less than an hour of sunlight left today, and I'm going to make the most of it. (natural light... erg.) I'm going to take the dogs for a walk, which they really need, then I'm going to come in and practise piano. And drop in here later tonight.

Thank you all, ya've been great. I can't really say much else- in fact, I've said way, way, way too much already.

So, yeah. I've got another map to post, eventually. And I'll keep on making them. And I'm sorry if this is all a bit too serious, and I'm even more sorry for the way it sounds like I'm just storming off.

#3634 1 2005-07-10T14:43:24Z Teedle
Level guide

Part I- Hole (formica)
Part II- Beach (maniac)
Part III- Muv (formica)
Part IV- Strange Trees and Mutant Fleas (sendy)
Part V- And Action! (llcooldave)
Part VI- Put Your Hands Up!(chimmneysweep)
Part VII- Spacecraft (formica)
Part VIII- Part VIII (atramentis) (under revision- may be replaced to fit the epic rules, and flow betwen the levels before and after this. Please state your opinion!)
Part IX- Clouds (great sea)
Part X- Thunderstorm (maniac)
Part XI- We Can Be Happy Underground (sweep)
Part XIV- Hill of Hate (andrelius)

Rules
These are the rules for adding a map to 'The Epic'...
  • Each map must play right- to- left, with the ninja starting on the far right, and the exit being on the far left.
  • Each map MUST contain, on the far right, the two columns that were on the far- left of the previous map. Thus, the series will play like a single, very long level.
  • Every level must bear some resemblance to something real- ish. No pretty patterns, or metanet style levels. Try to incorporate gravitiy in most, if not all, of the level design.
  • All level descriptions must link back to this thread.
  • You are not allowed to create 2 consecutive 'epic' maps.
  • The description must link back to this thread, and you must link to the map in this thread. The description should always involve- usually further- the vague plot of the thing. Nothing gory or too serious.
  • Nothing too insanely hard.
  • If I judge a level 'not worthy' of The Epic, it won't be included in the semi- official list. But this will only apply to levels that broke any of the above rules, or just suck to a Yanu- like degree.
Hey guys- just thought I'd fill you all in on The Epic. You should get the hang of it soon.... join, all willing people! This should end up great. I hope. Please join in.

New rules
(these rules won't affect existing levels, but will affect new ones.)
  • No more 'inside a building' type levels; the idea of The Epic is realistic landscapes, and the enterior of a bulding- type levels never seem to fit that. A cityscape or something might be allright, but no office blocks.
  • You must post your map within 5 days of it becoming your turn. If not, it'll go to the next person.
Please DO TRY to follow the rules- they've been bent and outright broken a lot lately, and, well, that's allright, but they ARE there for a reason. And I'd really appreciate it.

Oh- and maps in This general style are exactly what I'm after...

#3697 1 2005-07-15T15:02:00Z Teedle
Well, here it is. My love life, in (relative) brief, and my current pitiable- sorta- position.

I met a girl in year 7. Yay for love at first sight. She came onto me, sorta. This was in year 7, okay? I was an idiot, and yeah. She..... was- no, is- a devout christian, but the nicest person I've ever met. We spent a week- maybe a bit more- spending every possible moment as close to eachother as possible, just.. talking, and aggreeing, and seeing other views, and enjoying intelligent conversation. I thought it was the best time ever. Oh, she was smart, she was beautifull, and she.. seemed perfect.

Me, being an idiot, via a few secluded incidents, managed to make an ass of myself. As always. Not even that badly, but enough to ruin anything we had going. But, hey, this was year 7, yeah? What do puny year 7's feel? Their crushes are just pathetic flings. This was all near the start of the first term.

A few weeks into our _very_ long winter holidays- the time between years 7 and 8- I asked this girl out, via hotmail, because I was to chicken to do it face to face. I wrote absolute rubbish. Drivel. Hopeless sentimental, melodramatic rubbish. And... I mean, just so trashily rubbishy it wasnt funny. I sounded like the stupidest idiot, out of my depth, laughable in an unpleasent way.

I recieved no reply 'till the end of the holidays, when she wrote back- presumably worried about the awkwardness of the upcoming year- setting the record straight. We were too young, she was too responsible, and... well... I was very, very politely turned down and had it made clear that she had no intentions of going out with me, EVER. Period. And that was that.

Year 8 was spent with smiles, polite nods, and polite greetings. The occasional times we'd work together on some project, and I'd just be head- over- heels with- well, ya know. And I didn't make a fool of myself, once. I had a fight with a guy, too, that year. She was quite clear that she didn't like this, at all. She's a nonviolent, totally inoffensive person. Somehow I loved that.

Later that year, I then- stupidly, and typically- wrote an email to every single one of my close friends, male and female- her included. I apologised for all of the shit I'd done over the years since I started, the rubbish I'd said, stuff I'd brought up, and the longest apology to Jack. Ya know, pour your heart out drunkenly. Yet, despite this blatant stupidity, I somehow managed to get away with some dignity intact, and many people respected the fact that I could admit and apologise for my shortcomings. You know, I felt I'd gone against my morals that year, including the guy I'd punched. (On that note, I think he may have deserved it, but I was so self- rightouse about my actions its not funny.) Anyway, so I tried to straighten myself up. I even wrote a sentance to Her- very precise, punctual, and dignified. Perfectly written, I simply and plainly apologised.

Rest of year 8 passed uneventfully, in regards to my pathetic crushes.

Year 9, I managed to repair my relationships with most people. I believe I'm a much better person than I was in year 7. So, I still thought (yeah, right) I loved her, but didnt act like an idiot, never mentioned it, was polite to everyone, and let the world think I'd moved on. All good. Till the end of term 4.
See, our deb was coming up in a coupla years, but dance rehearsals were beginning the next, so... people started asking eachother. Things were arranged. I didn't ask anyone. I didn't particularly want to go, anyway... At least, not unless it would be with Her.

Enter- oh, we'll call him Jez. Jez is an idiot. Seems good- natured, but he's quite annoying in his way, ignorant and unwilling to accept other opinions, whatsoever. Never, ever, ever is he wrong. And, whenever he didnt have homework completed in the classes we were in together- who gave it to him, after carefully editing it just enough to avoid detection? Me. After a bit I did some quick editing the night before to save time in class. But this was voluntary, and we got along- if only due to lack of anyone better in any of my classes. By the way, I had next- to- no classes with Her in year 8 or 9.

Point of intrest- I introduced Jez to N, who thought it was too simple and deleted it. He eventually downloaded it again, got annoyed cause it was too hard, and deleted it again in a fit of rage. He never tried Ned- it was too complicated.

Then, term 4 of year 9, right before the end, 'Her' asked Jez to the deb. Yes, Jez. Who was fast starting to look like something vile and repulsive to me. I mean, they weren't right for eachoter. Jez didnt read, beat people up- or, provoked people to try to beat HIM up, then beat them up, has been suspended a coupla times, and is everything She isn't- and, probably worse to me, everything I'm not.

But, I smiled politely, for a few days. Then I broke down entirely, and acted as though the world was conspiring against me. I got annoyed at Jez, who handled it quite well. Jez told Her all about my little breakdowns. She was sympathetic, as she said *confidentially* to Jez via an email. I don't usually read other peoples emails, but there was a crowd around his desk, and I realised he was showing it off to 7 or 8 class members, the part where she talked about me included. See, I'd just figured that it was something funny, and went to have a look.

I got sorta annoyed, but managed to keep it to myself. When a similar crowd of guys formed the next day, I didnt go to look. But, via a quick glance, I spotted a lot of flesh. Yeah. Porn. He'd gotten one of his friends to burn himself a porn DVD, less than a week after what would have been the happiest moment in my life, had it happened to me. This... it hurt so excrutiatingly, a pain above all. Like the pain you feel when you staple- gun your tounge to the wall.

Yet, I made ammends to him. He was surprisingly quite understanding, in a sorta 'I'm not gonna spend more than 2 minutes discussing this' sorta way. And, the holidays came. I actually called Her up a few times, with polite discussion about this and that, you know... nothing major, and no mentions of the incident, of course.

Welcome to year 10. Started off allright- no classes with Her at all, which was a shame, but I'll live. Probably easier on me, anyway. By this point, they were dating. Yet, I just smiled and nodded and was quite polite. Then, on valentines day, Jez poured his heart out- to a different girl. He was rejected, so he reluctantly richoched back to the unknowing girl, whom I was still infatuated with. He _then_ tried to date a further 3 girls, being rejected by two. Then, he just dated a lot. I mean heaps. Tons of people. Including, two people on one night. One of which was.... Her. I wanted to tell Her, of course, but managed to abstain. More polite conversation and nodding.

Then, came term 2. There was a debate, and I was waiting for my dad to pick me up late that night. There was, pretty much, me and two other girls from different schools left. I met them, smiled and nodded, and got into a conversation with one. The other had to leave sooner than us. We... got along. Really, really well. We exchanged phone numbers, and I went to bed really really happy for once. I didn't think about Her twice- now, I was thinking about- oh, lets call her M.

So, M and I went to the movies. It was great. We decided to meet again. No contact, for several long, long days. She was out of credit, and we decided to meet again on a weekend. Last minute, she puller out. Her agent had called, and she was rushed off to audition for a part in the city- just days after being shot in Blue Heelers as a girl who gets murdered.

We arranged to meet AGAIN- and, then she stopped replying. Again. The day we'd aranged passed, and we didnt meet up. Then, she 'found her phone' and we were back. We went out- I think. I didn't do too badly, it was nice. Very, very nice. A day to be remembered. We decided to that again in a few days time, but she ended up having to rush off when one of her relatives landed in hospital, and she was sent to babysit her many, many younger siblings. (she's in a family of 12- 10 kids.)

We made more arrangements, and then my mum decided that our family would go skiing for a coupla days- 4, I think it was. I haven't heard from her for over a week now, and not from lack of trying. I'm so sick of her answering machine.

The thing about M is, just how much she ISNT the stereotypical dream girl. Not that Her was, but... M doesn't have that typical 'actress' face, nor that dreamlike lilting, gentle female tone, nor that tall, elegantness, nor that innocent- like look. Her family is badly off, she buys most of her stuff from op shops, and is entirely independant. And she is perfect in every way. And now I can't reach her, though my phone may be at fault- my headset keeps on acting like my phone is recieving a message, but nothing every turns up.

Now, here comes perhaps the only interesting part- this is all present day, allright? Right before M and I met for the last- or, latest- (very brief) time, I got a text message from Her (the first one) saying "call me- I need to talk to you about something." It was Her, on christian youth camp. She'd somehow found out that Jez was a total jerk, and said so. It sounded strange, coming from her. And, she really didnt want to go to the deb with him. There are still quite a few guys without partners, including a very good mutual friend of ours (a great, nice guy, and about her hight, too) - but she asked me.

I accpeted, of course. I mean, I couldnt go with M anyway, and people were bugging me to find a partner- Including the aforementioned mutual friend.

And, it's not like we're dating. BUT- her and Jez dating was bassically when they went to the deb together. That signified the fact that they were 'together', and from that point on Jez and Her could always be found talking, or flirting, or doing stuff that made me want to puke, rather than smile politely. Not that they kissed, to the best of my knowledge. But what does that mean?

But am- or was, for all I know- I dating M? I mean, I like her- a lot- but- well- we haven't kissed. Or hugged. Or held hands. Or done anything other than talked, and I know I've given her long sidelong glances in the movie theatre at about the time that Anaking was betraying the Jedi order...

So, yeah, that's it. I'm just hoping that having given all this information, all will become clear to me somehow. Not that I actually expect it to achieve anything- at all- but, well, I supppose you guys can always poke fun at me. This is in Bash 'n trash, after all. This took a long time to write, and it's achieved fuck all, but who knows...

See, there's not even a (real) problem for me to ask advice from, but there it is, a whole lot of words.

Appearance 4/5 points

Ease of use (if really cool tricks are easier to do it's a huge bonus) 7/10 points
Very inexperianced people may have difficulty jumping off the single tile things. Getting up to the second level is easy, which is good. Getting down the tiny middle column is very hard to do without breaking your flow or dieing.

Originality (pretty self explanatory) 10/15 points

I like pie.

The Alternative Love Poem

This is, basically, an English assignment from a while ago. I earnt myself a tidy A+, and thought you might want to take a look at this poem. Enjoy!




Her eyes were the deepest shade of toilet water blue

And her hugs were as warm as freshly spewed spew.

Her hair was as dark as the lid of my pen-

She truly was beautiful- and her name was Sphen.



My heart torn out, my love thrown away,

And shoved onto a metaphorical dump truck on Valentines Day.
It hurt so excruciatingly, a pain above all,

Like the pain you feel when you accidentally staple gun your tongue to the wall.



My love for you is forever a red, red rose,

That in a most desolate garden grows.

Flowering softly, where the air is still,

Grows my love- which looks vaguely like a daffodil. *



I dont even think you know my name,

Day after day, its all the same.

Looking on sadly as you give your love away,

Day after day, day after day.



Each day feels as sad as the last-

And yet, whenever you walk past,

My heart stops



And now Im dead.



*(Authors note: My love is also needs to be watered frequently with water, otherwise known as di-hydrogen oxide, and can be used by florists in flower arranging.)

Speed park (maximo) (not maniac) (sorry for confusion caused)
Appearance: 2

Load time: 5
Less than one bar- I cant ask for more than that.

Ease of use: 3
See, I thought that it was quite easy, myself. Yet a friend at school (Who is by no means anything REMOTELY like bad at N) had great difficulty doing- well- anything. And, since hes peering over my shoulder right now, well here ya are. Now go get lost, allright?

Fun Factor: 14
Very fun, in places. However, I found the transition BETWEEN these places a bit of a bother sometimes it could be hard to break out of cycles, but maybe thats just me. And I HATED some of the little sections and touches. (eg that little tunnel on the far left.)

Quality + Quantity of stuff N can do: 16
Okay, now then well, there was a lot of Quantity, but only a few jumps that I found very, very fun. And, well, some of it (most notably the far left section) felt as though it was just stuck in there to fill up room. (Also the central column on the right hand side, though less so. IMO.)

Ninja rating: 3
Well, yeah.

Originality: 6
Well, no astounding new ideas thatll take the world by storm, in fact, pretty much nothing new at all. Really.

Overall thoughts on the map: 4

#86314 143 2005-07-27T07:44:34Z Teedle
Atramentis: Drone park

Appearance: 3
Not my style. The drone prison type square thingos were especially ugly... though necessary for the 'challanges'. And, just, frankly I didn't like it. No offence.

Load time: 5
Less than one bar- So, well, what else can I give you?

Ease of use: 7
All in all, quite an easyish park. Breaking out of pattern can be ever- so- slightly difficult, and some of your challanges were- well- challanging. Hence their name. Still, some of the more cool stuff can be quite difficult.

Fun Factor: 19
Flow- I love it! And there's so much of it! And there's a ton of variety, if you look hard enough for it. I also really like some challange, and this has a few quite hard challanges included. Some. Ummm- oh man I loved that so, so very very much. Thank you. This is frank and total honesty- that was really fun. I enjoyed this one more than any of the others, by a considerable amount. I'm very tempted to give you a perfect score, but... it could always have been that little bit better, I suppose.

Quality + Quantity of stuff N can do: 25
At first it really doesn't look like much, and if you hadn't listed the 9 challanges this would have scored considerably lower. But the quality is all good, a list of challanges it a *great* idea I don't believe anybody else has come up with yet, (to the best of my knowledge- sorry if somebody already has, I'll be sure to aknowledge you too) and the challanges are all very, very nice. And good quality. And then just running around is great too, but that goes more under 'fun'. But, well, when push comes to shove this map didn't feel like it had all that much, at least compared to a few others I can think of. But the challanges rectify that entirely IMO, and there's a whole ton, and so I give you the very respectable score of 25

Ninja rating: 4
Well, _technically_ a 4.5, but nevermind that. Probably closer to a 4 than to a 5.

Originality: 9
I'm feeling a bit reluctant about this, as somebody may have done either of the ideas that I loved so much before, BUT:
*The idea of 'challanges' and areas was great, and added a purpose I've always felt the want for in the skatepark challanges. I know that that's not what the N park is all about, but, after all, they're not compulsory and I really felt they added another (even if slightly unnescesary) dimension to the whole thing.
*The walljumping was done effectively, and- well- was very fun. I know that walljumping between two walls isn't exactly original, per se, but it sure was done well, and I haven't seen it done in any other playpark levels.
I just hope somebody else hasn't already done the challanges idea...

Overall thoughts on the map: 9
I loved this, and that's all there is to it. I really loved playing this, and I think you deserve a bonus here. A big one.

#94608 198 2005-08-27T12:29:04Z Teedle
The N-tertainer (Mark_II)

Appearance - 2 points
Just not my style... I'm afraid I don't really like it.

Loading time/lag (the less there is, the higher the points) - 4 points
Quite nice, no real complaints here, but not as good as totally tileset based playparks.

Ease of use (if really cool tricks are easier to do it's a huge bonus) - 8 points
It's nice and simple to do the vast majority of the stuff, which is nice. There is nothing (overly) complicated here, at all.

Fun factor (how fun is it to play?) - 11 points
Now this one was a hard one to rate. See, parts of it I loved. And parts of it could only really be accessed (or broken out of) by breaking your flow, at least a little bit. And parts I didn't really like. My main complaint, though, is that at times it feels... sort of... one directional? Where, if you do something the author didn't intend, you break your flow a lot to get back properly.
Also, what was with the one ways in the wall?
I preferred the left half to the right, by quite a bit.

Quality & Quantity of cool stuff N can do on the map - 21 points
There is a lot to do, I can't deny that. There really is a ton, and a ton of variety. And it's not linked particularly badly. There's nice variety, even if it isn't quite open- ended nor quite flowly enough for my tastes. Nevertheless, it's very nice, so I'll give this a 21 for the huge range of things to do.

Ninja rating (how would I rate this map on NUMA if I didn't know it was linked to this competition?) - 3 points

Originality (pretty self explanatory) - 9 points
Well, what can I say? I can't really see anything not used elsewhere, except perhaps the one ways in the wall, which annoy me a lot. The two sectors are sorta nice, and the transition LOOKS like a good, original idea (even if I feel it could maybe have been done better.) So, well, yeah... a nice, but not exceptional rating here.

Overall thoughts on map - 3 points
I'm sorry for doing this, but there's nothing in this map that makes me go WOW! I JUST LOVE THAT! It was nice, I admit it, but there was nothing exceptional I thought really deserved the extra marks. It was just a nice, well... nice playpark. And what's wrong with that?

TOTAL - 61 points.
#94610 199 2005-08-27T12:54:33Z Teedle
If you tolerate this, then your children will be next. (Sweep.)

Rated with various (good natured) sweeps at Sweeps judging... but judged honestly by me.

Appearance - 2 points
Yipes. It hits my eyes in the same way green chickens do- ergh, that doesn't look right. Don't ask me why, though...

Loading time/lag (the less there is, the higher the points) - 4 points
Very nice, though it could it could, sorta, be a bit better; like some tacos with sour cream, guacamole and cheese, but no salsa.

Ease of use (if really cool tricks are easier to do it's a huge bonus) - 2 points
Okay, it looks simple, and at times even feels slightly so; but, like a pirate wielding a grenade, it is quite complicated, deep down. And, like a pirate wielding a grenade, this means that you will spend quite some time exploding.

Fun factor (how fun is it to play?) - 12 points
It's like a roller coaster painted pink with purple polka dots; it may be very fun, but there are some things that bug you so much you can't ignore them and get your mind entirey on the roller coaster; rather, you spend time moaning about the colour scheme.
For example, the top section: You can re-enter that once and it'll be fine, no problem. But, after that once, you're still perfectly capable of re-entering it, but going there gets you totally stuffed. A trap door or something like that, placed cleverly (maybe with gold?) would've been nice, and increased the playability if you could go somewhere new after doing it. Plus, the way one keeps on exploding, inconsistantly, at many various points... well, that bugs me.

Quality & Quantity of cool stuff N can do on the map - 15 points
High quality, I won't deny it. (At least, while it works.) But, like almost- empty toilet paper rolls, you end up wanting more long after you've used up what's available; which occurs far too quickly.

Ninja rating (how would I rate this map on NUMA if I didn't know it was linked to this competition?) - 3.5, rounded to 4 points

Originality (pretty self explanatory) - 12 points
It's like hamburger earmuffs; we have hamburgers, we have earmuffs, but we don't have them put together.
Actually, scrap that. The stuff used in here isn't really all that original (though I don't know how often they're used in this comp), but it's been used, for the most part, very well. And they're not techniques used in all of the playparks, so, have a nice juicy 12.

Overall thoughts on map - 6 points
This map is like Maddy. You really, really like her- more than you can say. And, when you're with her, nothing is better. But when you're away- or when you much up- things suck more than you can say. The periods inbetween those few golden moments are so far apart, it's horrible. And so long is spent listening to her answering machine, so many hours spent idly texting and knowing you'll get no response, so many e-mails, ignored... there are moments of bliss, but they're few and far apart.
Yet, when you're with her, there is no way things could be better.

TOTAL - 57 points.
It's like a 2 digit number, this total, in that it has 2 digits.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Rocket Park- Snuggletummy

Appearance
Not bad at all - 3 points

Loading time/lag
Very little - 4 points

Ease of use
Yes, it's very easy. There's no real joy in playing it cautiosly, but it's still- technically- very easy to survive, run around, and bounce - 9 points

Fun factor
I'm surprised- I like this. A lot. It sort of grew on me, but I really enjoyed dodging that rocket. Well, rocketS, technically - 15 points

Quality & Quantity of cool stuff N can do on the map
Let's face it. There's not a ton to do here- run around, and dodge a rocket. You'd think you'd get sick of it pretty quickly, but I didn't- but the fact remains, well, there's not a ton. Though the openess of the map was nice - 12 points

Ninja rating
Cheese is good - 3 points

Originality (pretty self explanatory)
It had enemies, to good effect. Forget what I said above, in this map, it worked. Running (or jumping) around dodging rockets is very fun. I know that the maps weren't supposed to use enemies, but this one did, to good effect. Also, it's simplicity was something that seemed to have escaped the other maps alltogether - 8 points

Overall thoughts on map
I actually liked this a lot more than expected. It was fun to mess around in, and lasted a lot longer than the others, when I went to judge it - 7 points

TOTAL - 61 points.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Kuru- Bars

Appearance- 3
It looks sorta pristine, and the mixture of angular angles and the curvy curves suggests something that could have looked nice...

Load Time- 5
No complaint, whatsoever

Ease of Use- 8
No complaints here, either.

Fun Factor- 4

Quanitity- 8
It's not that horrible an amount of stuff, but lots of it doesn't really... do much. Much fun, anyway.

Ninja Rating- 1
I'm sorry....

Originality- 6

Overal thoughts on the map- 2
Well, for starters, what was with those floor guards? And there wasn't any flow, any real... rewarding experiance... just not my thing. At all.

Full Epic Images

Parts I-XX: Left to right (Classic sidescroller style)
I'd reccommend that everybody has a look at these images to see what works when you make a level, for keeping the continuity... There are sections that really merge togtether, and bits that don't. Look, admire, and make a mental note to make sure that yours fits in well in the big image.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Rules
These are the rules for adding a map to 'The Epic'...

* Each map must play right- to- left, with the ninja starting on the far right, and the exit being on the far left.
* Each map MUST contain, on the far right, the two columns that were on the far- left of the previous map. Thus, the series will play like a single, very long level.
* Every level must bear some resemblance to something real- ish. No pretty patterns, or metanet style levels. Try to incorporate gravitiy in most, if not all, of the level design.
* All level descriptions must link back to this thread and you must link to the map in this thread. The description should always involve- usually further- the vague plot of the thing. Nothing gory or too serious.
* You are not allowed to create 2 consecutive 'epic' maps.
* Nothing too insanely hard.
* No more 'inside a building' type levels; the idea of The Epic is realistic landscapes, and the enterior of a bulding- type levels never seem to fit that. A cityscape or something might be allright, or the odd small shack, but no office blocks. And no buidlings that take up the majority of a map.
* You must post your map within 5 days of it becoming your turn. If not, it'll go to the next person.
* If I judge a level 'not worthy' of The Epic, it won't be included in the semi- official list. There will be no arguing with me- if I think it sucks, it won't be in The Epic. Breaking the rules slightly may, on occasion, be acceptable to me. But ask first, because if I don't like it, then I'm afraid you won't be in this.
* No making obscure, mixed references involving fat female hamsters. They can be taken the wrong way.

The Queing System
It's pretty much first come, first served. Stick your name down, and wait your turn. I will PM you if you don't realise you're up. You have a week to make your map... if you don't complete it by then, your turn goes to the next person in the que. You can re- enter the que as many times as you like.
VIP's are people who've been waiting a long time, somehow skipped, ignored, or not iinformed that it's their turn- and have the right to re-enter at pretty much the top of the que if they ever return to this thread.

The Maintinance Team
  • The Daily Llama: Creator of this thread, my decision is final and overides everybody elses.
  • Sweep: Filled in while I was gone. His opinions, advice, and requests in this thread must also always be respected and followed, unless contradicted by myself.
  • Aju (Formerly Wheel-_-134!!): The guy says he has a lot of free time, which is somewhat scarce to me. Listen to what the man says; he'll hopefully be there when I can't be.
Help is always appreciated. Just apply if you'd like to do some extra work. (Yay! Work that is extra!)
Anyway, well, listen to what Sweep has to say. I respect him a lot, and he has a great grasp of this. Everything he says is valid and should be listened to. Ta.

The Polishing Team
  • The Daily Llama
  • Sweep
  • _sketch
  • BSBen
Please, feel free to sign up for this *new* team. Chances are, you'll be selected. Basically, once the epic is finished, the maps will be edited very slightly so that they run into eachother better, and form a more full, complete map. We might try to tweak the difficulty very slightly- just tone down the ridiculously hard maps a little bit, too. The storyline will also be edited, so that it actually leads somewhere and builds up to something bigger than just 'and then N went into a building, and stuff happened'.

We may even eventually work on building a website for this to be hosted on. Maybe.

Other than this,
Yeah. Sorry about the whole rules thingo, and that it sounds complex, but anyway. It shouldn't be too hard to get the hang of, again. I hope you guys like this, and that it works out better than last time. Feel free to go through the other Epic thread if you want a feel of what I want this to end up like, and where I felt it went wrong. Thanks a lot.

Oh- and maps in this general style are exactly what I'm after...

Andrelius- Break a Leg

Appearance - 4 points
No complaints here

Loading time/lag (the less there is, the higher the points) - 4 points
I'm still reserving the 5's for absolutely tileset based maps...

Ease of use (if really cool tricks are easier to do it's a huge bonus) - 2 points
It took me quite some time to find out what would / wouldn't kill me. Plenty of the launch pads, when jumped into, would splatter you against one of the walls.... and there was one bounce block that landing on, from the RHS, would kill you.
Basically, it wasn't really easy... at all. Though, it was a good idea to add edited launch pads to make things easier.

Fun factor (how fun is it to play?) - 8 points
I did get some pleasure out of the nice, big curves... but, overall, this map wasn't my thing. It felt, at times, very awkward... Such as when you would land, running, on a slope going against you, or when the curves don't quite match... also, I had plenty of difficulty not dieing on this map, which is always a downer. Though, it may just be me.

Quality & Quantity of cool stuff N can do on the map - 12 points
What can I say? There wasn't a whole lot to do on this map, IMO. There were only 5 main jumps, and opportunities to mess around with launchpads and bouncy blocks.

Ninja rating - 2.5, rounded to 3 points


Originality (pretty self explanatory) - 7 points
Well... yeah.

Overall thoughts on map - 6 points
It was a nice idea, adding in the launch pads to 'help' people, and it gave the map a nice touch. But, they would also often be lethal, as would the occasional bounce block. Sorry about this.
I think I might also take this opportunity to mention that I somehow feel this map deserves to get a score in the 50's by me... but still, I guess the total is less than the sum of its parts.

TOTAL - 46 points.

Originality (pretty self explanatory) - 13 points

Overall thoughts on map - 8 points
I liked it, but not as much as I like- say- ducks.

Besides, call it genetics, but who knows that there's not something within our genes that determine- at least partly- what our values and talents will be. My grandpa died when I was about three, and I never really knew him. Here I am, and I value the environmnt- same as him. I keep scrapbooks- same as him. I do photography as a hobby, I like to write, I like to read, I even have a very similar taste in authors, at times. (Tolstoy and George Orwell. Oh- and Tolkein, I belive.) I never met this man, I didn't know all this untill my mother told me. I just mean, who's to say it's not proof?

(Incidently, I watched a vagually interesting documentery on a serial killer, who didn't see anything "wrong" with what he was doing... what happened to his moral code?)

Anyway... "proof" of evolution? Here's some of the best I can give, at the moment. Excuse the length.

Quote: ian johnston
The first step in demonstrating the truth of evolution is to make the claim that all living creatures must have a living parent. This point has been overwhelmingly established in the past century and a half, ever since the French scientist Louis Pasteur demonstrated how fermentation took place and thus laid to rest centuries of stories about beetles arising spontaneously out of dung or gut worms being miraculously produced from non-living material. There is absolutely no evidence for this ancient belief. Living creatures must come from other living creatures. It does no damage to this point to claim that life must have had some origin way back in time, perhaps in a chemical reaction of inorganic materials (in some primordial soup) or in some invasion from outer space. That may well be true. But what is clear is that any such origin for living things or living material must result in a very simple organism. There is no evidence whatsoever that inorganic chemical processes can produce complex, multi-cellular living creatures (the recent experiments cloning sheep, of course, are based on living tissue from other sheep).

The second important point in the case for evolution is that some living creatures are very different from some others. This, I take it, is self-evident. Let me cite a common example: many animals have what we call an internal skeletal structure featuring a backbone and skull. We call these animals vertebrates. Most animals do not have these features (we call them invertebrates). The distinction between vertebrates and invertebrates is something no one who cares to look at samples of both can reasonably deny, and, so far as I am aware, no one hostile to evolution has ever denied a fact so apparent to anyone who observes the world for a few moments.

The final point in the case for evolution is this: simple animals and plants existed on earth long before more complex ones (invertebrate animals, for example, were around for a very long time before there were any vertebrates). Here again, the evidence from fossils is overwhelming. In the deepest rock layers, there are no signs of life. The first fossil remains are of very simple living things. As the strata get more recent, the variety and complexity of life increase (although not at a uniform rate).   And no human fossils have ever been found except in the most superficial layers of the earth (e.g., battlefields, graveyards, flood deposits, and so on).  In all the countless geological excavations and inspections (for example, of the Grand Canyon), no one has ever come up with a genuine fossil remnant which goes against this general principle (and it would only take one genuine find to overturn this principle).

If we put these three points together, the rational case for evolution is air tight. If all living creatures must have a living parent, if living creatures are different, and if simpler forms were around before the more complex forms, then the more complex forms must have come from the simpler forms (e.g., vertebrates from invertebrates). There is simply no other way of dealing reasonably with the evidence we have. Of course, one might deny (as some do) that the layers of the earth represent a succession of very lengthy epochs and claim, for example, that the Grand Canyon was created in a matter of days, but this surely violates scientific observation and all known scientific processes as much as does the claim that, say, vertebrates just, well, appeared one day out of a spontaneous combination of chemicals.

And then, how do these new species form?
Geographical isolation- two segments get cut off.
Natural selection- to adapt to their environment, the weaker and less well adapted die and reproduce less than the others. Say, one group might get gradually smaller to hide in rocky gaps, and the other might delelop longer beacks to dig up insects. By develop, I mean that the longer beaked birds are ALWAYS more likely to get insects, so more ALWAYS survive. Thus, there beaks get gradually longer and the other birds gradually smaller. This would just be one adaption. And then there's random mutations (which are proven to exist, in humans too) to deal with, as well- if one actually ends up benefical, chances are that animal will reproduce, the reproduced animals will also reproduce with the beneficial mutation, untill eventually they all have the mutation. Make sense?
Eventually, they'll end up different species due to their adaptions.

"With all the foreign newspapers and multi-cultural sites, the Internet is making it almost impossible for the average American to remain uninformed and apathetic," said Samantha Lessborn of Washington State University, which conducted the survey. "Americans can still do it. But it now takes effort, whereas before it was as easy as turning off Tom Brokaw whenever he said 'In South Korea today...'"

According to survey participant Danny Grisham, a 22-year-old from Cheyenne, Wyoming, it's not just the plethora of international news on the Web that is irritating. "Look, I can get around the news. I just turn off Reuters headlines in MyYahoo," he said. "But even some of the search sites like Yahoo and Alta Vista are available in different languages. Like everybody in the world doesn't speak English. Yeah, right."

"I can see where it's important if we're, like, beating some country in the Olympics or bombing them or, ideally, both," Grisham added. "But if some Colombian drug lord sinks a ferry full of Israeli soldiers in North Latvoania or Serbo-Malaysia, or wherever, and Americans aren't involved, what has that got to do with me?"

Other respondents said they were appalled, not just by the availability of non-U.S. news, but by the way important U.S. news is reported by some of these foreign sites. "Yesterday, for instance, the St. Louis Rams beat the Atlanta Falcons, OK, and I go to the London Times site and it's not even there," said Chip Pernadge of Kansas City, Mo. "Jesus, no wonder those guys lost the war and had to give Hong Kong back to Canada."

Sensing a market opportunity, Net Nanny, makers of Net Nanny filtering software, announced this week it will introduce NetNarrow, an English-only product that automatically filters out content that appears to be international. Specifically, the software looks for world datelines and keywords indicative of irrelevant foreign stories, including "Shiite," "post-Apartheid," and "Bob Geldof."

Survey-taker Craig Barker of Brooklyn, New York, said he will be among the first to get NetNarrow. "On the Web, there are so many ways to get news from so many different places, I could really get some fresh insights into what's going on in other countries if I wanted to," he said.. "But I don't want to."

"You'd think these Internet people would know that," Barker added. "I mean, that's why the Internet is called America Online, right? It's supposed to be about America."

#104631 10 2005-09-30T08:16:53Z Teedle
As much as I agree with Blue, I also have something else to add to Attilas list... something that relates to America. (Yes, though, I am an Australian.)

A subtle sexual bias does exist in the English language, which is obvious in sayings like "a mans home is his castle", "mankind", "forefathers", "manhole" ect. for a long time. Maggio, for instance, wishes to change these around, to get rid of sexist and racist connotations with words. For example, swapping 'manhole' to the less objectable 'sewerhole', getting rid of remarks like 'left- handed compliment' as it's discrimination against people who are physically left handed, and not to use the word 'black' at all- such as in 'black eye', 'black humour', 'blacksmith' or anything like that. I can't talk for black people, but I don't think I'd have difficulty sleeping at night in the knowledge that one who shoes horses is called a "BLACksmith".
Anyway, to my point:
Whilst Maggio is outlawing expressions like "a mans home is his castle" (and, well, fair enough, I guess) but defends expressions like 'a womans work is enver done', because, well, apparantly women always have more work to do. Now, I think that that is pure, utter rubbish. Just because a senitmentis true doesn't make it non- sexist. (Anyway, it isn't true. It just isn't.)

So, yeah. There's just some random info.

(Ah- and when I refer to Maggio, I refer to this book:
Maggio, Rosalie, The Nonsexist Word Finder: A Dictionary of Gender-Free Usage, Beacon Press, Boston, 1988. )

Quote: blue_tetris, Oct 4 2005, 02:39 PM
This is, of course, using the term evolution in a less scientific sense. In the scientific sense, humans will not evolve. The species homo sapiens sapiens is unlikely to undergo any changes that would change its properties enough to warrant the deliniation of a new species. The enviroments that humans live in are unlikely to change in such a way as to warrant evolutionary mutations. Like many other species, humans have simply stopped evolving. If you don't see why, do some reseach into what causes mutations and prepare to learn.

You know, I agree with you entirely on this one, but I do feel like pointing out one thingo I learnt in year 10 science... oh so long ago.

See, basically, we were given some random sheet, that read pretty much like this:
"Humans have stopped evolving.

Blah blah rhubarb blah.

Furthermore, new evidence shows that evolution _may have_ occured in relatively short spurts, amidst very long periods of little or no change. Look at the graph in front of you. Now, look into the watch... look deep into the watch... see how it swings... you are getting sleepy... very sleepy..."

And the graph showed a couple of things, including:
a) A little sidenote saying about how often the random bursts of evolution occurred, and the amount of 'waiting' time inbetween for several different species, which was some huge, amazingly big number.
Showing how long ago Humans evolved from whatsitcalled into... well... humans. (Homo Sapiens.) Now, and I'm sorry I chucked this sheet out so long ago, the number of years ago that humans evolved into humans was a very small fraction of the number of years most of the species on that little sheet had stayed dormant between evolutionary 'bursts'.

So, basically, there's no solid evidence that we stopped evolving. I mean, I'm quite sure we have, and every single argument _for_ why we have stopped evolving in the physical sense makes absolute, perfect, almost inarguable sense... but still, I believe that the fact we think we're above evolution is probably partly intellectual snobbery.

If it's just something tacked on with the rest of everything, something you believe in because you "know" it's true, will it be anything special, at all? Will it help anybody or anythingthing, anywhere? If it's just like the theory of Gravity, something we just believe and get on with, what will become of it?

I can't really articulate my thoughts on this to my satisfaction, but hopefully you get my point.

No, _sketch's map won't count. Sorry, Sketch. It's up to you to replace it, I guess, sweep. The order can be found in my (constantly updated) first post, but I'll just copy and paste the whole thing over here, for you lazy people ...

----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Well, the previouse epic flopped, big time. I'm ressurecting the idea, but with stricter (and more enforced) rules to try to avoid how the previous epic ended up.

Level guide

Part I- Hole (formica)
Part II- Like a bridge over muderous chainguns (sweep)
Part III- Nobody likes a weenie (nevermore)
Part IV- Don't mess with Thor (ngaged)
Part V- Too hot to Handle (Mark)
Part VI- Floating Islands (formica)
Part VII- Cloudy with a 90% chance of death (Dadaluma)
Part VIII- The Basaltic Plateau (maniac)
Part X- The Big Mess Underfoot (sendy)
Part XI- Hand of God (sweep)
Part XII- Ghostly Reminiscentse (starcrossed)
Part XIII- The Giant Pear (barabajagal)
Part XV- Civilisation (formica)

Rules
These are the rules for adding a map to 'The Epic'...

* Each map must play right- to- left, with the ninja starting on the far right, and the exit being on the far left.
* Each map MUST contain, on the far right, the two columns that were on the far- left of the previous map. Thus, the series will play like a single, very long level.
* Every level must bear some resemblance to something real- ish. No pretty patterns, or metanet style levels. Try to incorporate gravitiy in most, if not all, of the level design.
* All level descriptions must link back to this thread and you must link to the map in this thread. The description should always involve- usually further- the vague plot of the thing. Nothing gory or too serious.
* You are not allowed to create 2 consecutive 'epic' maps.
* Nothing too insanely hard.
* No more 'inside a building' type levels; the idea of The Epic is realistic landscapes, and the enterior of a bulding- type levels never seem to fit that. A cityscape or something might be allright, or the odd small shack, but no office blocks. And no buidlings that take up the majority of a map.
* You must post your map within 5 days of it becoming your turn. If not, it'll go to the next person.
* If I judge a level 'not worthy' of The Epic, it won't be included in the semi- official list. There will be no arguing with me- if I think it sucks, it won't be in The Epic. Breaking the rules slightly may, on occasion, be acceptable to me. But ask first, because if I don't like it, then I'm afraid you won't be in this.
* No making obscure, mixed references involving fat female hamsters. They can be taken the wrong way.

The Queing System
It's pretty much first come, first served. Stick your name down, and wait your turn. I will PM you if you don't realise you're up. You have a week to make your map... if you don't complete it by then, your turn goes to the next person in the que. You can re- enter the que as many times as you like.

The Maintinance Team

* The Daily Llama: Creator of this thread, his decision is final
* Sweep: Filled in while I was gone. His opinions, advice, and requests in this thread must also always be respected and followed, unless contradicted by myself.


Help is always appreciated. Just apply if you'd like to do some extra work. (Yay! Work that is extra!)
Anyway, well, listen to what Sweep has to say. I respect him a lot, and he has a great grasp of this. Everything he says is valid and should be listened to. Ta.

Other than this,
Yeah. Sorry about the whole rules thingo, and that it sounds complex, but anyway. It shouldn't be too hard to get the hang of, again. I hope you guys like this, and that it works out better than last time. Feel free to go through the other Epic thread if you want a feel of what I want this to end up like, and where I felt it went wrong. Thanks a lot.

Oh- and maps in this general style are exactly what I'm after...
