And here's an updated-zorred first post...

--------------------------------------------------------

Well, the previouse epic flopped, big time. I'm ressurecting the idea, but with stricter (and more enforced) rules to try to avoid how the previous epic ended up.

Level guide

Part I- Hole (formica)
Part II- Like a bridge over muderous chainguns (sweep)
Part III- Nobody likes a weenie (nevermore)
Part IV- Don't mess with Thor (ngaged)
Part V- Too hot to Handle (Mark)
Part VI- Floating Islands (formica)
Part VII- Cloudy with a 90% chance of death (Dadaluma)
Part VIII- The Basaltic Plateau (maniac)
Part IX: The Crispy Cliffs Of Iqtaqtaluq (Blue Tetris)
Part X- The Big Mess Underfoot (sendy)
Part XI- Hand of God (sweep)
Part XII- Ghostly Reminiscentse (starcrossed)
Part XIII- The Giant Pear (barabajagal)
Part XIV- Raptured Landscape (pitch)
Part XV- Civilisation (formica)
Part XVI: Deadwood (sweep)
Part XVII: Darn Tall Trees (aju)
Part XVIII- Encased Island (Templex)
Part XIX: Science Lesson (bigblargh)
The Epic- Part XX- Eagle Point (Mark_II)

Total Epic Images
This section is, basically, for those of you who want to look at big, extended panorma type images of the entire epic.
I'll update the thumbnails every 10 maps or so- only at major landmarks- but here are one or two of the images... (Click the link to view the images- I can't stick them on these forums for fear of butchering the layout of this page of this thread...)
Parts I- XX: Right to left. (As played)
The Epic- Part I-XX: Left to right (Classic sidescroller style)
I'd reccommend that everybody has a look at these images to see what works when you make a level, for keeping the continuity... There are sections that really merge togtether, and bits that don't. Look, admire, and make a mental note to make sure that yours fits in well in the big image.


----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Rules
These are the rules for adding a map to 'The Epic'...

* Each map must play right- to- left, with the ninja starting on the far right, and the exit being on the far left.
* Each map MUST contain, on the far right, the two columns that were on the far- left of the previous map. Thus, the series will play like a single, very long level.
* Every level must bear some resemblance to something real- ish. No pretty patterns, or metanet style levels. Try to incorporate gravitiy in most, if not all, of the level design.
* All level descriptions must link back to this thread and you must link to the map in this thread. The description should always involve- usually further- the vague plot of the thing. Nothing gory or too serious.
* You are not allowed to create 2 consecutive 'epic' maps.
* Nothing too insanely hard.
* No more 'inside a building' type levels; the idea of The Epic is realistic landscapes, and the enterior of a bulding- type levels never seem to fit that. A cityscape or something might be allright, or the odd small shack, but no office blocks. And no buidlings that take up the majority of a map.
* You must post your map within 5 days of it becoming your turn. If not, it'll go to the next person.
* If I judge a level 'not worthy' of The Epic, it won't be included in the semi- official list. There will be no arguing with me- if I think it sucks, it won't be in The Epic. Breaking the rules slightly may, on occasion, be acceptable to me. But ask first, because if I don't like it, then I'm afraid you won't be in this.
* No making obscure, mixed references involving fat female hamsters. They can be taken the wrong way.

The Queing System
It's pretty much first come, first served. Stick your name down, and wait your turn. I will PM you if you don't realise you're up. You have a week to make your map... if you don't complete it by then, your turn goes to the next person in the que. You can re- enter the que as many times as you like.
VIP's are people who've been waiting a long time, somehow skipped, ignored, or not iinformed that it's their turn- and have the right to re-enter at pretty much the top of the que if they ever return to this thread.

The Maintinance Team
  • The Daily Llama: Creator of this thread, my decision is final and overides everybody elses.
  • Sweep: Filled in while I was gone. His opinions, advice, and requests in this thread must also always be respected and followed, unless contradicted by myself.
  • Wheel-_-134!!: The guy says he has a lot of free time, which is somewhat scarce to me. Listen to what the man says; he'll hopefully be there when I can't be.
Help is always appreciated. Just apply if you'd like to do some extra work. (Yay! Work that is extra!)
Anyway, well, listen to what Sweep has to say. I respect him a lot, and he has a great grasp of this. Everything he says is valid and should be listened to. Ta.

Other than this,
Yeah. Sorry about the whole rules thingo, and that it sounds complex, but anyway. It shouldn't be too hard to get the hang of, again. I hope you guys like this, and that it works out better than last time. Feel free to go through the other Epic thread if you want a feel of what I want this to end up like, and where I felt it went wrong. Thanks a lot.

Oh- and maps in this general style are exactly what I'm after...

And then, when all seemed lost...

Could it possily be? Yes, it is
Cyrano Mirage, striding across the planks, Sirrah on his arm and a roaring crew behing him. Via one thing or another, he became rich and wealthy, and drove the pirate invaders away.

Now, he has decided to return to you, the first crew he sailed with. There's one hitch- Cyrano Mirage seems to have picked up some new- found confidance along with his gold, which he left his old loyal crew. The one hitch, however, is that Cyrano wants to take over captainship of what introduced him to the life of piracy.

#5451 1 2005-11-29T11:30:35Z Teedle
Right. Time to ressurect...

It's Christmas Eve tommorow, and with keeping with the German tradition, that means that tommorow the exchange of gifts will begin. And so I thought I'd give you the following present- a BRAND NEW SONG OMMMIGODICANTBELIEVEHEACTUALLYDIDIT!!!!

Be warned, though. I went crazy with effects and flang and distortion and reverb and chorus and whatnot, just to see what it all did.

Don't worry, though, the novelty has worn off. And if I ever get around to recording Generic Blues or Shiny, it'll be
a) Better Quality than the first file
a2) Less tackily remixed than the second one.

You can still barely hear any lyrics, which is a relief, because it hides the fact that I simply cannot write them. It attempts to pay out bands like Simple Plan and whatnot, and to have a sort of wry humourous type of feel, but it doesn't really come across all that well when all you hear is "merrrgh engimmerrrrg agnmererrrrrga, faaaaaaawing thoooow ghhhh merrrrr meearerrerarearea angst."

So, without out further, besides me mentioning the lack of further ado, I present to you the most likely incorrectly spelt Engineered Angst.

Seriously, though, Merry Christmas. And I'd get you all something better, except that it'd cost money and be too much effort.

But it's the thought that counts, huh?

====================================================

Before you click on the link and download the first of my songs I've recorded, ever, (The rest are just floating along on the wind on loose- leaf sheets of paper), be warned:

This song has a keyboard and drum part I haven't recorded, due to tediousness, difficulty, and a severe deficiency in drum- owningness. Also, I am not- by ANY stretch of the imagination- a singer. My voice sounds like a hippopotomouse being slaughtered.

So, you still want a song from me, huh, huh? You can't heed my good advice and leave it alone?

Well then, you have nobody to blame but yourself.

Download and/or listen to "13th Serenade" right here:
The Daily Llama: 13th Serenade (Songs about songs)

Who knows. I might record one or two of my others- you know, other melodramatically titled and cheesily limericked songs- and post them here. Such as "A Dozen Blooming Roses", or "Romeo and Juliet", or "Fake The Emotion", or whatever. It's all good.
Or rather, it's all bad. This stuff is the sort of music you could stick in torture chambers. The perfect backdrop to getting your secret enemy to reveal all to you, ESPECIALLY when put on high repetition. (The song, not the secret enemy.)

So, enjoy. And I'm sorry I can't sing- but hey, because of that, the lyrics are pretty much incomprehensible on the recording, so no harm done, what what?

Here, have an updated first post

Well, the previouse epic flopped, big time. I'm ressurecting the idea, but with stricter (and more enforced) rules to try to avoid how the previous epic ended up.

Level guide
Part I- Hole (formica)
Part II- Like a bridge over muderous chainguns (sweep)
Part III- Nobody likes a weenie (nevermore)
Part IV- Don't mess with Thor (ngaged)
Part V- Too hot to Handle (Mark)
Part VI- Floating Islands (formica)
Part VII- Cloudy with a 90% chance of death (Dadaluma)
Part VIII- The Basaltic Plateau (maniac)
Part IX: The Crispy Cliffs Of Iqtaqtaluq (Blue Tetris)
Part X- The Big Mess Underfoot (sendy)
Part XI- Hand of God (sweep)
Part XII- Ghostly Reminiscentse (starcrossed)
Part XIII- The Giant Pear (barabajagal)
Part XIV- Raptured Landscape (pitch)
Part XV- Civilisation (formica)
Part XVI: Deadwood (sweep)
Part XVII: Darn Tall Trees (aju)
Part XVIII- Encased Island (Templex)
Part XIX: Science Lesson (bigblargh)
Part XX- Eagle Point (Mark_II)
Part XXI- The Forgotten Caverns (Alabaster)
Part XXII: Cave -in- Cliff (macaddict)
Part XXIII: Shrunk Evil_Bob
Part XXIV- The Cave In The Sky (wellsj)
Part XXV- Godspeed (_Sketch)
Part XXVI- The Slightly Insurmountable Hillocks of Granduer (KinGAleX)
Part XXVII: The Artificial (krusch)
Part XXIIX:As high as you can see (Aju)
Part XXIX: The Thorns of Alduran (Jiggerjaw12358)

Full Epic Images
This section is, basically, for those of you who want to look at big, extended panorma type images of the entire epic.
I'll update the thumbnails every 10 maps or so- only at major landmarks- but here are one or two of the images... (Click the link to view the images- I can't stick them on these forums for fear of butchering the layout of this page of this thread...)
Parts I- XX: Right to left. (As played)
Parts I-XX: Left to right (Classic sidescroller style)
I'd reccommend that everybody has a look at these images to see what works when you make a level, for keeping the continuity... There are sections that really merge togtether, and bits that don't. Look, admire, and make a mental note to make sure that yours fits in well in the big image.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Rules
These are the rules for adding a map to 'The Epic'...

* Each map must play right- to- left, with the ninja starting on the far right, and the exit being on the far left.
* Each map MUST contain, on the far right, the two columns that were on the far- left of the previous map. Thus, the series will play like a single, very long level.
* Every level must bear some resemblance to something real- ish. No pretty patterns, or metanet style levels. Try to incorporate gravitiy in most, if not all, of the level design.
* All level descriptions must link back to this thread and you must link to the map in this thread. The description should always involve- usually further- the vague plot of the thing. Nothing gory or too serious.
* You are not allowed to create 2 consecutive 'epic' maps.
* Nothing too insanely hard.
* No more 'inside a building' type levels; the idea of The Epic is realistic landscapes, and the enterior of a bulding- type levels never seem to fit that. A cityscape or something might be allright, or the odd small shack, but no office blocks. And no buidlings that take up the majority of a map.
* You must post your map within 5 days of it becoming your turn. If not, it'll go to the next person.
* If I judge a level 'not worthy' of The Epic, it won't be included in the semi- official list. There will be no arguing with me- if I think it sucks, it won't be in The Epic. Breaking the rules slightly may, on occasion, be acceptable to me. But ask first, because if I don't like it, then I'm afraid you won't be in this.
* No making obscure, mixed references involving fat female hamsters. They can be taken the wrong way.

The Queing System
It's pretty much first come, first served. Stick your name down, and wait your turn. I will PM you if you don't realise you're up. You have a week to make your map... if you don't complete it by then, your turn goes to the next person in the que. You can re- enter the que as many times as you like.
VIP's are people who've been waiting a long time, somehow skipped, ignored, or not iinformed that it's their turn- and have the right to re-enter at pretty much the top of the que if they ever return to this thread.

The Maintinance Team
  • The Daily Llama: Creator of this thread, my decision is final and overides everybody elses.
  • Sweep: Filled in while I was gone. His opinions, advice, and requests in this thread must also always be respected and followed, unless contradicted by myself.
  • Aju (Formerly Wheel-_-134!!): The guy says he has a lot of free time, which is somewhat scarce to me. Listen to what the man says; he'll hopefully be there when I can't be.
Help is always appreciated. Just apply if you'd like to do some extra work. (Yay! Work that is extra!)
Anyway, well, listen to what Sweep has to say. I respect him a lot, and he has a great grasp of this. Everything he says is valid and should be listened to. Ta.

The Polishing Team
  • The Daily Llama
  • Sweep
Please, feel free to sign up for this *new* team. Chances are, you'll be selected. Basically, once the epic is finished, the maps will be edited very slightly so that they run into eachother better, and form a more full, complete map. We might try to tweak the difficulty very slightly- just tone down the ridiculously hard maps a little bit, too. The storyline will also be edited, so that it actually leads somewhere and builds up to something bigger than just 'and then N went into a building, and stuff happened'.

We may even eventually work on building a website for this to be hosted on. Maybe.

Other than this,
Yeah. Sorry about the whole rules thingo, and that it sounds complex, but anyway. It shouldn't be too hard to get the hang of, again. I hope you guys like this, and that it works out better than last time. Feel free to go through the other Epic thread if you want a feel of what I want this to end up like, and where I felt it went wrong. Thanks a lot.

Oh- and maps in this general style are exactly what I'm after...

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Order, Order! (Future levels)

Sign up now!

(Part IIL=Aju)
Part IL= sweep
Part L=formica)

Aju is here for his great help during a second absence, and being a huge all- around help in this thread. If you are not sweep or Aju, you will NOT get the same privilige. Sorry.

"Christmas"- or, as it's now more commonly called, "Xmas"- is a holiday. HOWEVER.

Christmas, almost inarguably, has become *very* commercialised. It's... well. Okay. I believe it's a holiday, and pretty much nothing but.

When I say "Merry Christmas", I mean "I hope you enjoy your holiday". Not "I hope you enjoy the date that Christ, if you believe in that stuff people like some people do, may or may not have been born." Ergh. So. I, basically, mean "Have a happy holiday."

And, here down under, that's pretty much how it seems to be taken.

HOWEVER...
Maybe the only reason we're arguing against 'Happy Holidays' is force of habit and what we're familiar with- I have never once been wished a 'happy holiday', or heard anybody wish it to anybody else. Quite possibly the reason we're taking this ground is because, well, we don't know any different...

Ultimately, everything that anyone does will probably be offensive to someone else at some point; see chaos theory and all that jazz. The key is to strike a balance. Also true. A balance must be stricken. However, sounding like an idiot isn't anywhere near a valid reason to not be sensitive to another's religion, or beliefs, or practices. To say that it wouldn't be appreciated by "anyone" is a ridiclulous over-generalization, and I would like for you to retract that part.

Despite what I said above, I feel that this does demand something of a response.
It wouldn't just be sounding like an idiot.

'Happy Holidays' is, well, pretty much considered meaningless (possibly outside of America, possibly Australia, maybe just Victoria, I dunno.) Telling somebody 'Happy Holidays' sounds like you're wishing them something LESS than if you wished them a Merry Christmas. I don't know if this makes sense, but I think that this is the way it stands.
And I think it's also part of the reason why people outside of America, in this debate, seem to be choosing to say 'Merry Christmas', as opposed to those people in it, whose general trend seems to be saying 'Happy Holidays'. Because, 'Happy Holidays' seems to be a meaningless expression of goodwill in this sunburnt, skin peeling, skin cancer riddled country.

This isn't saying that I think this is a good thing, or something that shouldn't be changed- (if changing something like this is at all possible without constant exposure to it)- On the contrary, yes, I do think (for once) that this may be one aspect of American life I actually aprove of, but, well. Quote: Macaddict, 2005-12-23T20:49:49Z
Now, if the Bible was without artifacts to back it up, we couldn't say that it is accurate, because we wouldn't know. But tons of things in the Bible are backed up by archeology. Goliath, Babylon, the Assyrians, Hittites, distances between cities, even mountains.

So. Ummm. Let my grab a few examples of books I'm reading at the moment...

Angels and Demons- Dan Brown
For starters, I'm rereading "Angels and Demons" by Dan Brown. All artwork and locations in the book are true, as well as references to Satanism, the Illimunati, The Vatican, the process of papality (what a sweet made up word) and all of that. They are all fact. All of the distances, locations, directions, settings, duties, statues, paintings, and documents in the book are true.
However, there's no secret Illuminati lair in Sant Pauls. There never were four potentieal popes killed right before the election type thing. A canister of antimatter was never dropped from a great hight in midair from a helicopter. Robert Langdon, the main character, is complete fiction in an otherwise totally true environment that's sort of taken a turn from 'reality'. Everything in that book is true, except for the events and many (note: Many, not all) of the people.

Harry Potter series- J.K. Rowling
Another book? Allright. Harry Potter and the Order Of The Pheonix, which I'm also rereading. Slightly harder, this one. However- it takes place in the 'real world'- we just can't see the Wizarding world, because it's hidden by their magic. Thus, we can't disprove that they're around, because we'd never find out- and on the occasion we did, we'd have our memories altered. But the locations in the book- England and whatnot- are correct.

A Quiver Full Of Arrows- Jeffery Archer
Then there's Jeffery Archers "A Quiver Full Of Arrows", which consists mainly of actual events that've just been embellished a lot to make them a lot more interesting to read. Only 1 of the short stories was entirely made up from his imagination. However-
It has been embellished A LOT to make it readable. To a huge extent. And a whole host of things that didn't happen happen in the stories, to make them more exciting to read.
(Sound sorta familiar, MacAddict_17? To, say, The Bible?)
Or, shall we twist it this way...
Twelve Red Herrings contains 9 true stories, and 3 made up entirely by Jeffery Archer. So. Does the fact that 9 are true, and that three can't easily be disproved, make those three made up ones true?

The Hitchikers Triliogy of 5- Douglas Adams
One or two more examples of books I've read recently come to mind:
The Hitchikers Guide To The Galaxy, which STARTS in an actual place in an actual country on the earth, and the earth related bits occur in the real geography and with real factual stuff.
However, I think we can all say with great certainity that the world hasn't exploded yet. And the whole concept of, say, Vogons in space seems quite unlikely.

The Science of Discworld parts 1, 2, and 3- the bits written by Terry Pratchett
Or, how about, Terry Pratchetts "The Science of Discworld", which has sections based on the 'real Earth'. How can we prove we're not just sitting in a contained reality on a shelf in the Library of Unseen University on the Discworld? There's no way to do so at all. Period. Because this universe in whole, complete- but accessable from a different universe, though we can't go there.



Read the above examples. In 2000 years time, does this mean that all of the above examples will suddenly be true? That people should believe everything listed above, because they can't disprove the 'false' stuff and know that lots of the things in there are true?

Go ahead, say No. I dare you.

(And I'd deal with some of your other arguments too, but frankly, I can't be bothered, and you're not going to change your opinion at all.)

Quote: 7!, 2006-01-14T00:09:39Z
Some features are hard to turn off, (system restore
how is system restore hard to turn off? its better off anyway and only takes a second or 2 to do so.

Better.... off?
(Repeats to self.)
System restore... is better... off....

No. Just, no.
It's saved my neck a total of once, but it was worth it.

I installed some software the school gave us ("Norman anti- virus", written in the same font as Norton) because our good 'ol system hogging Norton had long since expired. So, I figured, why not give this a try- I'm slightly sick of Norton and its system hoggingness, and the virus definitions were a few months old.

So, in I go and install Norman. It loads the installation screen, and freezes. I idly fidly with CTRL- ALT- DLT untill I realise nothing is doing anything- even the mouse is frozen. So I switch the computer off at the socket, and restart it.

For the startup time of the computer, everything is fine. And then, 3 seconds after windows boots, every last bit of the computer freezes. Every. Last. Bit. Mouse included, again.

So. What am I left to work with? I can't get rid of the half completed installation in 3 seconds, I can't stop the thing from loading without msconfig, and I can't do much else. I try restarting in safe mode. But, seeing as the creators of Norman AntiVirus are idiots, it loads up anyway and freezes it after those dreaded 3 seconds.

If I didn't have system restore, I would've had to reinstall EVERYTHING from scratch again, and would've lost a major assignment as well as some pretty important stuff Mum needed for work- powerpoints for seminars and stuff. Seriously. It paid off in a big way. And I'm very, very gratefull to that nifty little function, even if it has pretty much no value for getting rid of viruses and whatnot and you need to disable it before doing a full system virus scan. What the heck, I don't care. It saved my neck, and thus to it I am eternally gratefull.

CUPERTINO, Saturday: Apple Computer CEO Steve Jobs announced today that his company had retained global leadership in the lucrative wanker market in 2003.

'Sure, they push the "technology" and "value" envelopes, but we're out here on our own pushing the "pretty translucant plastic" envelope,' he said.
The Apple boss believes the company's strong performance in the wanker sector is a testament to the company's careful attention to its users.
'Often computer companies focus on things like power, features and ease of use', he said. 'Whereas Apple focuses only on its computers featuring in wallpaper magazine.'
Job is confidant that Apple can continue its dominance amoung the snob set. 'We're continuing to build OSX, which is just a great product,' he said. While it performs exactly the same as the G4 and costs tice as much, it's in a whole new tint of beinge.

In any case, the original intended lighthearted tone to this thread- which I was sorta pulled away from partway through- is sort of irretrievably lost, which is exactly why I'm gonna try to retrieve it anyway.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

I just spent a weekend at the beach, and this country of Australia isn't the only thing that's sunburnt. On top of which, the week before was totally and utterly miserable with temperatures reaching the 40's and high 30's at night, and muginess so thick that breathing became next to impossible, leaving me the choice of slowly drowning in a rapidly expanding pool of sweat drooling from under my arms, or going into the two air conditioned rooms in my house, which'd result in more difficulty breathing due to asthma attacks due to the air conditioners being sucky.

And, I really do quite dislike this country, from its absolute abundance of poisonous snakes- in fact, for a while we had a brown snake living in our garden, prompting much wearing of rainboots even in afore- mentioned 40 degree weather, to its demented chainsaw swallowing a frog-esque traditional accent, to the government, to the absolute lack of snow, but most importantly- the horrible (and in Melbourne, extraodinarily erratic) weather. It's really left me yearning for someplace where the weather is considered horribly wet and miserable all the time, someplace without summers and where I can wear my full length coats and jackets, someplace- well- not here.

Did I mention the half- dead Australian music scene? Well, the music generally isn't even too bad, but the lyrics tend to be about as heartbreaking, gripping and emotional as "Three Blind Mice."

I gave up on America due to the lethal combination of Bush, Religous extremists, and Rednecks- which I've had enough of here in Australia, thanks to my sunscreen never quite seeming to work.

So, I narrowed it down to Canada, the UK, and New Zealand. These are my thoughts on each of the above-

England Pros:
* Utterly mild- some might even say unpleasent- weather.
* The English accent is the most wonderfull thing I've ever heard
* The cities sound beautifull, as do the museums, libraries, countryside, and old castles and ruins
* People there are, apparantly, very polite and apologetic and reasonable
* Place names like "Shellow Bowells"
* Near the rest of Europe, as opposed to Australia on the arse- end of the world.
* Europeans tend to be tall, which is helpfull if you're nearing 7 foot like me.
England Cons:
* The culture and wonderfull quirks of Britain architecture are being eaten up by sensless new buildings being errected, tearing beautifull old homes down
* So very, very small
* Lack of employment
* "Musn't grumble, musn't grumble"
* The beaches. Did you know that a number of beaches in England- some popular tourist hotspots- aren't classified as existing as, well, beaches? And this is because they breached the maximum sewerage levels in the water so much it seemed easier to ignore they exist than to actually try to dilute the turds a bit more.

Canada- Pros.
* Some people say I have a canadian accent
* It's cold, horribly wet, and icy
* Skiing! It probably exists, I think.
* It's near America while not being in it. Maybe even close enough to shoot Bush, if I ever see him.
Canada- Cons
* It's surrounded by a country ruled by a man that is sorely missed by a village in texas, who want their idiot back.
* I have very little idea about anything else to do with it.

New Zealand: Pros
* So very, very green. Wonderfully green.
* Similar to Australia in many ways, stopping me from stressing too much when entering this foreign environment and forgetting some things, like how to be house broken.
* The Maori culture sounds very interesting.
* Home of EXTREME SPORTS and stuff, which'd keep me amused for a while.
* The land of THe Lord Of The Rings.
* It, like Australia, is girt by sea. (Honestly. 'girt'. Who uses the word girt? When's the last time you've heard somebody say "That lake is girt by houses", or "My bed is girt by toenail clippings", or in the movie cinema "LOOK OUT, JAMES BOND, YOU'RE GIRT BY UKRANIUM NUCLEUR WEAPON EXPERTS HOLDING GUNS!". It's such a useless word.)
New Zealand Cons:
* It's like Australia in many ways, including the weather, which is only slightly midler. Or so I believe.
* The accent. Oh, goodness, the accent. See, I think I just hate it so because I once had a really, really bad teacher with a new zealandish accent who yelled at me when I accidently stapled myself in the finger in first grade, but I really dislike it.
* Upon meeting ANY foreigners, hearing them make the cliche'd sheep jokes, as though they're ignorant of the fact that after we've finished our sexual activities with the sheep, we export it to THEM and THEY are the ones that eat it.



(Oh, and off topic, but-
Blue Tetris. How would you feel about being arch nemesises? I've wanted one for quite some time, and you definately look suitable to me! Seriously, we could be great together! Those romantic voyages on shipdeck, shooting at eachother with machine guns... those lonely islands in the carribean in which we'd set up our bases and stock up on weapons, ready for our next attack... those few extra words at the end of our sigs, saying "Arch nemesis of...."
Oh, the places we'll blow, we'll blow! Up! It'll be fantastic.)

#140784 55 2006-02-08T07:57:25Z Teedle
The waves of the sea, drooling half- heartedly onto lukewarm, muddy sand. The sound of the aforementioned waves of the sea, drooling half- heartedly onto the lukewarm, sandy mud.
The sky was black, though a short burst of light would sometimes flicker from between the clouds, and a gap in the grey smoke filling the sky.

Now, move up the beach the ashed remains of what was once a beautifull line of palm trees, still glowing red at places. Move up the slick of a blackened, oily substance... avert your eyes as you pass by two dead bodies, still oozing blood... up to the humble huts of the villagers, or what remains of them, and smell the well- poisened, a smily green, polluted forever, with a foul stream rising from the muck. Now, hoist yourseld on a huge crane like in movies, and sweep down the other side of the hill, past more damage and a few twisted metallic ruins, speeding up over a green slope marred by burns and festering, ozzing bodies... back to the oily sea, reluctantly schmooling more muck onto what were once pristine, white grains of sand.

Now, walk towards what you mistook as a lump of blackened seaweed. Zoom in- I mean, bend towards- it.
And jump to the top of the heap, where a head suddenly emerges, gasping and sputtering a mixture of blood and grime.

Watch it lie there for what would be hours, but which has been reduced to seconds so that you don't get bored by long, long paragraphs explaining the general lack of action. Watch it stagger to its feet, with what was one the mans hair now a wretched wreck of tangled blackness, allready host to several insects and lice. Look at its face, one handsome in a rugged, small mouthed and sort of Llama- like way. Look at the Darth Vader- esque remains of its face grimace in pain, rage, and disgust.

Suddenly, an inhuman shreik of pain as it drops once again to its knees, tears leaving little pools of grime on its cheeks. A gentle curse, another scream, a choked sob which turns into a horrendous cough as the hideous vision sways upon its legs. And then silence.

Now lean forwards, as the synthesid orchestra fads away, and there is no sound left but the sound of the waves. Listen harder, and hear the faint and shallow rasp of my voice.

"I'll kill you, someday..." comes the whisper. "You'll pay... for what you've done..."
"YOU WILL PAY! I'LL KILL YOU!!"
And then, nothing but echos.
"You killed my family, you took my townspeople, I lie in the bodies of my kindred spirits and dearest friends... and for what? What have I done to earn this cruel punishment? Why did you have to do this?

WHY?!

But it's not over... I will... I will have my... vengance... on you... Blue... Tetris..."

And then the figure falls over onto the grime, a sillouhette against the sickly light of the moon. The crane, still attatched to you, pulls away- and you see the distant, twitching figure grow smaller on the sand as the landscape fades to black and the sound of the waves die, choked by the nothingness.

And then one last whisper, before a scroll of paper filled with a ton of words and names is rolled up in front of your face- "Oh, Blue Tetris, you looked so bloody hot when you killed my sister."

TO BE CONTINUED...

(And on the comic? Yeah, sure, I might actually give it a shot...)
#141203 64 2006-02-09T06:13:46Z Teedle
Foromika Kampur- Airport.

An airport- dirty, shabby, grimy, and all sorts of other adjectives. Grey suits walking past on either side, and in the middle of it all, an unkempt man with slightly more stubble on one side of the face than the other.

The man is barely recognisable as The Daily Llama, once a proud, tall man finally settled down with a life, and with a future... now a broken, shattered, and just as tall man unsettled with his life, and the prospects of his future.

It was days like these when he considered that maybe his future wasn't worth having, when he thought of all the other futures that had been cut horribly short, due to.. events... and-
No. Don't think like that. You know where it'll lead.

But still, sometimes the empty sea looked so inviting... to dive into the waves, and end the whole tortured wreck there, to wade onto the rocky shores of eternity. But, no, not yet... maybe once Blue Tetris had been torn from his miserable, lowly existance, maybe then he could...

A mobile phone rang, jerking the world back into focus. A stumble, a quick dig through torn and dirty pockets, and the phone fell through a hole in one of them, only to get snagged around the knees. Quickly, the Llama shoved his hands down his pants to grab it and recieve the call, only to have his phone fall onto the floor, and himself promptly follow. A few awkward moments later, the phone was in his hands and the small crowd that had gathered to oggle at the man struggling with his hands down his pants had dispersed.

"Hi, Jerome" said a brittle and broken voice, the voice of a broken man.
"Hey, Llama! It's great to hear from you at last! I never thought you'd come off that Island again!" This voice was bright and perky, and everything that The Daily Llama's voice wasn't.
"No. Neither did I."
"Anyway... I've heard some interesting info on this Blue character... Intersting sort of a guy, as far as Mad Scientists go."
"He's evil."
"Oh, right, whatever you say... but then again, the handsome ones always are."
A sigh, and a fidget, and the readjustment of a belt to free the second arm that was still dangling on the inside of his trousers.
"Well... anyway... I've collected info on the guy, and even found the location to his secret lair." An awkward pause, then Jerome enthusiastically went on. "It wasn't actually that hard to find, you know, because it said 'Blue Tetris' Secret Lair' on it."
Another sigh.
"Come now, Jerome, did it never even occur to you that anything proclaiming itself to be a secret lair isn't, in fact, secret, and is doubtfull to be even remotely lair-like?"
"Oh, you're always criticising me! Always! I do my best, you know."
"Yes. Yes, I'm sure you do. Anyway, I have to leave now, my plane's going to go. I'll meet you at the usual place?"
"I'll see you there."

As the plane took off, The Daily Llama fancied he could see another smaller plane- a blue one- in the distance, flying towards the island. For a further second, he fancied he could even see Blue Tetris' face, staring out the window.
But then the vision was gone, and the sky was empty again.
Nothing for it, then, but to get some sleep...

Sitting in Economy, The Daily Llama tried to relax insomuch as it was possible with your knees pushed halway up your nostrols by the back of the chair in front of you, and a crying child kicking the seat behind.
When he did fall asleep, he dreamt of his sister, and of Blue Tetris, and of a burning island, and the bittersweet taste of revenge... and, inexplicably, of a giant burger riding a pogo stick.

A few hours later, he arrived on the sunny shores of Australia.

A few hours after that, his luggage arrived in Kyrgastan.

A heart is a precious thing to waste,

So. The hearts target is clear but once a year, when cupid pulls his arrow string. That day seems to me to be most likey Valentines Day, which seems appropriate seeing how recent it was.

For the eighth is always on the hour,
the twenty being on the min.
The one is left trailing far behind,

Okay. Now. This is still very unclear to me, but something worth consider is that we have the whole 'always' thing returning for this verse;

Be warned- there's much speculation in this post, nothing definate.

Roy. G. Biv's a jerk.
Okay, so using the list I was fiddling with a while ago, I decided to try adding the number of different letters under each 'catagory' to the letter that catagory began with, to come up with a different series of letters...

R+4= V
O+3= R
Y+1= Z
G+5= L
B+4= F
I+5= N
V+2= X

(Other+6=x+6)

Okay, so, that's definately pure nonsense- it doesn't even have any vowels...
But, what IF the letters under 'other' are added to 'O' (for Orange), then you'd get...

R+4= V
O+9= X
Y+1= Z
G+5= L
B+4= F
I+5= N
V+2= X

Still not good. Maybe the amounts of letters under the catagories should have counted for ALL of the letters in the passage...

But a prelimary scan of the sorts of letters you'd probably end up with seems to make that seem highly unlikely. So, I *think* this means that the ROYGBIV approach isn't going to get us anywhere. Please, Kablizzy, feel free to contradict me... And, anybody, please feel free to contradict me here too... I might do it properly a bit later, but not right now, because there's something else I'd like to post...

#145537 931 2006-02-19T04:06:01Z Teedle
Relating to Sweeps stuff

Oh, goodness!

I just had a thought, laying on my bed and looking on my bookshelf...

The Carlyle group- as referenced by Sweep on the madness temple hosted Legacy thingy (Seen here: http://www.madnesstemple.com/legacy/) is none other but that thingy that Michael Moore was talking about for part of Fahrenheit 9/11. I can vagualy remember that, and it was something to do with Bin Ladens family, I think...

A quick google search showed that this was true, coming up with many bin laden/ bush/ carlyle group references, and also THIS:
Quote: http://www.carlyle.com/eng/geo/casestudy-2226.html
Carlyle Realty Partners has successfully exited 74 Grand Street, a 300,000 square foot redeveloped office building in Jersey City, New Jersey.

In June 1999, Carlyle entered into the redevelopment of 74 Grand to take advantage of increasingly tight leasing conditions in Manhattan.  Carlyle and its partner, SJP Properties, delivered the building for a cost of $145 per square foot, which represents a 50 percent discount to Manhattan building values and 30 percent below Jersey City values.  "With this advantage, we were able to seize on demand from financial services companies that were seeking lower-cost space outside Manhattan," says Gabe Finke, Carlyle's Principal who led the deal.

Carlyle completed a full-building lease with Merrill Lynch at rents 16 percent above original budget and well ahead of the projected lease-up pace.  After completing the lease, Carlyle sold the building in March 2001.  Over a 21-month hold period, the investment generated a 2.5x equity multiple and approximately $17 million of profit.

George Bush's father works for the Carlyle group, and the carlyle group made much money from the War on Terrorism (You know the war, right? The one where they liberated oil?)

There's a whole lot of information in Fahrenheit 9/11 (Of which I have the book, which I'm planning on rereading to refresh my knowledge and maybe get a better idea of how this may tie in with this), but there's also plenty of websites around... a skim read of this one: http://www.truthout.org/docs_01/01.11F.Arms.Carlyle.p.htm - seems to be looking very helpfull, too, for anybody else interested.

The problem is, I don't know how this relates to Kablizzy's clue, though Sweep has told me that his clues are unrelated to Kablizzy's- though they should lead to the same conclusion/ word, the two do not tie in together- people can work them out using only one set.

So. I'm considering working on this, and doing some research (Though, right now, I really should be studying...) on The Carlyle Group and their move to New Jersey...

But Wait- There's SO MUCH MORE just 'discovered' by me...

Allright. Adding in 'anon' to the google search of keywords from Sweeps legacy thing, guess what? I found a sight that has the same message, pretty much word for word, as what Sweep has hosted on the legacy thing. Furthermore, what's the site called? Radiohead News. Guess who sweep's favourite band is? Radiohead.

Here's the website: http://www.ateaseweb.com/news/
Here's the relevant post: Radiohead is dead, long live The Carlyle Group

Two new posts again on Dead Air Space tonight.

nr. 1:

If you cant beat em, join em.

We have decided to change the name of the band to

THE CARLYLE GROUP

for tax reasons and are moving our offices to Jersey.

Thank you. That'll be all.

Anon

nr 2:

i was looking for a drum machine and found this.

http://www.albinoblacksheep.com/flash/drum.php

Thom

[Posted by adriaan at 01:24 AM, February 17, 2006]

Okay...
So. I figure it's some Radiohead themed political swipe at the carlyle group by the alternative band... Written by Radiohead, perhaps?

Anyway, the ONLY inconsistancy between the two messages- the one on Sweeps website, ande the one on the Radiohead News website, is the word band, instead of Project.

I'm still poised to do some more research on the Carlyle group if this turns out not to be the answer, but I'm currently putting my money on the word band.

I'm just going to check to see if there's any obvious way you could get the same answer from Kablizzy's clue, but I'm fairly confident that's the last word.

*phew*

#148744 7 2006-02-26T06:28:01Z Teedle
Great idea, Atramentis...

The most amazingly simple recipe of all times, the thing I've been making after school every couple of days for the past year or so...

Sweet potato Mustard Chips. Llama. (Sorry, no clever Llama themed pun this time, folks!)

Ingrediants:
*Sweet Potatoes
*Olive Oil
*Mustard seeds (About 1.5 teaspoons per serving)
*Mustard powder
*Dried chilly/ perri perri/ cayene pepper
*Dried spices of your choice
*Dried herbs- of your own choice.
*salt + pepper to taste

Method:
*Slice the sweet potato finely.
*Dry- fry the mustard seeds in pan.
*Add in the oil and sweet potato slices
*Fry the sweet potato slices, stirring constantly to mix them around and get them properly cooked on both sides
*Sprinkle on mustard powder + chilly from time to time
*Take out of pan when golden brown
*Sprinkle with salt + pepper
*Can be served with tomato sauce (ketchup), or sweet chilly sauce, or whatever you jolly well feel like serving them with.

Takes me about 10 minutes to slice, but I'm totally paranoid about chopping off my fingers (I cut them quite badly a couple of times as a kid), so it should take you no more than 5 or 6.
cooking is very easy, and can take 5 minutes if you do them all at once and do them right... although, for your first few batches, it can be safer to cook them in batches and take slightly more time.
I strongly suggest you fry them in a pan and avoid the deep fryer- you get more of a sweet potato-y taste that way.
Modify the recipe to your taste- add in whatever dried herbs + spices you want/ have on you.
You don't even need to use the mustard seeds + powder if you don't like it, but I think it goes brilliantly with the sweet potato taste.
I prefer them dry, without sauces, but use them if you like.

It's a lot nicer than it sounds, and probably the easiest- and nicest- way of preparing sweet potato, my favourite vegetable.

#7118 1 2006-02-28T06:21:21Z Teedle
For about a month, I've been putting together thoughts- a lot better arranged and thought out than my thoughts for the Meteor thread- and scribbled comments for a new, hopefully rather spectacular RPG I've been working on.

I've got about 10 'riddles' (Though much more than that) and a further 3 'steps' fully drafted, with about 5 more riddles and 10 more 'steps' existing in little notes to myself to be more fully explored later. There's going to be about 25 riddles and 16 steps to get through before finishing, but this may change, depending on if I can get away with doing less or if you all die or not.

This roleplaying game is hopefully going to be rather different to anything done before, dealing with influences as varied as Gary Kilworths satire, the television show 'lost' and Agatha Christies '10 little niggers'. Not to mention some very Joss Whedon style situations, provided any of you know him and his work well enough. An a ton of small in- references. All set in a survival- type situation, desperately stumbling towards the exits as they rest of you are picked off, one by one.

None of the graphics, sound clips, or animations have even STARTED to be converted to a format more readily shown on the forum than sketches on loose leaf paper, but they'll get there. I'm going for a very lush look for this, in order to give it a very different feel than, for instance, Kablizzy's forum event. Not to mention I have some interesting, relatively short prose allready drafted for the plotline, which should also help here. Trust me, this should be big, if it works out.

(And, for the record, the riddles are going to be- for the most part- very different to the type done by Kablizzy, though there may be some influnces from what he's done...)

And, hopefully it will. You'll all control 2 characters- seeing as it's so easy to get killed, it's nice to have somebody to fall back on, rather than to die on the very first 'event' and be forced to stick around only as a ghost, with no real motivation to get through this.

So. Hopefully this'll be big, and I have a lot allready planned- riddles, graphics, music, sounds, even a nice little excursion to another- very simple and basic- forum involving no signup, created exclusively for this event, with a certain 'cameo' primed to make a guest appearance that'll hopefully turn out fairly interesting.

Anyway. The problem is, if I only get very few people interested and sign up, this whole thing will probably just flop. So this thread words twofold.
First of all, as an advertisment for something being planned that'll probably come out in a month or two, and second of all, a way to let me know if this will just be a waste of time- if this generates little intrest. It just won't work as well without a relatively large 'cast'.

Keep all of this in mind, and that this is looking to be a LOT more special than Meteor, who here is interested?

Thank you for sharing.

But, on the note of garlic bread,

The Daily Llama Bread
Ingrediants:
*French Stick
*Butter/ Margerine
*Garlic
*Mozerella cheese
*Parmensan cheese
*Chilly sauce- I reccommend hot perri perri or a habanero paste, and sweet chilly tends to taste horrid in here.
*Italian herb blend

The method is really, really simple. Cut up the french roll, butter both sides of the bread very well (to stop it from drying out in the oven), stick on many combinations of above ingrediants and lay each piece individually on a tray, which then goes in the oven for about 12- 15 minutes at a reasonably high temperature.

For more traditional garlic bread, just use margerine, garlic, and italian herbs, and reform the portion of the french stick as you make it- layer it back in on itself. Then, simply wrap the whole lot in aluminium foil (bread stick shaped again, but cut in pieces inside) and stick that in the oven for a while.
Tastes way, way, WAY better than anything you can buy at a shop.

Oh- and, a very brief overview of something worth experimenting with-
Pazza
Basically, make like a normal pizza- but use pasta sauce rather than tomato paste on the base, and layer with pasta prepared simultaneously as the rest of the pizza. Other than that, do the same things as normal with the ingrediants that you most like.
(Tastes the best when you make your own pizza base, but most people don't have the time. I've only done it twice (with my own base), and it was brilliant- I'll look up the recipe if anybody is interested.)

ALTERNATIVELY-
Put on a small layer of pasta sauce, some lasasgne sheets, then more pasta sauce of a different nature (A homemade cheese sauce, using butter, flour, milk and chese can work great on the top layer) and simply do normal pizza stuff on top of this.

It's way, way nicer than it sounds.

(Yes, Pazza IS inspired by the Eoin Colfer book "The Supernaturalists" (a very good book), but significantly advanced beyond the brief mention of pazza being a mixture of pizza and pasta. So there.)

#155219 52 2006-03-16T14:16:41Z Teedle
Okay, so today I bought the colplay album "A rush of blood to the head"...

It's... an awkward album... A lot more in the style of Parachutes than X&Y, which pleases me greatly, seeing as I preffered their old sound. (Not that it's changed all that much, but still.) Yet, it lacks whatever it is in Parachutes that made my go "MAN. I LOVE COLDPLAY AND WANT TO MARRY THEM. OH WAIT, I CANT BE A FANGIRL, I'M MALE. *sob*
My life sucks..."

So, anyway, I finally got around to buying A Rush Of Blood To The Head- I chose it over the Mountain Goats' The Sunset Tree (An album that amuses me very greatly, and that it does this causes great offence to his many fans, but meh...) because the album art is so cool. It's, like, some semi melted retarded sculpture of a person of unknown gender and sort of missing the top half of their head- including the section that contains a brain.
Now. The first track of this album is very political. George Bush is very political. There's a guy without a brain on the front cover of this song... Coincidence? Or something much deeper?!
Also, whoever made the computer thingo appears to have forgotten to actually apply the texture to the thing. I find this impressive- it makes the album look so stylishly unique, yet also half- assed... I love it.

Anyway. Onto the music...
The opening track, Politik, is a piano wrecking heavyish alternative ballad with lyrics just cryptic enough to draw in listeners who agree with what they think Coldplay are saying about, well, politics in this song- and also audiances who would dissagree if they could see what the other fans think coldplay mean, but don't quite see it...
In any case, this song rockzers my sockzerz. So, yeah.

In My Place is a nice, easygoing pop ballad which breaks up the solemn, sad and slightly confused mood from Politik. Then comes another song. Woot.

The Scientist is a song that I used to absolutely adore, untill I realised that it was pretty much the only song a certain female and I had in common with our musical tastes... A certain female who stole my copy of The Sims 2, a crime so horrible that it pales all other crimes by comparison.
Except for that theft gone horribly wrong in the bleach factory... but ANYWAY.

Then there's, like, more music and songs... none of it really matters all that much, really... and then, right at the end of the album, there's a song called "Amsterdam."
I have never heard such beauty before in my life....
It takes 4 minutes (on a 5 minute track) before any instrunments other than the piano kick in... but I don't care. I love this song. So much. I've just heard it repeated about 10 times in a row, and I don't plan on stopping playing it any time soon...
I haven't acted that way with any song since "The Xbox Song"


(Oh- and, incase there was any confusion... Yes, I do love Coldplay.)

#156106 31 2006-03-20T14:09:26Z Teedle
On cutting yourself...

Before reading this, especially if you happen to be a snooping family member, a forumer who particularly cares for me anybody I know 'in the real world'- please, know that I haven't cut myself. And that, insofar as I can tell, I'm not going to.

I don't want to get too deeply into the circumstances, but recently, I... well, actually, I don't even want to go into this with cryptic remarks about all of this 'lest it ends up becoming obvious exactly what it is I'm talking about, and adding a couple of numbers together and realising something that I've been trying, and failing, to keep private.

Suffice to say, a few weeks ago... I was happy, content, and filled with bubbly feelings. Then, I came back from this, intergrated back into the world past that one brilliant, flawless moment... and, I realise I'm not happy and content with the ways things were before that night. And I realise that things are, in fact, a lot worse than they were before that...

Lots of this does happen to hinge on a girl. One whom I had desperately yearned for, then desperately hoped I was over, and thought I was. And one whom...
I should cut lots of this out again, because- again- of people who might read this who I actually know... So, I'll try to be suitably brief and vague...
My memories of this are so vivid, so clear, so... everything. Every last moment, gesture, smell, sight, sound... I'll never forget them, and these hours in my life- the joyous ones- are ones that seem so real, so full...
I can barely recall what I ate for breakfast, and the past 3 days- involving a party, shopping (and again about 5 days ago), having a friend over and going to a different friend's house, computer games and conversations and walking in the woods- are a blur, a mixture of vague images and feelings I can sort of recall if I concentrate hard enough, but know that a month or so from now I'll have more or less no recollection of.

But, suffice to say, I'd never felt as close to anybody before, even if a logical part of my mind was able to tell the rest that-
Oh, screw it.

Anyway, things have come to pass that will never be repeated again... or anything remotely like them. Circumstances have changed more drammatically, and there's a sense of loss beyond what's easy to describe.
And, despite what it may sound like, I'm not talking about "had a girlfriend, dont have a girlfriend anymore". It's not even mere unrequited love. It's far deeper, but I really, really don't want to get into this now.


So. For a brief, shining moment everything was brilliant. Now, life sucks more than it ever did before, and there's a sense of loss more than what text- or emoticons- can describe. I'm getting frequent dreams and nightmares on the topic, every moment awake feels pretty much meaningless, and you're pretty much in the darkest days of your life so far- but its even worse, since you're haunted by the memory of intense joy, so recently.

Did I ever feel like cutting myself?

No. Not untill later, at a party, when a certain song played.
I can't describe it exactly, but feeling so miserable and having this brief recollection of a moment of perfect happiness, and of hope, and of being absolutly oblivious of how the situation is going to end and what absolute crapness lies ahead, stretching towards the present and as far as you can see into the future- It was, basically, a wave of emotion stronger than ANYTHING I had ever felt before. I felt like (though, on reflection, I doubt I was) on the verge of spewing, or passing out- feeling beyond tears, beyond sadness, beyond anything in the world that words could describe something like that.

If you're in a situation like that, and you're like me- hell, I can't imagine how some people could live their lives in such a state- you'd want to do anything to just tear the feeling away from you. Anything at all.
The thing about physical pain is that, it hurts less. A lot less. And, when you're focused on how much your hand or wrist hurts, it hurts like hell- and you don't notice the other pain. You're never going to feel good doing it, but at least you're going to stop feeling quite so crap- if even for a relatively short time.

At least, these are my thoughts, as longwinded as they are. I don't know what the experiances of anybody else are/ have been, but I seriously think I understand how people can drive steel into their flesh in return for nothing but misery... because it happens to be lesser misery they're heading towards, and that's better than nothing.






(Oh- and, heck, sorry for making you read through such a long post filled with so much drivel. Don't worry, I'll try to spam lots to make up for it. )

YES. YES YOU DID. I WANTED YOU TO HOPE THAT THINGS GET WORSE- THEN, I COULD FULLY... erm?

No, thanks for that... as in, seriously. And, moments do pass, I know- but the knowledge of that is sort of cold comfort actually during them... still, I hugely appreciate it.

More on emo stuff and the emo subculture: Maybe I'm wrong/ naive/ don't have a proper understanding/ (even Australian?) but here, insofar as I can tell with friends and the like, people don't... label themselves something and then try to fit that label. The people I know well and are labelled something, sort of act like themselves then there seems to be a general consensus of "She's acting goth", "He is acting emo", "She's such a hippie", whatever...
If anything, the conforming to fit your subculture has occured quite some time after they've been thought of as part of it... such as, a girl becoming labbelled 'emo' and continuing to wear brightly coloured clothes untill there are very strong expectations amoungst everybody that she'd wear black... and so, she eventually does.
(This is all based on my narrow experiance of the matter, which is definately very limited, and there's a huge chance that what I'm describing isn't the norm.)

On the splurge of text up there and people flaming emoness...

That wasn't intended to make me sound emo or justify my being emo, because I'm sort of... not. Given a choice, I tend to wear semiformal shirts and long pants, with a jacket (if I can find one) or a sweater over the top... My musical tastes nowadays are generally lighter alternative (the verve, coldplay), some australian rock pop (Brilliant Fanzine comes to mind), some folk styled pop (say, Belle and Sebastian or Josh Pyke), some occasional heavier alternative (such as, the Betea Band or Vast- yes, I definately understand those of you who hate the band) and a couple others like Rooney or The Mountain Goats.

I wasn't trying to say I'm emo. I know as a fact that I'm definately not labelled as one... (Quick! Quick! Hide from the evil flaming forumers! Stick your head in your shell and look non threatening! )
Just that, for the first time, I understand... I understand how people could want to be, and I understand for the first time how people could feel crap enough to want to cut themselves, and I truly understand for pretty much the first time in my life how truly crap other people can feel in theirs... And that the perspective of "Oh, hey, at least I'm not being bombed by America" can be pathetically unhelpful in the circumstances.

I'm not saying that no emos are people who sign up just to be part of the current passing subculture fad. Heck, I'm not even saying that they make up a minority of the group or anything like that...
I have no idea about this stuff. But I seriously reckon that, unless you've been in Master JMD's exact situation- Unless you've actually BEEN him and felt what he feels/ has felt, and unless you've lived his life entirely and can say for a fact exactly what he must be feeling and/ or going through... you can not just say to him (or any emo), "Get Over It. Its really easy, you know. Oh, and you're just part of a fad in the subculture trend, you're just in there to be a nonconformists and you're conforming anyway, so get over it you little whiny jerk."
Okay, I know that none of you are actually saying that, but still.

Unless you've been through it (And who knows if I've been through anything that compares with the majority of 'emo' cases), you have no right to generalise and insult people based on the way they appear/ act or the subculture they belong to. The fact they belong to a subculture doesn't necessarily mean anything other than that they've been through some tough stuff, acted a certain way, and been labelled accordingly.

I've never lived anybody's life, and so I can't criticise them.
And I've only learnt recently just how crap life can make you feel, and why you might want to cope by doing things that 'emos' do... and I have a strong suspicion that many people who are critical of emos cannot relate.

This is why I don't hate emos.




Oh- and all of this reminds me of a quote:
You nonconformists are all the same!

Have you ever done something really stupid while angry- like dig nails into your hands, leaving little half moon circles of blood, or smashing objects or throwing stuff or whatever? There's a good chance you haven't. Have you ever felt like it, despite the fact that it will help nobody, make your problems worse, and is- in every possible way- an entirely stupid thing to do?
Can you picture being angry- in an extreme, complex situation- enough to be pushed over the edge and actually do something like punch somebody hard in the face, punch a wall or tree and graze or break your fingers, throw a knife at a mirror or act really destructively?

I'm hoping that I'm talking about something that many of you can relate to, even if you never threw things around or screamed or abused people. I still hope that most of you can see how people would go over the top and do these things, despite the fact that they must realise its stupid.

What I'm trying to talk about is something, in some ways, similar to this.

What I'm talking about with cutting yourself definately echos the sentiments I'm trying to bring about above- cutting yourself (or, punching or breaking an inanimate object) something stupid, pointless, and harmful. It benefits neither you nor anybody in any way at all. But I can see how somebody would do it.

Cutting yourself isn't logical, it helps absolutely nobody and nothing, and leaves you worse off- in every single way- than before you went and cut yourself. For the moment, though, it could be a release- of forms- or at least feel like it. The moment when you're no longer choked up by whatever pain or trauma or whatnot, and notice that your wrists really, really hurt is one when the above pain is, in some way, lessened- or, at least, shoved behind the pain of the now glaring problem.

It helps nothing. The harm is still there, and you've got a ton of other worries on your hands as well. IT IS A STUPID THING TO DO. I get that, and hopefully all of you should, too. All I'm saying is that I can understand how people can do it.



On the other hand, cutting yourself to become part of a certain group- which seems to be exactly what Blue Tetris has been talking about, in a manner which implies that it is the ONLY reason people cut themselves- is something that I don't understand, and something thats just another sign of how messed up the world is. Far moreso than people who cut themselves out of sheer desperation to take some of their internal pain away, if only tempoarily.

Okay. You're playing a computer program.
You come to a screen saying "pick A or B". One of them will kill you. You don't know which, and it is impossible to forsee whether it is A or B that will kill you, because you just don't have the information.
Yet, the programmer of this little game knows which one will kill you, because he both programmed it and happens to have a good memory.

#7695 1 2006-03-28T10:23:25Z Teedle
This is a thread for, basically, whatever little bits of helpful trivia you've picked up in your life. Helpful tips to save time, effort, money, or get more enjoyment out of the time you've got on this earth. Little things and whatever wisdom you can disperse, on any aspects of life, that don't belong in any other threads.

I have one or two things to get us started... on

Gardening.
If you're growing spring onion or lettuce (Actually, this rule applies to most salads) don't, no matter what the label says, pull them out root and all.

Wait untill the spring onion is pretty big, and then just cut off some of the multiple branches that are evident at where the plant splits... basically, you'll get the same spring onion as you would otherwise, without killing the plant and preventing it from growing any more.

On lettuce:
Grow it as per usual, and when you harvest it, cut it off at the lowest point to the ground. Worst case scenario? The plant dies anyway, but you get just as much salad. Best case scenario? It grows back entirely, and you get twice as much salad. (Though, I don't know much about the quality of this salad...) Typical, to the best of my knowledge, scenario? It grows back to a certain extent- not enough to give you another meal, but enough to go to seed and, hopefully, give you a lot of salad the next year.

DISCLAIMER!! I dunno why people tell you to pull it out roots and all, but they do, and there may be a good reason for this- so don't blame me if your spring onion or salads spontaneously explode the night after only cutting small sections off.

#7782 1 2006-04-01T01:57:50Z Teedle
Well. This is due to me wanting to have a power trip somewhere other than the Epic, seeing as it's almost finished. (And only 1 year after what we originally were expecting! ) So, here's my newest map collaboration project...

Common Ground.


Map list.[/color]
Halo.


Rules. [/color]
*All maps must have something in common with the last map posted.
*What this common ground is, is entirely up to you- It can be very trivial, if you want it to be.

Common Ground can be...[/color]
*A style of mapmaking
*A genre. (Race, puzzle)
*A feature of a previous map. (Lines through tileset, edited launchpads)
*Using same enemies in similar ways.
*Using similar feeling
*Whatever- there are many, many more options than this- as long as you can explain what the map has in common, and other people can see this, it's all peachy.

Common ground cannot be...[/color]
*Unrelated to map code. (Title/ Description/ ect)
*Impossible to see without being told what it is
*'Inspired' by similar sources. (Such as, a song- see point one.)
*Anything too small.

On the last point, an example of what would be suitable would be "We both use floorguards to result in undeath", and an unsuitable example would be, "Look, we both use floorguards somewhere in the map, even if that's the only common enemy." Mainly, this is all just common sense.

Que...[/color]
I'd prefer not to have one, to keep the maps flowing quickly... you can 'shotgun' a map to work on, but that'll only last for a few hours, rather than a few days. Basically, there's no formal rule that can allow you to keep a map to yourself, more than hoping other people respect your attempts to reserve it for yourself.

Maps...[/color]
I'd like this thread to go in two directions at one, to keep it moving even further- so, let us begin with Halo. From here, we can have two maps using something in common- and then, from those maps, one each. So, what I'm aiming for is a form like this:

(Map) (Map) (Map) (Map) (Halo) (Map) (Map) (Map) (Map)

Thus, letting people choose between two maps to work on, to give this thread some more pace.

So, anyway, let the games begin!

#7818 1 2006-04-02T12:17:31Z Teedle
Gday, guys. I've got something sorta big to announce... But I'd rather waffle on and use as much ado as possible before the relatively straightforward announcement.

The Legacy, my friends, is the team of mods. A team that, as they put it, "became a force to be reckoned with." But what good is that, if there's no force that reckons with them?

So, myself and- well- I'll keep the details small, but I'm part of a rather small group. That calls itself "LA3^3", and the name is something of a hint at the actual members. Anyway- let's just call them... Atramentis.

So, we've put together a team... the idea, at first, was to partially challange and partially pay tribute to the Legacy team. Then, we started moving in different directions with different ideas... there's quite a bit going on, and much of it looks as though it's going to be rather interesting to watch develop.

But... how to introduce the LA3^3 team?

I thought a new column for N sounds like quite a nice idea, sorta to compliment the Legacy set but also with a slight twist that makes it recognisable as an individual project. So I made one. And here it is. 50 levels, about 80% of them never before seen, from yours truly. As in, me.

Some have been posted on NUMA before, but have been slightly modified (and/ or polished) for use in this column. And I am very, very proud of the result... some of my favourite levels made by myself of all time are in this collection.

Each episode runs in classic M&R difficulty, both within itself and in the entire episode set. The difficulty curve is slightly harder (and a bit more... haphazard) than would be idea, but hey- you can't have it all.

And each episode has a theme, which are as follows:
Episode 0: Prolouge
Episode 1: Lines
Episode 2: Towers
Episode 3: Symmetry
Episode 4: Pseudo- Survival
Episode 5: Augie March song titles
Episode 6: Floating objects
Episode 7: Race maps
Episode 8: Trees
Episode 9: Epilouge

Enjoy!

(A note- while this is all my own work, LA3^3 is- indeed- founded, and hopefully going to go places in the not too distant future. Stay tuned...)

I agree entirely with your first choice in the above list, Sweep... thanks for saying that.

Anyway. A list of top 10 (or, 10 random but arranged more or less in ascending order) songs with lyrics I love.

10. My Humanity- Tripod
I really, really wanted to put "Suicide Bomber" by Tripod at the top of my list, but seeing as I've only ever heard it once- live- and it's not on any of their merchandise, I don't know the lyrics well enough.
But, this song will have to do in place of the other. It's a nice, very sarcastic and very, very silly song about love songs.
"Do you know, how hard it was for me, to say these things to you,
To apologise by writing this song for you.
Do you know how much courage it took, to not talk to your face?
...
Do you know, how hard it was for me, to say these things to you,
In a song, so you don't get to answer?
Do you know how much courage it takes, to stand infront of people that love me?
And baby, this song will elevate me, to a godlike status,
and then you will see, the people validate me, 'He's vulnerable, he's sensitive, he's lovely.'
And, from there they go on to talk about their rise to the evil warlords conquering the earth with the mobs of the world behind him... But, somehow, it works.

9. Hallelujah- Rufus Wainwright
(CORRECTION: Original songwriter was Leonard Cohen.)
A brilliant artist (if a little odd when compared to rest of my music collection...), with a lot of great songs. The knowledge that Rufus Wainwright is gay may influence ones opinion of his music (What? That romantic song was written by a HOMOSEXUAL?! is pretty much the reaction I've seen to that information), but- umm- I did have a point...
I think it was something like "This Song Rules", but that got lost somewhere along the way. Oh well.
It goes like this, the 4th, the 5th,
The minor fall, the major lift,
The baffled king, composing Halelujah...

8. Get Over It- OK GO
It's the anti don't you wish your girlfriend was hot like me song... so, what's not to like?
Got a job, got a life, got a four-door and a faithless wife.
Got those nice copper pipes, got an ex, got a room for the night.
Aren't you such a catch? What a prize! Got a body like a battle axe...
Love that perfect frown, honest eyes...
We ought to buy you a Cadillac.

7. Champaigne Supernova- Oasis
Duuuude... the lyrics to this song, are like, so deep, duuuuuuude....
Someday you will find me,
Caught beneath a landslide,
In a champaigne supernova in the sky.

6. End of the world- REM
Complex, twisted lyrics about, well, The End Of The World As We Know It spewed out at a ridiculous pace. Not really all that profound or anything like that... but I like it anyway, so it may as well go on this list.
Six o'clock - TV hour. Don't get caught in foreign tower. Slash and burn,
return, listen to yourself churn. Lock him in uniform and book burning,
blood letting. Every motive escalate. Automotive incinerate. Light a candle,
light a motive. Step down, step down. Watch a heel crush, crush. Uh oh,
this means no fear - cavalier. Renegade and steer clear! A tournament,
a tournament, a tournament of lies. Offer me solutions, offer me alternatives,
and I decline.

5. Beg Your Pardon- Josh Pyke
A touching australian folk/ blues artist, this is a... truly touching song about unrequited love and reactions to it, regret, and all that merry stuff! Sometimes a bit simplistic, but rather touchingly so.
But oh no, around you I forget behaviour,
but if I begged your pardon, might I once again be in your favour?
I know that I'm not the one of whom you think at night, but I know I,
Presume to think I made you think of me right now.

4. American Pie- Don McLean
What can I say... an old song, but a very, very good one. And my pride in knowing the lyrics of this song by heart tops even my pride of being able to recite "One Crowded Hour" to anybody who'll stand still long enough.
And in the streets: the children screamed,
The lovers cried, and the poets dreamed.
But not a word was spoken;
The church bells all were broken.
And the three men I admire most:
The father, son, and the holy ghost,
They caught the last train for the coast
The day the music died.

3. Heartbeat and Sails- Augie March
Not only probably my favourite love ballad of all time, but with lyrics that are Augie March at their very best, showing off what is quite possibly nothing more than skill with a theasaraus... heck, I love it anyway.
Scoop my brains and let my heart have action, in its thousand million lots.
In the dumb city dawn we dispense with the forlorn beasts that we were in the night, grown lean on love.
A love which will pierce and callous and tumesce,
O upon the birth oath the morbid bloom
Is a child's sense of impending doom
in a womb that is ambushed.

2. Brain Damage- Pink Floyd
What can I say? Perfection in music and song writing... I can't picture a better tribute to the member this song was written about.
The lunatic is in my head
You raise the blade, you make the change
You re-arrange me till Im sane
You lock the door
And throw away the key
Theres someone in my head but its not me.

And if the cloud bursts, thunder in your ear
You shout and no one seems to hear
And if the band youre in starts playing different tunes
Ill see you on the dark side of the moon


1. Magic Hours- Explosions in the Sky
Sometimes less is so much more.

It was over sentimental, badly made, and an absolute hack job of a movie. I strongly disliked it- partially because the 'true story' was anything but, partially because there were so many film making cliche's in it, and partially because it evokes sympathy towards the aboriginals based on 'true' events that never happened.

I could go along pointing out the inconsistancies in the film, stupidities, innapropriate slow motion moments, bad acting, examples of shoddy plot and huge historical inaccuracies (riding to the Moore River Settlement on a train line that would not be operational for quite a few years), but it doesn't really relate to this discussion. At all.

Make it enough to say that the only reason I've viewed the film was due to us studying it in literiture, from a teacher so left wing she's swung around the other side and become far right. A teacher who's so much of a tool you could assemble furniture with her. A teacher with the mental capacity of an ant. (A teacher who gives me bad marks, too... *The term 'cycles' in the following sentance: 'The novel cycles through the viewpoints of the various characters'
*The term 'bad parrenting', with the comment: 'Don't use the word 'bad', use a theasaurus and find another word for it.)

Oh, man, is this winding off topic.

So, in this film, near the beggining, when the aboriginal woman's daughters are dragged away, kicking and screaming, into a car that will bring them to the prison- like Moore River settlement, she struggles desperately to keep them there. When she fails and they're driving off and she knows she can't reach them, she falls to her knees and bangs her head with a rock repeatedly.

Apparantly, this is an aboriginal thing supposedly helping show the viewers of the film the grief the mother is going through, and that she's trying to make the pain of the immediate loss of her daughters hurt less by, you know, bashing herself on the head with a rock.

Which is a neat little parrallel between modern emo culture and aboriginal society in badly made films...
The main difference being that, in the former,
*There's more 'incentive' to hurt yourself, based on the emo subculture and the messages and morals it supposedly stands for.
*We are not encouraged, unless we are ourselves 'emo', to feel any real pity for the 'idiots' cutting themselves.

Whereas, in the film, there's two major differences. For one thing, there's no horde of people around the woman subtly encouraging her to bash herself on a head, and we're supposed to feel a huge amount of sympathy for her as she inflicts the pain upon herself.

And there are very few people who watch the film and go, "That woman is an absolute COCKBURGER, why is she hurting herself, it's not going to MAKE ANY DIFFERENCE TO THE SITUATION, the idiot." They sit there and are immensly saddened, feel a huge amount of sympathy for the aboriginals, maybe cry at the end of the movie, leave the theatre feeling very moved and ashamed of the sins of one A.O. Neville (The injustice of that last part is astounding) and, possibly, in later life become crap literiture teachers, and refuse to ever read anything by Keith Windschuttle.

I'm working on a theory involving the first e-mail being something to help us read the rest/ portions of his other e-mails. A code for working out which letters and/or words are signficant.

490 495 489 493 495 489 490 495 489 491 495 489 489 494 498 497 495 489
49195 489 491 495 489 489 495 489
Here we are... 49195 clearly breaks the pattern of the rest of the segment I copied. The significance of this, however, is beyond me... Also notice how certain numbers come up often and others don't?

What *does* seem significant, though, is the way that the majority of the document seems to be divided into these 3 digit numbers beggining with four. The above selection is from relatively early in the text, however even in the bottom line...
495 495 489 491 495 489 490 495 489 489 495 489 491 495 489 492 495 489 489 495 489 490 495 489 494 495 489 494 451
And here, again, certain numbers seem to be repeated often; and all seem to have been chosen from within a rather limited range. '451' seems to be the only number hugely out of the ordinary in the last line of numbers...

Maybe the code lies in the numbers that are 'out of the ordinary'... maybe it lies in the common, oft- used numbers. I'm not really sure.

491 495 495 489 495 495 490 495 495 495 494 497 491 495
