487 473 473 473 451 451 495 491 491 495 494 490 495 496 490 494 498 493 494 497

For my dark lady...

One gentlemen from Italy stepped aboard a ship, bound somewhere that was- in fact- a lot simpler to get to by simply travelling across the land, rather than travelling about twice the distance over land merely to get to the sea, and to take a boat from there. But it didn't really matter... Boats were pleasent, and he could have enough time to mull over the events of the last few days in his mind on the peaceful voyage.

Walking upon the deck of The Collosus, he had to say that he was quite impressed- it was a classy ship, and a huge one. The Collosus. Totally unsinkable, or so they said. It sounded like a bit of a challange, but oh well... let the worst happen. If he were to die, so be it- for what is life without love, and what is love when it lies with a maiden of whom you have only memories and a single ring?

And with a heavy heart, he went off to try to find his bunk.

* * *

As I walked onto the deck of The Collosus, I almost gave an ejaculation of surprise upon finding out just how large the deck was.

My longtime friend and companion behind me in his famous lodgings on the street that often smell ever so slightly of bread, I was off on an adventure of my own... yet I missed his company, for all of his faults. Even his cocaine addiction was a small price to pay to be constantly in the company of his brilliance.

And here I was, a humble doctor, travelling alone on such a large boat, bound for exotic locations currently unknown to even myself. This would, I thought to myself as the boat began to move, be a voyage to remember.

Little did I know just how correct that thought would prove to be.

* * *

And thus begins the epic voyage of The Collosus, and a journey which will end in thousands of small allusions to- well- stuff, many riddles and many tasks. A journey in which many, many members will perish and some will- hopefully- survive.

So, it's time to introduce the people whom shall soon, for the most part, quite likely be corpses. Each member of the forum is granted two characters, who may be whoever they like, within reason... No superheroes or special qualities, please! Allusions to people in plays, movies, or books are a plus.

Enjoy! This should be good, once it gets going. We'll have a few days of voyage in which people can introduce eachother, and then we'll get into the whole riddle related thing. I hope this works. The plans are still hugely incomplete, but I've got quite a bit to work from, and this should be fun.

Quote: Wikipedia
In the fiction of J. R. R. Tolkien, the White Council, or Council of the Wise, was a group of Elves and Wizards of Middle-earth, formed in 2463 TA. to contest the growing power of Dol Guldur at the request of Galadriel. It was officially the Second White Council, a successor of that of the Second Age.

The White Council's head was the Wizard Saruman the White, (although Galadriel wished for Gandalf the Grey to be made the leader). Other members of the Council included the Bearers of the Three Rings of the Elves (although this was not known to any save the Bearers) Gandalf the Grey, Galadriel, and Elrond Half-Elven. Crdan the Shipwright (who had borne Narya, the ring of Fire before handing it on to Gandalf), and Radagast the Brown. It is also confirmed that Alatar the Blue and Pallando the Blue were members of the white council.

The White Council first met in 2463 TA, at the end of the Watchful Peace. In 2851 TA. the White Council met to decide on whether to act on Gandalf's discovery of the identity of the Necromancer but Saruman disuaded the others. During this meeting there was much tension between Saruman and Gandalf, for Gandalf already suspected Saruman of desiring to have the Ring. When he realised that the One Ring was possibly still in the area of the Gladden Fields and Sauron was actively seeking it Saruman relented and in 2941 TA. Sauron was driven out of Dol Guldur only to re-appear in Mordor. The Council last met in 2953 TA., at this meeting Saruman insists that the One Ring has been swept out to sea.

Less known is the First White Council, in which most of the same members participated as in the Second. It was formed after Sauron's defeat in Eriador in 1701 SA. It's main decision where that Eregion was to be abandonned in favour of Imladris.

#8337 1 2006-04-29T04:57:48Z Teedle
3 WORDS OR LESS
Being a competition of inspiration; relations; things

Dedicated to cheesegod for not being annoyed at how identical this is to his thread.

Feedback on quality of competition appreciated.

How To Win
(or, Judge, Jury, and Excecutioner)

The aim of this game is to win. This can be done by making the best map. The person who judges which the best map is, is the person who has last made the map picked to be the best map by the previous judge.

Winning is good, because it always you both a fuzzy feeling of superiority, and makes you a judge yourself. Which is good, because it always you to endow others with warm fuzzy feelings of superiority, gives you a powertrip, and always opens up the opportunity of being bribed by competitors.

The Judge
(or, The Boney King of Nowhere)

Upon having won, you are now a judge for the next round. The first thing that you must do is set down the theme for the next series of maps, using a maximum of three words.
The more obscure and open to interpretation your theme is, the better. Your words should serve more as a source of inspiration than a set of guidelines for the next map.

Acceptable- but not hugely wonderful- examples are, for instance,
Floating Islands
Flowy race maps
Chaingun drones

The sorts of examples that fill me with giddy joy are ones such as
Professor Moriarty
Radiohead
Genre: Horror

After this, you simply pick your favourite map and bestow unto them your previous position. From this point, feel free to re- enter the competition.

Round Commencement
(or, Your Time Is Up)

Each round lasts untill the judge has picked a map- and, thus, the next judge. After this point, no new maps can be made untill the new judge posts with the next topic.

A judge cannot pick a map untill either
  • 5 maps have been entered into the competition
  • 5 days have passed since the round has begun
However, maps may continue to be submitted after these criteria have been fulfilled- up untill the point that a winner has been picked.

Rules for Entry
(or, No No No No No No No No)

The rules are very basic.
Your map must relate, in some way, to the topic given. If the way in which it relates is trivial (for instance, a boss map of a large squid for the topic of "Professor Moriarty") you must provide a description of exactly how it relates (for instance, "Professor Moriarty is the arch nemesis of Sherlock Holmes, on whom the books are based. This squid thing is the arch nemesis of N, on whom the game is based.)
Your map must be submitted to NUMA.
Your map must be a playable map- Action, Puzzle, or Race.
For obvious reasons, you cannot submit a map when you are a judge.

And that's it.

A Wolf at the Door.
(or, It Girl. Rag Doll.)

* * * Round One * * *

I will be judging this round, because I'm just that cool.

The first topic is "STARRY, STARRY NIGHTS."

A few suggestions...
You don't need to do the obvious map things here- you could research the song and do something based on the title of another song by the artist, or you could do something that resembles a painting or the artistic style of the person whom the song is about. Or you could do something to do with space, or something Star Wars themed.

.yojnE

Genetically engineering crops and plants is something I'm rather... squemish about...

See, I guess I'm (somewhat illogically and unreasonably) against the idea of it and of playing God with these things, (partially because, in my limited experiance, they tend to taste like faintly tainted water) BUT- we're talking about making more food. We don't have enough food. (Or, rather, food isn't spread out enough but we're NEVER gonna start changing our policies to start sending money to countries that need it more.) People are dying of starvation. More food, more easily grown, can't be anything but a good thing- especially in countries that don't have enough to go around.

In short- I don't like the idea of genetically modified food much, but it could potentially do a ridiculous amount of good in the world- by far enough to convince me that it's definately a good idea and worthwhile field to research.

Genetically engineering humans, however, is something I strongly disagree with. If, for no other reasons, because of the 'results' of early, failed experiments before the technique is perfected. And, even beyond then, I really don't think these are things that should be meddled with, at all. I can truly imagine a Gattaca- esque society developing were we to begin genetically modifying and creating people.

I'm definately pro- abortion.

Holy Jesus on a Stick do I hate Norton.

I updated the version in the vague hope that this new one may be either...
a: Better
b: Hog less system resources

The new, 2006 version is
a: Flashier, shiner, and more obtrusive (it has a demented tab on your bottom bar that fits in with exactly NO color schemes and just generally looks unnescessarily retarded- also- what, exactly, is wrong with the task bar?)
b: CONSTANTLY updating things without telling you that it's doing so- which is fine, except that it seems to take priority over pretty much everything else I'm doing on the internet, slowing it down to the speed of a retarded donkey. What's more, I'm yet to figure out how to tell when it's doing this, and I'll never know what's causing it to not so much 'run slowly' as 'vagualy hobble', and I get paranoid about hackers, viruses, spyware and the like.
c: The most system resource hogging version yet, with plenty of things running in the background that the task manager doesn't allow you to disable, even when you disconnect from the internet. (Which I tend to do when I run complex games like The Sims 2.)
d: Unnescessarily 'in your face'. For example, every time you turn on the computer, it will run a check to make sure all components are running properly. Swell- I can see this as worthwhile, even if it does jack up the load time of your computer a lot. But then, when it detects that everything is working as planned, a huge, distracting, ugly box pops out of the bottom right corner of the screen, taking up about 1/10 of the visible space on your monitor, seemingly allerting you- urgently- that "everything is allright."
Why, oh WHY did it not occur to these people that maybe you should only allert people when things AREN'T working, and NOT have to constantly tell them that 'everything is fine, everything is fine, everything is _still_ fine..."?

On top of which, the automatically starting a full system scan once a week thing is very, very, VERY annoying. ESPECIALLY when you're using full screen applications, and it causes the computer to stumble, pause, freeze, unfreeze, half crash, and then half an hour later come up with Norton's nice, friendly window stating that it's scanned 3 files in the 1/2 hour it took to compete with whatever applications you're running.

Yeah. Norton irritates me. Although I can see that it is, probably, in actuality a very good program.


I mean, in my opinion Norton does a good job. (Even if things such as spybot are far better for spyware, which they specialise in.) But I _hate_ how it's getting more and more obtrusive, system resource hoggy, and in your face. It's bloated by it's own sense of self importance, and I don't like this much at all.

The country music marathon that had been running on every single Rockville FM station 24 hours a day since 1978 was still in full swing, so I alternated between an AM station that was filtering some staticky Spanish-language thing and a local right-wing talk radio program.

"...I'm here to tell ya, immigration, it's like rats on a ship. America is the ship and allllll these rats are comin' on board, y'all. And you know what happens when a ship gets too many rats on board? It sinks. That's what."

#8662 1 2006-05-13T13:41:18Z Teedle
Quote: Neil Gaiman in American Gods
There are stories that are true, in which each individual's tale is unique and tragic, and the worst of the tragedy is that we have heard it before, and we cannot allow ourselves to feel it too deeply... if it were to touch us it would cripple us or make saints of us; but, for the most part, it does not touch us. We cannot allow it to.
Tonight, as you eat, reflect if you can: there are children starving in the world, starving in numbers larger than the mind can easily hold, up in the big numbers where an error of a million here, a million there, can be forgiven. It may be uncomfortable for you to reflect upon this or it may not, but still, you will eat.
There are accounts which, if we open our hearts to them will cut us too deeply. Look- here is a good man, good by his own lights and the lights of his friends: he is faithful and true to his wife, he adores and lavishes attention on his little children, he cares about his country, he does his job punctiliously, as best he can. So, efficiently and good- naturedly, he exterminates Jews: he appreciates the music that plays in the background to pacify them: he advises the Jews not to forget their identification numbers as they go into the showers - many people, he tells them, forget their numbers, and they take the wrong clothes, when they come out of the howers. This calms the Jews: there will be life, they assure themselves, after the showers. And they are wrong. Our man supervises the detail taking the bodies to the ovens; and if there is anything he feels bad about, it is that he still allows the gassing of vermin to affect him. Were he a truly good man, he knows, he would feel nothing but joy, as the earth is cleansed of its pests.
Leave him; he cuts too deep. He is too close to us and it hurts.
...We need individual stories. Without individuals we see only numbers: a thousand dead, a hundred thousand dead, 'casuaties may rise to a million'. With individual stories, the statistics become people - but even that is a lie, for the people continue to suffer in numbers that themselves are numbing and meaningless. Look, see the child's swollen, swollen belly, and the flies that crawl at the corners of his eyes, his skeletal limbs: will it make it easier for you to know his name, his age, his dreams, his fears? To see him from the inside? And if it does, are we not doing a disservice to his sister, who lies in the searing dust beside hinm, a distorted, distended caricature of a human child. And there, if we feel for them, are they now more important to us than a thousand other children touched by the same famine, a thousand other young lives who will soon be food for the flies' own myriad squirming children?
We draw our lines around these moments of pain, and... they are covered with a smooth, safe, nacreous layer to let them slip, pearl-like, from our souls without real pain.

Wikipedia- Developments in 4th millennium BC

Wikipedia- 5th millennium BC

Notable occurrences in this millennium include the introduction of the plough in Europe, the development of the wheel in Europe and- more importantly- the invention of Beer.

6th Millennium BC

Here we have the development of agriculture, the 'first' invention of the wheel, and the creation of the first wine and bricks in Persia.

And, here, objects begin to be made not only for function, but also aesthetic value.

7th Millenium BC

Inventions, discoveries, introductions

* Circa 6000 BC Wall painting/map from atalhyk, an early-civilized city that prospered by trading obsidian, Anatolia -- modern Turkey.
* Agriculture appears around the Mediterranean (Greece, Italy), see Old European Culture.
* Beekeeping is first recorded. Rock paintings on cave walls in Africa and eastern Spain show people gathering honey from trees or rock crevices while bees fly around them - cave drawings in Spain, near Valencia.
* Pastoralism and cultivation of cereals (East Sahara).
* First pottery in Mesopotamia.
* Gold and native copper begin to be used.
* Domestication of the cow in the Middle East.
* Archaic pottery making, burial mound construction, and garden technology (North America).
* Indigenous Peoples of the Americas begin using stone to grind food and to hunt American Bison and smaller animals (North America).
* Deciduous plants make their appearance on Long Island (North America).
* Northern Atlantic Ocean is cooled by 3-6C due to collapsing ice dams releasing enormous floods (North America).
* Better toolkits in use by 6000BC. North America

* Mexico - Incipient agriculture begins (North America)
* Peru, Guitarrero Cave, plant fibers are twisted, knotted, and looped into baskets, mats (South America).
* City: Asia - 6, 000 BC: Village of Ban Po in China.
* City: 6,000 BC: Jericho.
* Eastern Mediterranean - Forms of pottery become decoration .
* Animal figures of Estuarine-period rock painting in Australia include saltwater fish and crocodiles Australia.

#8836 1 2006-05-20T04:31:01Z Teedle
Allright, this isn't a poll, because I want reasons and opinions and stuff more than plain yes/ no answers.

So, here's the thing.

I want to leave NUMA.

Now, I don't want to stop making maps entirely, allright? I'll continue to make them, but submitting them to NUMA holds little appeal to me anymore.

The reasons run thusly-

1. Sniping.
Sweet corpsified lord am I sick of seeing my maps go down from 5 to 3.5 in one swell vote, and drop down the ladder when they're bombarded by people who think that the maps deserve less than a 4.5, and thus figure the best way to ensure this happens is to give them a 0. I hate sniping with a passion.

In fact, Sniping has meant that this map (underground meteor, back from when I was new) is my second highest rated one in my collection (under improbability drive, which has too many ratings for sniping to really work), purely because it hasn't attracted the same attention that the rest of my highly rated maps get, mainly because it's such an old map before the days when I made some of the really good ones I have today.

Okay, you may say 'Ratings don't matter, just ignore them", but they DO. It was what drove me to try to improve myself on NUMA, and what made me addicted to the place- the competitive spirit, the creation of something from nothing and seeing how well your creation does, the sense of accomplishment when you spend a lot of time on a map and it gets a 4.5/5.

To me, ratings mean a lot. I know it's sort of stupid, but it's the way I feel. And it became the only real reason I continued making maps after my first one, 'towerful'. And ratings are screwed around with so much on NUMA at the moment, that they've become nothing but an endless source of frustration.

2. Maps that recieve low ratings.
From time to time I'll just create a nice, little, quirky level that I'm quite fond of, that isn't exactly brilliant but it sort of nice on a small scale.
I love levels like these. People on NUMA don't.

If a map isn't big, awesome, or outstanding in any way- if it is just a solid example of enjoyable gameplay- I find it tends to get a low rating and a whole lot of people abusing people who think that it's good.

There seems to be something sinful about giving people a high rating for a map that's merely enjoyable, and this annoys me to no end. I mean, sure, I could just ignore the ratings and submit it anyway (and, were I a better man, I probably would) but somehow, I tend to not like the idea of compromising my overall reputation and author ranking by making these maps.

I know this is flawed and dumb, but this is how I tend to treat submitting maps to NUMA, despite my better judgement.

3. Making episodes, levelpacks, and stuff is more fun.
And you know why? In making episodes, you can do far more than you can using NUMA for the same sort of system. You can make things far more complex and involved.
Also, I *love* playing around with difficulties both within episodes and within total columns, tweaking them untill I think they're just right. Whereas, on NUMA, difficulty is often
-Hard to justify
-Complained about (which doesn't happen when it's 'taken in context')
-Ignored entirely and totally insignificant

Also, in levelpacks, nice little quirky maps have their place. As do easy maps. And maps that aren't made on a huge scale, but made simply because they're sorta enjoyable, if not totally groundbreaking. And these sorts of maps- taken in context- tend to make a lot more sense and seem a lot more fitting.

Why I don't want to compromise.

Because, were I to do this, it'd feel slightly cheap having all of my best (or all of my NUMA maps in general) in the levelpacks, except padded out with 'filler' that wouldn't do well on NUMA. No, I think I'd prefer to move entirely to one or t'other.

The case for NUMA.

Here's my problem. Using my LA3^3 levelpack as an example, I can say for certain that less people played the maps as would have were they to have been submitted to NUMA individually. And very few people could be bothered playing them all, preffering to take their maps in small, individual doses from NUMA than in large doses in levelpacks.

To some extent, I feel the same way in relation to map packs and NUMA.

NUMA is simply... easier and more accessable, whereas map packs are a daunting task to start getting into. They're also a huge daunting task to make, and it's something of a letdown when almost nobody plays them.

So... have you any thoughts, opinions, or advice on any of this?

EDIT: Now with 4 less typos!

Allright, fine, the first post could probably have been narrowed down to two a lot less longwinded points.

1. NUMA irritates me, mainly because of the competetive spirit I can't help myself 'playing' it with. I treat it like I treat the game itself- something to be 'beaten', something to 'win', something to do the best I can at.

Which is stupid, because that shouldn't be what NUMA and making (and sharing) maps is about, but it's how I treat it nonetheless. I get dissapointed when maps are sniped, I'm thrilled whenever a map gets a lot of good comments and ratings, and I just generally feel a sense of accomplishment after having made what I believe is a good map.

When I get maps with low ratings and no comments (save the odd trivial one like "this is not a food"), I feel dissapointed, especially if I quite liked the level. Evidently people didn't like it, and I've just recieved a low score on a game. I'm now amoungst the lower segement of the players- like playing soldat and seeing your lonely name at the bottom of the screen.

Add to this sniping and unfair representations of ratings (and, also, very little 'middle ground' in ratings as you've described in your post above), basically, NUMA irritates me.

Allright, this is stupid, but it's how I feel.

But it's not a reason to leave a perfectly good place like NUMA. Not at all. This is merely establishing the grounds that I'm not enjoying NUMA as much as I once was.

2. I had a lot more fun creating- and felt a much larger sense of satisfaction after finishing creating- the la3^3 levelpack than I do making maps for NUMA.

I like themed episodes. I like non themed episodes. I like tweaking difficulty, and the grand scale projects. I enjoyed making the la3^3 levelpack a lot. A ridiculously huge amount, considering that all I was doing is- you know- the exact same thing I do for NUMA. Make maps.

I'm saying, basically, that I prefer making levelpacks over making maps for NUMA. Much like, you know, (I think) members of the Legacy team have said they did. (I seem to remember Kablizzy saying as much.)

You've got to assume that the rooster lays an egg for the question to work, as in much of my maths methods course so far. I've had a SAC involving quadratic paths of toast launched by a beagle to feed his friends in a dog shelter so that they'll play better at their football match in a weeks time (TRUE- I'll scan it for you if you want, it was the best SAC ever ) , and I'm fairly sure that if I were to say "But dogs don't launch toast out of toasters, nor do they hang wet toast to dry on washing lines that follow the line of a quadratic graph with clearly defined domain and range!" I would have failed the SAC entirely, thus lowering my marks for both the year and pheaseably having an effect on my TER score next year.

So, when you are given a question like that, I think it's a much better idea to assume that it _can_ happen, rather than saying "This doesn't happen in real life! Waaaa! The question is worthless!!!!" and throwing away a large number of marks.

So, I recently caught up with an old friend on mine. A friend who, whilst we were playing gamecube, casually remarked to me that one could unlock gigabowser if he beat even match 51 with bowser himself.

He also remarked something about beating the left masterhand in less than 1.5 minutes and earning him as a secret character, but I've finished the whole two hand thing in less than 50 seconds using almost solely gannondorf's up + a smash move, so that's rubbish.

(Although, one _can_ fight the left master hand if one removes 150% damage on the right masterhand, on difficulty normal, in the normal game mode. (Classic.) However, while I've never done this without looseing a life, I'm fairly sure it's not meant to unlock any other characters, since it _does_ give you about an 80,000 point bonus.)

Okay. Anyway. So, I see this as a promising sign that maybe, just maybe, giga bowser could be unlocked...
He's a different character to the normal bowser. Most of his moves are the same (but not all), he looks _similar_ (but not entirely the same, especially around the head) and this is all rather remiscent of many, many 'unlockable' pairs in the game- link/ young link, marth/ roy, mario/ doctor mario, ect.

The differences arise in, say, giga bowsers down + a move resulting in a small ice flurry totally unlike bowsers (which freezes characters), and his smash moves setting the characters on fire, which is utterly unlike bowser.

So, I say that the concept that he could be unlocked in this method is not entirely ludicrous, especially since my game has room for exactly two more characters on the table. (On either side of the bottom row.) And so I set to trying to defeat event match 51 with bowser.

Problem is, I can't do it. I can beat giga boswer himself, about 1/4 of the time, by using plenty of fire breathing and up + b on him, followed by down + b-ing him once he gets over 130% damage. Occasionally he'll try to stomp me over the side and commit suicide, and that'll help, too.

No, he's not the problem. Gannondorf + Mewtwo are. Try as I might, I can't defeat them- I'll always just get chucked off the stage, and it's rare that I face them when I have more than one life. (And when I do, I get sorely owned anyway.)

So, this thread- for all of you super smash bros. fans- is twofold...

#1- Any advice on beating mewtwo + gannondorf with bowser?
#2- Come help me prove/ disprove giga bowser as an unlockable character!

And if he can't be unlocked this way, well then, Nintendo are just evil to create an entirely new character that plays exactly like normal ones, but can't be played from the players perspective.

(My one problem with this theory is that All Star mode- fighting all of the characters in the game, once unlocked- would be obsolete if you could unlock any more characters. But there's always a chance, right?)

Oh yeah- and, I've beaten all- star mode on normal. Contrary to what some cheat websites say, this achieves nada. So boo to them.

#183406 32 2006-06-02T06:41:03Z Teedle
Quote: Cerberus, May 28, 2006 11:12 am
Quote: Trogdor007, May 27, 2006 10:40 pm
Shaun of the Dead.  Scariest movie of all time.
What the heck, wasn't that a horror comedy?

For those unlightened people who have not watched the DVD special features because they were very, very bored...

Yup, Shaun of the Dead _is_ a horror comedy, (or, as the box says, "A romantic comedy. With zombies."), but the two genres are merged- it doesn't make fun of horror or send it up, it merely aims to create a comedy taking place in a horror environment.

And much of the film- most of the second half- is pretty centred around the horror aspect of the film even moreso than the first. Many of the (in my opinion) funniest scenes in the film were cut out of the second half because the makers felt that it interrupted the flow and progression of the plot around that stage, where 'jokes' as such were no longer as appropriate.

Anyway, on the commentaries, the film makers specifically said that they didn't want to make fun of horror films (totally unlike, say, the Scary Movie series)- they just wanted to make a comedy that took place in a horror environment respectful to those that made the genre. So, "horror comedy" doesn't mean it's not scary.

It _does_ get pretty tense towards the end- lots of people dying, including many that you start off sure will live in the early, much lighter sections of the film. I can picture it being considered quite frightening, even if I've seen far worse. (Although the mixture of comedy and then brutal death- the flicking between genres- is often more shocking and entertaining than the straight genres themselves are, at least when pulled off correctly- and a good deal of my respect for Joss Whedon comes from how well he can do this. Take, for instance, the death of Wash in Serenity- one of the best deaths I've ever seen on screen.)

#9444 1 2006-06-13T09:45:24Z Teedle
****. Just, ****

Man, I dont know what to do. ****, oh ****... OH ****ING HELL!!!

Ummm Crap, I dont know how the hell Im supposed to say this. ****, I dont have a ****ing clue. Theres got to be a way to say this properly, but I dont know it. Hell, I didnt ever think that Id ever be signing on to an internet forum to tell its members that one of their most loved members has died.

Im sure you all know Atramentis, or his internet persona, anyway. Brilliant mapmaker, was the top for quite some time, you know the guy? He goes to same school as me, but is in his final year whilst Im still in year 11. We met properly, believe it or not, while playing N He came over, said something like Wow, youre playing N! and then we started talking about stuff like, Have you heard of NUMA?! and so we started talking.

Since then, we got to know eachother quite well He was in the year above me, but we were quite good friends. Wed joke around and stuff, and were trying to arrange a student harvest as his year 12 leaving prank, where wed have this table on the oval, and nothing else, and

No. Enough of that.

I was at school when I got the news. Not the news of his death. He was in intensive care at the time. I was joking around with some of the year 12s he used to hang around with, and there werent a ton of them there, and I asked Wheres Jared? and one of them said in intensive care. You know. I treated it like a ****ing joke, laughed, and asked where he was again. I must have looked like such a ****ing arsehole, ****ing around laughing when there friend was in hospital after getting hit by a car right near his home.

The car driver wasnt even drunk. Or using a mobile phone or anything. There was nothing wrong with her, it wasnt a hit and run or anything, they just ran over who you know as Atramentis on the driveway of a sub divided block. Or maybe there was something mentally wrong with her, I think I heard something of the type mentioned, but screw it, I dont really care about the person who killed Jarred. It couldve been anyone who did the killing, but its the death that screwed me over.

He was wearing headphones on high volume, and thatd be the lesson of the death, insofar as there is one, dont wear headphones in traffic, but it wasnt in traffic and it there isnt a lesson to be learnt here, just a bloody pointless waste of life.

And, again, I dont bloody know how to say this, but hes dead. He was in intensive care for, I think, 18 hours or so. He died with his family at his side, but hell, what difference does that make? Hes still dead. He still died. In a charmless hospital room with machines pumping stuff in and out of him

Hell. What do I know of that? I wasnt there. I didnt see it. And Im sort of grateful for that. I dont want to have the memory of a last rattled breath, or of the slight, almost undetectable switch from tortured living to the nothingness of death no, who needs the memories of such things? The imagination of it is bad enough.

I only recently heard that hes dead. Full on dead. Not lying down someplace slowly recovering, to emerge not unchanged but ALIVE, damnit, and still the same person in some deep down place And thats that. A brilliant man lost to the world from

Oh, damnit, I sound like Im delivering a Eulogy or something. Plenty of time for that later, when a real one does get delivered over what used to be Jarred. Probably delivered by a priest or something, who never knew of his convoluted, partially atheist but GOOD views on religion. I prayed for him, can you imagine that? I dont even have a clue if he wouldve wanted me to or not, but I did all the same, and I never wouldve thought it

Crap. I really dont know what to do, what to say, what to write, what to tell my family when at long last they come home (though they never even met him, and only supplied transport to his house grudgingly when they had nothing better to do), and well, here I am. On the frigging internet, telling a frigging bunch of zit- covered prepubescents about the death of someone they know nothing about, somebody who theyll never feel the actual zest of loss for anymore than they would somebody like Brickman who just, one day, disappears. Hell, to you, he could still be alive someplace and well for all you know, and so it wont be real.

I only wish I had that.

So yeah, thats it. He died, I didnt even hear about it until it was almost over, and now hes being shoved into the ground like so much garbage in an expensive case in just a few days time. No, if you live nearby, youre frigging not allowed to drop in and pay your respects during the service like some sort of retarded, messed up gatecrasher.

And here I am, going to watch my third generic, fill-the-blanks eulogy from some uninspired priest, and see my third body swallowed by the earth, and wish it wasnt so. Violently, violently wish it wasnt so.

The world has just experienced a great loss. Just another great loss, and they happen all the time, but this shouldnt have been. Im sorry.

And thats it. Im done.

Bye.



[ I know this is a very strong subject, but it is still public news and so I have censored out some language. Strong condolences for our friend. ]

#192975 30 2006-06-22T15:07:12Z Teedle
I hate to say it, but I sorta disagree with Sweep and much of the mainstream opinions he's evoked.

Why? Here's what he is saying- "People comment, affecting the way people vote. Bad comments = bad votes. Pick + select your comments, and you'll be able to help your map's ranking." Well. Umm. So?

It won't be any more unfair in benefiting your map than a bad comment is unfair in hindering it. It might alter people's interpretations of THE SAME MAP, but so what? If you can make a map look better by editing comments- and if everybody is aware of the ease with which this is done- then people will know that the comments create a certain amount of bias, and that the comments posted might not always be representative of what the mainstream thinks. Therefore, people will be more likely to vote based on their perception of the quality of a map, rather than on the perceptions of other people.



... having said that, I don't like the idea of my criticism getting deleted and, as such, ignored- especially if they try to be helpful, constructive criticism. It might take away some of the motivation to improve, if you can just ignore, control and 'delete' part of what suggests you could. (By which I mean comments.)

Furthermore, while this might have some positive effects- as outlined above- it seems a rather stupid thing to do just because of the possible way people might react based on how I described. I sorta like the idea, and sorta agree with sweep, and sorta think that criticism should be respected enough so that it can't be idly deleted- so, I guess I'm against the idea. I just thought that this might be an interesting angle.

I don't know. I won't say small, or small minded, but often so concerned with these little unnescessary grudges and miniture fights we really don't need and would be better off without.

There's been quite a bit of laughter, lately. A lot of hanging around with friends, planning stuff (preperation for next year's Pre- Or- Post Exposure Prophylaxis Day is already underway, and it will be a day to remember. This is amoungst many other, more local projects) and, finally, it looks as though I might be in a band that'll end up halfway serious. One Way Jesus, it's called. It has around 6 members.

My mapmaking has been... very haphazard. I have a lot archived, saved for. Well, I guess I shouldn't give it away.

And, I'm here again. Well, sorta. I'm not sure, really, but I guess... I'm potentially here, if you ever need to contact me. I haven't exactly left. I guess I don't really see much of a need of you guys in my life, no hole that you'll fill or... something like that. But I am here, and if you ever need me, I will never hesistate to reply to a PM or e-mail or offer my opinions wherever they're wanted. I don't want to selfishly leave. I want to do the right thing.

I've been listening to more music than ever, and have memorised more lyrics than I ever thought was possible. I have about 15gig on the computer, about half of which comes from actual CDs. I've been painting, too... some slightly surreal, impressionist stuff. It's quite bad, but I do kinda like it.

School has... been a huge mixture of ups and downs. Grades and sometimes going up, sometimes down. Some are higher than they've ever been, others- like Lit and German- have plummeted. Lately I've come very close to yelling at my Lit teacher, and storming out of the classroom, on more than one occasion. And she hit me, once, in class. Only on the hand, but it's still wrong.

I've started keeping a journal, too. Leatherbound, written with a fountain pen. It's... odd, what it contains, when you read over it. Overtures of lightheartedness and frivolity and... nothing substantial or groundbreaking underneath. No archived secrets. Just some records, some observations, some comedy, and some meditations on not much at all.

There's laughter. There's music. Lovers never having kissed, and empty space yet still unseen. Writing, dancing, singing, living, debating, playing, walking... There's life.

And I guess that's sort of what I want to say. I love you all, but I guess I've allready told you that. I'm here, and if you ever want to talk, I'm more than glad to listen.

#10340 1 2006-07-30T02:21:12Z Teedle
So here I am again, mainly because it sees a lot more fun than picking my university courses. I don't have a clue what I'm going to do. I feel like I should have more than vague sorts of feeligns about the courses- some sort of clarity when it comes to picking what could ultimately decide my courier path, rather than going purely by guesswork and hope.

Anyway. I realised something lately, about the time when I discovered how one uses apostrophes on the word 'its'. I'd never been taught grammar.

Either that or I was just too busy doodling at the time. But, no, I feel that to some extent it was just ASSUMED we knew it from reading other texts and stuff like that. It's almost like there's some sort of attitude around suggesting that because most printed texts are grammatically correct, this will just imprint itself onto us.

Rubbish, in my humble opinion. Perhaps to some extent it helps, but it is always better to be TAUGHT these things, rather than going by intuition.

Grammar runs largely by rules (though they can sometimes contradict other rules or there are two sets out there- the oxford comma, anybody?) and slightly by intuition and personal taste. I think that the rules need to be known and spread amoungst the general public. Why?

Well, you think that that rock and roll and those drugs you do are cool? Well, I don't think YOU realise JUST HOW COOL GRAMMAR can be.

Seriously, though, I think it's important. Because it's curteous. Because it's a lot easier to read and understand a post that is grammatically correct. Because, while not exactly necessary to get the gist of what one person is typing, it is very helpful and will make people's lives a lot easier.

So. This isn't exactly a revolutionary plan to MAKE PEOPLE USE THE CORRECT GRAMMAR. But it's very easy to live in ignorance of the way things work.And thusly I've decided to compile a neat little, occasionally expanding, simple grammar list. To make everyone's lives a little easier. And to make myself look like a self- righteous prick demanding the co- operation of all others. But I still think it's hightime that the news was spread and people begin to use grammar good internet on.

LESSON ONE: CORRECT FORM OF ITS.
Righto. And here we go, emarking upon the seas of grammatical adventure.
This one irritates me a lot, because nowadays I tend to read the form of 'its' that's grammatically correct rather than the one that logic dictates should be placed there. It's confusing and irritating.

And so, here's the simple way it works.

it's : It Is. That's what it means. Simple. If you want to say "It is cold", you can use "It's". It's really quite simple.
its : Belonging to. A nice, clear meaning. For what one might say if one wanted to bring about the vibe of "The feet belonging to it(/he /she) were cold." Instead, you would write "It's feet were cold." The feet belonging to it were cold. This one is slightly odd, since it goes against the vibe from some rules involving apostrophes.

But, anyway, it's (it is) very easy to remember.
It's a cold day.
The planet was the earth, and its dying years were very cold indeed.

LESSON TWO: APOSTROPHES
Apostrophes. For plurals, ONE DOES NOT USE THEM. For saying something belongs to someone/ something, YOU USE THEM. For ommiting a section of a word, YOU DO NOT USE THEM. For a plural of a word ending in a vowel, YOU DO NOT USE THEM. Though you CAN use a tilde (~) if you're a part of that new revolutionary campaign.

But nevermind that last bit.

Bananas: More than one banana. There are several bananas.
Banana's: The banana's... something. Such as, "The banana's skin had been turned blue by some random kids playing paintball."

And then we have things like,
There's/ Don't/ It's: "There is", "Do not", "It is". The apostrophe is shoved in there to show that there are sections of the word missing, or that two larger words have been condensed. It's simple. There's not a lot to it. Please don't omit these apostrophes.

Also, contrary to popular belief, it is "Two Week's Notice"- the notice 'belongs to' the two weeks.
Stupid, stupid movie title.

The tilde: Some groups want to use this to seperate the 's' from the endings of words ending in a vowel. Like, "folio~s" or "banana~s". These groups amuse me almost as much as the groups that want to replace "hello" with "heaveno". But not quite as much.

LESSON THREE: WHERE AND OTHER THINGS LIKE IT
Let's talk about Where.

Where is my mother? At what location is my mother?
Wear the turban, it looks good on you. Put on the turban, it looks good on you.
We were young, happy, and eating ghoulash. We, at a point in the past, have been young, happy, and eating ghoulash.

These ARE NOT INTERCHANGABLE. It is rather irritating constantly reading things that seem to be saying, for instance,
"We (put on) young, happy, and eating ghoulash."
"(it was/ we have been) is my mother?"
"(at what location) the turban, it looks good on you."

Whenever I see things like this screwed up, I want to wrench.

Yes, I did mean wrench. Wrenching is very theraputic. You should try it sometime.

LESSON FOUR: COMMAS AND PERIODS (FULL STOPS): USE THEM
Commas are very good, as they seperate things. They do this much more effectively and easily than other punctuation marks; the semicolon has nothing on the comma.
It is easier to read things when progression of thoughts are seperated, as you can keep track of both your own mind and the mind of the writer more easily. Often, writers on the internet don't put them in, because they're idiots.

It is difficult, reading posts without commas. And wihout full stops. Meanings can get seriously skewed.

dear jack i want a man who knows that love is all about you are generous kind thoughtful people who are not like you admit to being useless and inferior you have ruined me for other men i yearn for you i have no feelings whatsoever when were apart i can be forever happy will you let me be yours jill

Yours,
Jill.[/i]

Grammar is good. Commas are good. Periods are good. USE THEM, PLEASE, and delay my inevitable suicide.

LESSON FIVE: YOU'RE AN IDIOT

Your: Belonging to you- your car, your computer, your lack of grammatical prowress.
You're: You are. The apostrophe shows the middle bit is kinda missing. Remember how we talked about that? Please don't screw it up again.

AND THAT'S ALL FOR NOW, FOLKS.
I may bring out another installment of GRAMMATICAL FUN next time I have serious life- changing decisions to make. Something on, I dunno, colons or dashes or something amazingly exciting like that. But for now, I have to pick my university courses.

I'm considering the whole blindfold- point at something method. It could work.
Or I could end up training as a birthing assistant.

Correct my own grammatical errors on this post and DIE.

'Till the babies start coming,
Goodbye!

To Obby and Keron-
I get the point on mere puppy love and the like, but I also think that there's an argument going on at a slightly... wrong... level here.

Even disregarding issues of trust in the other person entirely- we all tend to get pretty paranoid at times, myself inclusive- it can work if you love them enough, and the feeling is reciprocated, even if you don't know for certain whether it is.
Let's say you've met somebody. You've kissed them and realised that you no longer want to kiss anybody different. (Look- let's just ignore proofs about how this state of mind really, really tends not to last. Purely emotional arguments with no basis on actual facts- that's the llama way.) Even if you don't trust her entirely, if you want nobody else but her, you'd want to try to make it work.
And even if she doesn't trust you entirely, but she wants nobody else but you, ever, she'd want to try.
And if it's really... true... it might just work.

The problem being here, that if you've only met eachother briefly, the other party in question would probably end up looking like an unattainable kind of perfection that nobody else can compete with. They'd look above human, because you wouldn't have had time to learn of your disagreements or annoying idiosyncracies yet.

Come the time when you're reunited (Alright, I admit it, I probably don't think a long term relationship with no hope of ever being reunited could work) you'd probably end up... pretty, iunno, dissapointed.

But I'd like to think that if things between people can last in the way they have between myself and a special somebody. We were apart for 6 months, and we're back together, and I've never been happier.

True, 6 months is nothing compared to some of the lengths of time we're talking about here, but half a year later and I've never known that anything could be so blissful. That anybody could fill my heart with cliche's in quite the way she does.

I still think that they CAN work. And we lasted 6 months apart with no contact- no phone calls, text messages, not even emails, only memories and hopes for the future. It might not sound like a lot, but half a year apart feels that way. Once again, it's extremely tame when compared to the scenarios we're ACTUALLY discussing, but still. THINK OF THE BLISS. AND THE LOVE. AND THE MAKING OF LITTLE BABIES. AND SMALLER BABIES. AND MICROSCOPIC BABIES.

And there, my friends, goes an in- joke you will never understand.

I thought it could be more 'interesting' while it was still... raw, crap, and poorly thought out.

It's fairly terrible, but it's a starting point for a project I've been wanting to get off the ground for a while now. Give it a read if you've got some spare time. And please, don't spare the critique- but keep in mind I have no delusions about the quality of this stuff.

Also, please don't give me advice on the direction of the plot. I've got that down, though I probably should have worked out exactly what would happen in each act and scene before beginning to write...




Shades
Episode 1
Not Fade Away

CAST

REGULARS:
Ben -
Blane -
Simon -
Holly -
Daisy -

RECURRING GUESTS:
Moriarty -
God -

GUESTS:
Thomas (Ghost) -
Jacques (Ghost)-
Charles (Ghost)-
Anne -
(ENTER TEENAGE DELINQUINTS HERE)
Lou-
Mark-
Sarah-

MINOR ROLES:
Inconsequential ghosts (Several)
Frumpy Woman -

[GOD to appear in story arc over first 3 episodes, and again in the 7th.]
[MORIARTY to appear haphazardly during the duration of the first season.]

Overall style of the show: Think the Fuck Forever music video introduction. Yup, something like that.



Teaser, Scene 1

A small apartment bedroom, charmless and cramped. The walls are mostly bare. Its late night, and the room is scarcely lit by streetlight.

[We see a younger BEN stirring from sleep, and a figure by his bed. As he opens his eyes, he starts as he sees THOMAS standing over the bed.]

Thomas: Hi.

Ben: Youre not here.

Thomas: I thought that too, you know. I was wrong.

Ben: Im dreaming.

Thomas: That makes sense.

Ben: Yes. It does.

[A pause, and we see the room revealed again, without Thomas in it.]

[The alarm clock sounds, and it is day. We see BEN rise from bed, enter the bathroom, and wash his face. There is nothing in the mirror, but as BEN turns around, he sees THOMAS immediately behind him. BEN jumps, shocked.]

Ben: Youre not here. So theres a rationalisation. Im dreaming. Or hallucinating. Or something.

Thomas: Try pinching yourself.

[A pause, and then BEN moves back to the bedroom, talking distractedly to THOMAS as he dresses.]

Ben: Or swallowing pills. Medication. For mental instability. That works.

Thomas: How do you know you need it?

Ben: Because Im talking to somebody who isnt here.

Thomas: How do you know Im not?

Ben: Because youre dead.

Thomas: How do you know Im dead?

[A pause. Ben is finished dressing.]

Ben: Because I killed you.

[Exit BEN]

Teaser, Scene 2
L.A, inner city- Morning

[BEN walks through the streets to work. A figure catches his eye, briefly, which seems otherworldly and insubstantial. He walks through a crowd (literally through), and BEN loses sight of him. Some stock footage and fast editing brings us through the rest of the day to the night.]

Teaser, Scene 3
Bens Apartment- Nighttime

[BEN is in bed, and stirs from sleep to see THOMAS standing above him]

Ben: The whole terror of the night thing?

Thomas: Yeah?

Ben: Its a bit of an exaggerated title, dont you think? Mild annoyance and sleep disturbance of the night might be slightly more accurate.

Thomas: I can do more than just irritate.

Ben: [Goadingly] So whos a big scary ghost?

[THOMASS face distorts into something horrible, slimy, and possibly maggoty. With arms outstretched, what remains of Thomas rushes- or, rather, floats- towards Ben and far, far into his personal space. A moment before it touches him, we cut to Ben truly waking up. For a moment, he appears relieved]

Thomas: Bad dream? [BEN starts]

Ben: Oh, its you. [Pause] How could you tell?

Thomas: For how many years did we sleep in the same bedroom when we were kids? You get to know these things.

Ben: How come I could never tell with you?

Thomas: I didnt dream. You, on the other hand, kept a diary of yours. Through your teenage years and everything. Some of them were pretty entertaining.

Ben: Oh. Good to know.

[BEN gets out of bed and pulls on a coat.]

Thomas: The ones containing Lucy were always the most entertaining. Remember the one with the whipped cream and the midgets?

Ben: I honestly dont.

[Still in his pajamas, under the coat, BEN heads out of the apartment.]

Teaser, Scene 4
[A nearby park, with the dawn just beginning to break]

[BEN is sitting a bench. Far across the park, a ghostly figure catches his eye, and he follows it with his eyes, until it disappears behind a clump of trees on the other side of the park. He is relieved that it- whom he believes to be Thomas- hasnt spotted him, but THOMAS is actually behind BEN.]

Thomas: Running isnt going to work.

Ben: Why not?

Thomas: I can walk through walls. It cuts off a lot of distance.

Ben: So how come you can reach floor 30 of my apartment?

Thomas: I can walk into walls, too.

[A pause]

Ben: You had no right.

Thomas: No. I didnt. But how did you?

Ben: Because we were engaged. Because we were planning on having many fat little children and moving into the country and breeding llamas for a living or something like that. Because we were in love.

Thomas: And we werent?

Ben: A happy life. A life with many more llamas and a lot fewer suicides than the life you gave her.

Thomas: Im sorry.

Ben: If I forgive you, will you go away?

Thomas: I wish I knew.

Ben: Does it suck, being a ghost?

Thomas: More than I can say.

Ben: Good.

[A few seconds of stock footage and footage from morning in the apartment plays, the sun goes up and back down again, and we are left in no doubt that a day has just passed.]

Teaser- Scene 5
Early the next night, in the same park

[BEN is sitting on the grass, looking at the sky, when THOMAS approaches. A FRUMPY WOMAN is walking her dog- something small and ridiculous- nearby.]

Thomas: You werent back in the apartment.

Ben: I know, what with being the person who wasnt there and all.

Thomas: You might not want to talk too loudly.

Ben: Why?

Thomas: Because that frumpy woman over there is looking at you as though youre a bit odd.

Ben: [Turning to look at FRUMPY WOMAN] That frumpy woman looks a bit odd, herself.

[The FRUMPY WOMAN overhears Ben and leaves in a huff]

Thomas: Tactful.

Ben: Youre a bastard.

Thomas: And youre a murderer.

Ben: But at least Im sorry. [A pause, and its repeated with far more gravity] Fuck, Im so sorry.

Thomas: So am I.

[The touching reunion is cut short by CGI effects as Thomas fades away in some sort of whirl of trippy, trippy colours.]

Ben: [To the now nonexistent Thomas] So its over now?

[For a few moments, Ben remains in the same position, reaching his hand into where Thomas stood a few moments ago. Eventually, he begins to return to the apartment, deep in thought. Partway there, he spots an INCONSEQUENTIAL GHOST as it walks through the walls of a building. He gives chase for a few steps, until another INCONSEQUENTIAL GHOST catches his eye, walking along the other side of the park. BEN spins around a few times, scanning for more ghosts or information.]

Thomas: [As a disembodied voice] No, Ben. Not for you.

OPENING TITLES
(Gomez- Chasing Ghosts with Alcohol?)


Act 1, Scene 1
City Of Lounge
Bloc Party- So Here We Are

[The room is blackened, and the camera navigates it in sweeping moves as the lights slowly come on. As time passes, we can make out the silhouettes of dancers, drinkers, and motion everywhere- except on the still shape of JACQUES BELAIR]

[The movement on set as well as the lighting matches the music.]

Jacques: Ive always liked to live on a large scale. Tried my best, since I was a kid, to be the top. The best there is. Some people say that its easier to aim low; dive off the low boards before the high ones. Less painful if you realise youre going to hit the water belly first halfway down. I never agreed. I always preferred to forget my reservations and just throw myself off.
It made sense at the time. Throw all of yourself against the universe, hoping that the universe would yield to you, rather than the other way around. And it worked, for a spell. Until the universe stopped yielding to me and I landed belly- first into the chlorinated cesspool of last year. If you aim high and fail, its a bigger fall.
A few days ago I ended up at the top of a rather large building. All I had left in my life was substantial eviction notices and insubstantial memories. Id always liked to live life on a large scale. It was a large drop.


Act 1, Scene 2
[The lighting becomes standard for the rest of the episode, and everything is visible from this point on. The place is alive with dance, drink, and people moving through life- oblivious and a stark contrast to JACQUES, stationary in death. GOD is the only other person not moving or infected in some way by the atmosphere, watching JACQUES.]

[Enter SIMON, HOLLY]

Simon: The place is busy tonight.

Holly: It is. So who reported one of them in here tonight?

Simon: They didnt leave a name.

[A pause]

Simon: Look, so I was thinking, while we wait, if youd maybe like to grab something to drink?

Holly: Probably not a good idea. We should stay alert, hope we see something.

Simon: Okay, sure. That works. Youre right. We should stay on task.

[Another pause]

Simon: Do you want to dance? [Sensing incomprehension] With me?

Holly: Okay. Suddenly I do feel the need for a drink.

[Another pause. Enter BENJAMIN, BLANE]

Blane: I get mystical stuff, yeah. You cant have this gig and not think so. But dragons they cant be anything but old wives tales.

Benjamin: Yes, but who said that old wives tales are doubtful in the first place?

Blane: Does it matter?

Benjamin: The old wives themselves. So who can you trust?

Blane: Explain it, then. How can dragons possibly exist in this world, undetected?

Benjamin: The same way life can exist. And ghosts. Just because you dont understand it, doesnt mean its not there.

[HOLLY and SIMON make their way to the group]

Holly: Hey! Guys! Whatre you going here?

Simon: Yes. What are you doing here?

Blane: Got a call. Somebody in here apparently started acting as though they were convinced there was a ghost in front of them.

Benjamin: Apparently it was a celebration party for a guy who got a promotion. One of the guys was convinced Charles, who used to hang with the group before he died, was sitting in his chair. He panicked, shouting and throwing handfuls of nachos at the empty place. His girlfriend was trying to calm him when he ran off.

Holly: Kind of like Macbeth.

Benjamin: Exactly like Macbeth. Except with some guy in the background complaining about having to clean up guacamole.

Holly: How did he die?

Benjamin: Who? Guacamole guy?

Holly: Charles.

Benjamin Drug overdose is the popular theory.

Holly: So they were druggies. And how do we know the guy who saw his friend wasnt just hallucinating?

Benjamin: We dont, but

Blane: I think I see him.

Holly: Whatever. You guys are here. Im going to go get a drink. Tell me if you need anything.

[HOLLY heads to the bar, not seeing JACQUES. BLANE moves towards JACQUES]

Ben: Howd you get the message before us?

Simon: Didnt. I was here with Holly on a. Umm. Date. With Holly.

Ben: Wait. So you two... You finally asked her out?

Simon: Would have. If you lot hadnt shown up.

Ben: We didnt know you guys were here. We got a call. We heard there was a ghost or a shade of something- thought we should check it out.

Simon: Youve got to be kidding. Ben, theres no ghost here. I just used it as an excuse to talk to Holly. Why did you guys come?

Ben: We got a call. Unless you hired a guy to pretend his friend had gone crazy, theres a shade here.

Simon: Bloody hell.

Ben: So, youre dating Holly, then? Congratulations. When were you planning on telling her?

Simon: Bloody hell.

[SIMON moves to leave]

Ben: Where are you going?

Simon: Out. Away. Someplace thats not here.

[Exit SIMON. BEN moves to rejoin with BLANE, who has reached JACQUES, and GOD, who is staring at JACQUES. Ben moves to talk to JACQUES.]

Blane: Wait. Look.

Ben: At what?

Blane: Him. [BLANE points to GOD]. He can see the ghost.

Ben: Are you sure? Wait, no. Of course.

Blane: So what do we do?

Ben: The same I did with you. Hes a spotter. We talk to him.

Blane: He can see the ghost. Hes a murderer. Could be dangerous. Could be insane. Are you sure you want to try this? [BEN moves to talk to GOD] Ben! Wait a moment!

[GOD turns away from JACQUES to look at Ben and Blane]

God: Hi! Im God! I could be smiting you right now. But Im not. Because Im merciful. And thats a good thing!

Blane: Remember that whole insane thing I was talking about?

Ben: Hi. Im Zeus. Its a pleasure meeting you.

God: No, youre not. Youre a twenty two year old guy trying to test if insane or not by seeing if I treat you like Zeus.

Ben: [To BLANE] He seems alright to me. [To GOD] True, sorry. Really, Im Ben. Its a pleasure meeting you. And Im not one for subtlety, so I was wondering what youd think of coming with us to help ghosts move from the end of this life into the next. Its kind of our calling. And the pay isnt too bad, either. Would you like to join us?

God: Yes.

Ben: See? Hes totally on the level. And he agreed to help us.

Blane: And the fact he just agreed to that by no means makes his claim to sanity seem at least slightly dubious?

Benjamin: No. [Moving towards the exit] Holly! Were leaving.

Holly: Whos the new guy?

Ben & Blane: [Together, Blane disdainfully and Ben enthusiastically.] God.

Holly: Oh. Cool.

[Exit Ben, Blane, and Holly. The lighting begins to dim, and everyone on set seems to eventually disappear, save JAQCUES BELAIR.]

Jacques:
They say that death is the end. The problem is that they dont really speak from experience. If only we were all that lucky.
We are those with deep regrets, those who have been murdered, and those whose unfinished business makes them think theyre not ready for the afterlife yet. Shades are people whose loathing of their killer binds them to this world even after their bodies dont. Ghosts are those who wish- who need- to haunt their killers.
So where does this leave those of us who have committed suicide?
I never told her I loved her. And Ive never hated anybody more than I hated myself for not telling her before I left.
I love her. And in all these years, I never told her.
So how do you haunt yourself? How do you come to peace with yourself? How can you manage to simply fade away?
Or maybe I was never meant to.
Its cold, being dead. Its colder than youd believe, when you dont have a body. And lonely, too. Very.


Act 1, Scene 3
Inside the Shades second- hand bookstore.

Daisy: So it didnt go very well.

Simon: Understatement. Might as well say Tiananmen Square didnt go very well.

Daisy: I went there a few months ago. Its actually pretty, these days.

Simon: How symbolic.

Daisy: Im sorry, Simon. [A pause] Want a coffee or something to drink?

Simon: Tea

Daisy: How English of you.

Simon: And I was trying to keep my nationality secret. Bollocks.


Act 1, Scene 4
A street in the inner city.

[BEN, BLANE, HOLLY and GOD are walking towards the Shades bookstore. BEN and BLANE take the lead, and GOD trails behind, constantly distracted by displays in the windows, cars, and empty space. HOLLY frequently returns to drag him forwards.]

Ben: Does anybody else feel like weve forgotten anything?

Blane: Like what?

Ben: I dont know. Its like that feeling when youre packing clothes and you think youve left behind your razor or something. But you push it to the back of your mind until you end up in Africa and realize you didnt pack any pants.

Blane: No, I think were good. We didnt come with anything. And were returning with an omnipotent being. Which cant be too bad.

Holly: Dont mock him. He might smite you.

Blane: What are we doing with him, anyway?

Ben: He can see them. Were recruiting him. Like we did you. Besides, how can it be a bad thing to have a God around?

Blane: Please. What would a God be doing in Los Angeles, of all places?

Holly: You do know what Los Angeles translates to, right?

[The camera tracks Holly, Blane, Ben and God as they enter the Shades bookstore.]

Daisy: So how did it go?

Ben: Good. We picked up a God.

Daisy: Oh. Is this one of those things that takes a long time to explain?

Ben: Kinda, yeah.

God: Hi. Im God.

Daisy: Pleased to meet you.

[Daisy offers her hand to God, who stares at it curiously]

Blane: Hes all powerful and has infinite wisdom. Can you tell?

Ben: Did Rachel call while we were away?

Blane: Isnt it usually the girl who stresses when the guy doesnt call?

Ben: Are you implying Im being effeminate?

Blane: Do you know how manly using the term effeminate isnt?

Daisy: So wheres the ghost?

[A pause]

Blane: About that

Ben: I told you guys!

Blane: When?

Ben: When we were coming here! I said I felt like wed forgotten something! Like that feeling when you leave the iron on.

Simon: You iron?

Ben: On occasion

Blane: Very manly.

Act 1, Scene 5
City Of Lounge
Vast- Touched

[After an establishing shot, we move in onto BLANE, who is talking with a distracted bartender- Moriarty]

Moriarty: Ah, my dear, unobservant Blane. They were easy deductions. Your tie is loosened, but not undone. Youre breathing heavily. So you came here quickly, and didnt have the time to pre- meditate coming here quickly or the foresight to think of taking your tie off. Judging by the fact you came so quickly, Ill guess you forgot something important. Judging by the fact youre talking to me, Ill assume its about a ghost. Judging by the positions of the scuff marks along the side of your shoes, which appear to be relatively new, Ill assume he was about five foot six, maybe 25 years old when he died, and had brown hair.

Blane: You saw him here, too.

Moriarty: Yeah, of course. I just figured you guys were here to pick him up. You noticed him, obviously. Then you left with some random. And now youre back. Thus, I can easily deduce that youre all either drunk or stupid, and seeing as your speech isnt slurred, Ill go for the second.

Blane: He still around?

Moriarty: Left about 5 minutes ago. Went out the back way. Or, actually, the wall just to the left of the back way. Hell be around someplace.

Blane: Thanks.

Act 1, scene 6
Inner city LA street

[BLANE walks idly through the inner city, looking for a sign of JACQUES. His mobile rings, and he takes the call as he continues to wander the streets.]

Blane: Hello?

Ben: Blane. Any luck?

Blane: No. Talked to Moriarty. The shade left just before we got in. He really needs to lay off the Arthur Conan Doyle.

Ben: Its late. Holly and I are heading off soon. Well call it a night, alright? Just come by to pick your stuff up.

Blane: Sure.

[BLANE hangs up, and turns to head back. ANNE is running in the other direction, carrying coffee and a handbag. She runs into Blane, and is sent sprawling on the sidewalk. Her coffee spills, as do the contents of her handbag- among them, a mobile phone, a cross, several cloves of garlic, and a gun.]

Blane: Sorry! Are you alright?

Anne: [Collecting the items and putting them back into her handbag.] Fine. And dandy. If you ignore the whole sitting on the sidewalk thing with hot coffee spilt on me and the last train back leaving in all of twenty seconds.

Blane: Sorry. You should look where youre going.

Anne: Wow. What perfect timing for your timely warning. [ANNE attempts to stand.] Ow. I think I might have sprained my ankle.

Blane: Are you okay?

Anne: What part of I think I might have sprained my ankle gives you the difficulty? [Begins to limp away] Ouch.

Blane: [Picking up a clove of garlic from the sidewalk] Wait! You forgot your... garlic.

Anne: Thanks.

Blane: Odd sort of a thing to be carrying around in a pink handbag.

Anne: Why? What do you usually carry in your pink handbag?

Blane: Look, its just-

Anne: Its 11.55. The last train leaves in the subway in exactly three minutes and maybe if I hobble fast enough and resist the urge to open about my life to the cause of the coffee spread across my chest, I might just be able catch the thing and return home to lick my wounds and maybe, just maybe, get a good nights sleep.

Blane: Sleep? Leave yourself that vulnerable to vampires?

Anne: Huh?

Blane: Garlic and crosses. People use them to keep vampires away.

Anne: Oh. Right. Umm. Are you sure?

Blane: Pretty.

Anne: Oh. What about silver bullets?

Blane: Thats for werewolves.

Anne: Damnit. Saying the persons name?

Blane: I think it might kill mummies. Or just help you relate to them on a more personal level. One or the other. You really dont watch many horror movies, do you?

Anne: Just none containing vampires. Or, umm, werewolves. Or mummies. [A pause] So what do you usually do for ghosts?

[ANNE suddenly looks apprehensive and vulnerable, and BLANE gets a knowing look. Hes about to say something when we cut.]

End of Act 1

#12589 1 2006-12-02T15:48:55Z Teedle
"Rage", for those of you who don't know it, is a music video program which airs through the night and into the morning on most Fridays 'round where I live. It's the insomniac's dream- music video upon music video to squander away the small hours.

Anyway, I figured that it could be fun to do a hypothetical guest programming of a much shortened version of the epicness which is Rage, to help some suitably bored others shoot off some time. So, make your own mini- programs, and I'll be indebted to you and be glad of something to do during the night.

Anyway, there's no need to introduce every video- just shove in some chunks interspersed with a bit of idle banter and we have our own version of Rage- "Milk Anger"- right here on the metanet forums! And don't label the links- it's nicer not to know what's coming up. A better way to waste time, too.

I'll kick us off with a series of some of both my favourite videos (in regards to artsyness and movingness and coolness visually) and songs...

So, here we go, with Teedle's Odd Few Hours Of Music Video Funness

First up, we have a music band from the absolute embodiment of britpop, Morning Runner- With a groundbreaking new video, in which things move backwards and people come back to life and the song begins with just poppy piano before adding in guitar and a few slightly heavier sections.

Video 1

The Second Video

See what I mean? An entirely original idea.
This next video, by german punk band Die Arzte, holds the world record for the shortest music video at 44 seconds. The song also holds the world record for the shortest single of all time at just over 30 seconds.

Video the Third

Video the Fourth

#5 (five)

The next video is by scene indie rockers Wolf Parade, and the music video is pretty special. It's well- directed, very pretty, and contains guns and people dying and, randomly, a chicken. There's not much not to like.

6 comes after 5

Seven

And this here is probably my favourite video of all time. It's by Ok Go, and it's all filmed on a oner. Dancing on treadmills. Just awesome.

Eiiiiight

The ninth video! Wow!

Ten. Now here's a great milestone, right here.

Okkervil River's "For Real" is a song I love and a video I love. Yay for it. They're kinda edgy, it's kinda dark, and somehow disturbing in a saladfingers-esque sort of way. Or maybe that's just me. I am kinda unusual.

11: The One One

I Bet You Wouldn't Have Guessed That This Is Video Twelve

13, the lucky one

Anywho, Silence by Gomez has a pretty trippy clip. Enjoy it! Random colours and stuff. Yay for them.

Fourteen
Really, I think you've got the hang of counting. It's the one after fourteen, and the one before sixteen. Take a guess.

This was a pretty amazing video when it came out, in a "Yay for topless guys!" sort of a way. It's quite famous, and needs no introduction. Which is exactly why I'm introducing it- Red Hot Chilli Peppers, Californication

Sixteen

And no introduction could do this last clip justice. It's just... beautiful. Perfect way to end a binge of youtube music videos. Enjoy!

The Last Video (17)



And now, my friends, I am off to bed. Please load us up with some 'programs' of your own? That'd be simply awesome.

Quote: Macaddict, 2006-12-13T22:25:57Z
Oh, and while we're on transitional fossils, here's a list of 'missing links' thought to have connected dinosaurs and birds, and the reasons why they were rejected:

Archaeoraptor, though an article appeared in National Geographic entitled "Feathers for T-Rex?", was actually a fraud. The company posted a partial retraction on their website.

Bambiraptor was dated to be 75 million years younger than Archeapteryx, and had not a single trace of feathers found near or with it. Nevertheless, cladists said they should be there, so they were included in the description of the fossil.

Sinosauropteryx prima was thought to be proof in 1996. However, the feathers turned out to be fibers, and it was put onto a side branch.

Monoykus claimed to be a flightless bird, drawn with feathers even though no trace of feathers were found. D.P. Prothero and R. M. Schoch, editors of "Major Features of Vertebrate Evolution", said "Monoykus was clearly not a bird...it clearly was a fleet-footed fossorial theropod."

Protarchaeopteryx robusta and Caudipteryx zoui were reported to be links in the vast chain in June of 1998. They cannot, however, be the ancestors of modern birds when Archeapteryx is dated about 30 million years older than them.
