#13065 1 2006-12-22T13:46:57Z Teedle
aight, guys, listen up. I just sent this in an epic e-mail to a certain special canadian, and decided to share a slightly edited version with you guys.

It's a true story. Well, almost. It's been embellished a little bit, admittedly- but it's pretty damn close to the true story. And I mean damn close.

CHAPTER ONE: You cannot boil the fish, sorry but

It was a dark and stormy night.

Actually, it was a warm and humid day, but it was overcast and humid and occasionally spitting the variety of rain that doesn't so much serve to cool things down or provide water as to provide a sort of secondary, slightly more intense humidity to the air.

This doesn't have much bearing on the story, but it does give you an idea of just how wonderfully uncomfortable the weather has made me; and how I was feeling inside the train, which is where the bulk of this story was set.

It all started around Flinders Street Station- where the goths have been misplaced (or possibly converted to) the emos, and where the clocks show times from around the world for some complex reason quite possibly involving terms like 'trans- cultural', 'society', or 'unification'. And a train which was leaving at neither the right time nor the right platform as, in a more perfect world NOT run by connex, it would have.

Turns out that connex where having even more competency problems than they usually do. The trains were in chaos, going where they shouldn't at the wrong times from the wrong platforms as the entire system continued to lag up as trains, somehow, against all reasoning, managed to gridlock themsleves. And it is against this backdrop- one of a world gone mad- where I lay my scene.

My friend and I part our ways, heading onto seperate trains to make our way home. He was the lucky one- his train went halfway through to the next station, paused for quite a while, and then the driver walked through to the other end of the train and they slowly rolled back to Flinders Street, spending only 1/2 hour or so sitting around wedged between two other trains.

Myself? My train paused for a while, then made its way down to Southern Cross station, where an announcement came over the loudspeaker. I didn't quite hear it, being pre- occupied listening to the Shout Out Louds on my mp3 player. So I took my headphones out, listening to the announcement to see what was up and why, suddenly, there were only a few people left in the carriage, making their way to the doors. Turns out we were supposed to get off the train and head to the next platform down, where the service would continue as THIS train was now going to go out of service. I stand up and head for the doors, when I notice there's still a guy sitting near where I was, fast asleep.

What could I do? Everybody else has ignored him, so I run back loudly saying "Mate, you have to get off this train now." and then giving his shoulder a bit of a push to try to get him moving so he doesn't wind up stuck on a train headed to god- knows- where which doesn't stop at any of the stations.

Now this is all well and good. But as I do this, I hear a beeping noise, and spring to the doors to watch them close, lock, and feel the train begin to move. The 'next station' signs flick to 'not in service', and I start to worry. I look back to the guy I was trying to wake, when I notice that- while not the stereotypical terrifying muscular type of guy- he was still rather heavily tattooed on one side, had a kinda extreme haircut, and just looked like a rather unpleasent sort of fellow. Insofar as you can tell based on looks.

But what with the paint- speckled pants, the facial piercings, what appeared to be a wiry kind of strength in his muscles, the facial hair, and the ridiculous amount of tattoos spinning their way painfully down the side of his body, he did look a little frightening.

During the time I'm contemplating this, the train is moving through the city loop, rushing past the stations when we near them and I see nothing but glimpses of slightly blurred faces looking at the train as it rushes past. All of this has been underground, and I notice as I try to text my friend to tell him what happened, that I have no reception. And then the train starts to slow down. And eventually stop.

In the middle of part of an underground system. Nothing is visible outside of the carriage but a slight suggestion of nearby concrete in the blackness. We are, insofar as I can tell, far, far away from any station.

Picture it. One sole man, standing in an empty train, hanging onto one of the green- painted metal poles, surrounded by blackness. The other carriages are ahead, and there's nothing in them but empty seats. Presumably, somewhere at the other end of the train, there's a driver. I, on the other hand, am at the exact opposite end- the last carriage. Then the engine of the train stops idling and seems to shut down entirely, and I keep on standing there, looking around, wondering just what to do. I flip out the phone and look at it again- no reception.

I hear a noise behind me, and turn around. It's the other guy. The one with large amounts of body art, slight facial hair, and his mp3 player still blasting out grunge music he had fallen asleep to- now audible in the empty carriage. He lets out another groaning sound, and opens his eyes. They're very, very bloodshot. I'm standing entirely still at this moment, looking at him from a few metres away. His eyes focus on me-

And the lights flicker. And for a split second, there's nothing but a blackness darker than pitch and some grunge music coming from headphones a few metres from me.

And THAT ranks as the most frightening moment in my life so far.

CHAPTER TWO: The unsatisfying conclusion

Yup, so, that's pretty much it. My heart's beating three times the usual rate at this point in time, and though I feel no particular inclination to wet myself, it seems traditional to do so at a time like this and I'm contemplating it. Anyway, the other guy gets up, swears a bit, and asks me where we are. I explain, and he asks why I'm still on the train. I say I tried to wake him when I got locked in too, and he seems pretty appreciative. He says he's been drinking a lot, and that's why he was pretty out of it.

Anyway, we find one of those red emergency buttons in the carriage. With a label saying "WARNING: Pressing this button will activate CCTV and emergency procedures", and while I'm wondering whether or not it's a good idea to press it, my new friends of the tattoos presses it for me and kindly spares me from an internal monolouge. It dials for a full minute or two before somebody picks up. (Huh, they sure treat their emergencies seriously.) Tatooman explains that there's still two of us on this train, and we're told it should wind up back at Flinders Street Station. Eventually.

So we sit back down, both of us sprawling over a full three seats each, waiting for the train to start to move again. The engine starts again (or possibly just starts idlying much more noisily) and eventually we casually roll back to Flinders Street, stopping at a platform I never knew existed, where nobody at all boards the train, very little light reaches, and there's little sign of life untill you reach th part near the bottom of the esculaters, where it merges with another platform and there are, thankfully, people.

I reach the light, and bump into my friend, who caught a different train, once more. And together we catch a different train which gradually makes its way back home.

THE END

No, it really isn't. When you think that you're shit, it projects into your body language. People will think you're shit too. People won't want to get to know you; you'll be alone. You might as well try to give up getting a job as well; honestly try to get a job when you project that you're shit and there's definitely someone better out there than you.

On the opposite side, confidence is a good thing to have. That projects in your body language as well. People will want to be around you if you love yourself and think you're amazing. Women love confidence. Going to job interviews will be a breeze; the people will think that you're amazing and perfect for the job if you think that about yourself. It's all relative.

And there are plenty of jobs that don't require a great deal of self- confidence. Incidentally, these are the types of jobs I would like above anything else. Writing (albeit for television moreso than novels), music, anything artistic- these sorts of things appeal to me more than anything else. These are the sorts of things that I think I could do, and be happy doing. The greatest artists, musicians and poets tend to be pretty messed up. Not to mention there being a much higher incidence of suicide among the greatest of these people than, say, among the greatest bankers or franchise creators throughout history.

On top of which, I reckon I'm a lot closer with my group of close friends than most people are with their groups of large friends. Possibly some kind of tradeoff, possibly some kind of comsic fairy balance, but when you wind up spending New Years Eve with two people you know you'd die for and know would do the same for you, it feels slightly amazing.

Basically, I reckon that like attracts like. And I don't subscribe to the whole shallow "YOU are important! YOU are worth it! YOU DESERVE FRUITY FRUITNESS HAIRWASH!!!" line of thinking. I'm not worth it; what I want isn't the most important thing in the world. And I don't like who I am, but I'm- in some ways- cool with that.

And, finally, despite everything you've said, I don't see how any of it makes the lack of an unreasonably bloated sense of self- esteem a bad thing for anybody other than the person without it. Which in turn probably aids other people. If nothing else, the job you miss WILL go to somebody else, and maybe they need it more than you do. Maybe the individuals don't gain anything, but maybe the world does. And maybe, just maybe, that's worth it.

Okay, yes, I realise I've veered way, WAY off topic here. But I still reckon that was worth posting, even if I have gone from talking about my opinion of myself to something probably closer to my worldview. But anyway.

Now where have I read something like this before... Ah, yes, that's right... I seem to remember Sythe posting a very helpful wikipedia link...

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argument_from...ncredulity'

Quote: Wiki
Argument from personal incredulity

Two common versions of the argument from personal incredulity are:

    * "I can't believe this is possible, so it can't be true" (The person is asserting that a proposition must be wrong because he or she is (or claims to be) unable or unwilling to fully consider that it might be true, or is unwilling to believe evidence which does not support her or his preferred view.)
    * "That's not what people say about this; people instead agree with what I am saying." (Here the person is asserting that a proposition must be inaccurate because the opinion of "people in general" is claimed to agree with the speaker's opinion, without offering specific evidence in support of the alternative view.) This is also called argumentum ad populum.

An argument from personal incredulity is the same as an argument from ignorance only if the person making the argument has solely their particular personal belief in the impossibility of the one scenario as "evidence" that the alternative scenario is true (i.e., the person lacks relevant evidence specifically for the alternative scenario).

Quite commonly, the argument from personal incredulity is used in combination with some evidence in an attempt to sway opinion towards a preferred conclusion. Here too, it is a logical fallacy to the degree that the personal incredulity is offered as further "evidence." In such an instance, the person making the argument has inserted a personal bias in an attempt to strengthen the argument for acceptance of her or his preferred conclusion.

#293439 36 2007-02-04T02:35:16Z Teedle
So it's been awhile since I've gone onto NUMA, but I decided to give it a shot. It's been said several, several times before, but just to restate it once more with feeling:

The problem with NUMA is the emphasis on ratings and the competetive nature of it. With the author rankings page, the top rated maps page, and all the rest of it, it becomes about beating other people rather than sharing maps.

Comments become in the vein of "its alrght 3/5", talking about the ratings and little else. Maps become rated down without explanation or advice (ala sniping), maps become resubmitted when they're lacking in ratings, and people get pissed off. A lot.
People also just become apathetic about ratings (on account of them not meaning anything anymore), like I did, and hence also become apathetic about NUMA in general. For me, NUMA has mostly been about the ratings- after all, what else is there, really?- and when you're fed up with how little they mean to the population of NUMA in general, you kinda lose the motivation.

It's also been pointed out to me that I only have a ratio of maps made to ratings of about 1:4.6. The reason for this is as follows: I enjoy making maps more than playing them, I prefer giving comments to ratings, I give bad ratings. They vary from day to day and mood; I tend to see the flaws in popular maps and recognise greatness in far less popular maps.

I understand why this is a 'problem', mostly- but I still don't think it should be. If you prefer to make maps, that should be fine. If you prefer to rate them, that should be fine.

The thing is that this shouldn't be a call to abolish the ratings system: It's good, it's useful, and it's nice to see that other people have appreciated your map or get to learning what sorts of maps other people like.

THE THRILLING CONCLUSION

What we DO need is a way to... add... something else. I'm not sure what, but we need more features to make NUMA more about making and playing maps than rating them or makings the ones which get the best ratings.

It's not a competition, and that it is sours the community. I dislike the NUMA- going community while I like the metanet community, despite how similar they mostly are, for this exact reason.

The liberty to be homosexual or practise religion is less likely to be harmful to others. And we do need to deprive people from certain liberties, if they do (or can) harm others. Absolute liberty and laws used to protect people don't, as a general rule, go well together.



And on the topic at hand-
I was at school backstage in theatre studies, where two friends of mine were messing around with two guns used as props. The stage manager, a random classmate (who has no soul) came in and started yelling at them, saying that "That is TOTALLY inappropriate behaviour, considering what just happened in America with the gun massacre." At which point I said something about America happening to be far, far away and nobody in our year level ever having lived in America, and that I'm fairly sure there's always a recent tragedy involving firearms having happened recently, even if not in America, and how unreasonable it is to take offence at these actions.

At which point Rob pretended to fire the gun at me and we launched into a rather intricate, dramatic, and awesome death scene which ended in a round of applause and Chloe, the stage manager, leaving in a huff.

So juvenile. But so much fun.

(Of course, here, considering that people are somewhat more affected than in a random school in Australia, I think I need to put a disclaimer that I truly mean no disrespect. It's only that I believe that there are constantly tragedies happening which don't affect me, and this is just one of the very few of which I am aware have happened. So I can't say I see much importance in changing anybody's behaviour because of it- at least while everybody is entirely unaffected by it.)

#336210 32 2007-06-27T05:12:10Z Teedle
I like to think of myself as something classier than an asshole, though. A classhole, if you will.

Anyway, once more with feeling, for the people who haven't exactly gathered this yet merely from my saying so not once but twice...

I haven't 'returned.' I got an e-mail in an account I don't check all that often, and decided to see how this place was. I decided I might post an update on my life, maybe check the thread and answer one or two questions (On, say, my friend's project which wound up on the backburn after we had difficulty finding a good place and way to host it) and post a borderline amusing picture of myself a friend took before a party a few weeks ago, and a link to a live recording of a song I'm loving at the moment.

I wound up sticking in this thread after B_T pulled another random spasm of spazzfulness, 'cause I still have this ingrained desire to point out he's a dick when he proves himself to be. Habit, I suppose. But never mind that.

The thing is that... nobody really cares. Until B_T posted for the first time, the thread was pretty much filled with 'bahas' and 'lmaos' and presumably nobody _thought_ I was having a grand comeback until B_T started saying how sick he was of them.

I thought it'd be amusing to write again and say a friendly "hello" to everybody here after a couple of months of inactivity, after Keron sent me a random, friendly PM sparked by some stuff we talked about ages ago. (Mostly, me sending him my love... and refusing to let him reject my love... and hiding my love in dark alleyways to jump out at him... and sacrificing virgins in his name. You know, normal stuff.) Sorry if anybody took it the wrong way or found that offensive somehow. Well, actually, I'm not. You'd have to be borderline retarded to do so.

But look- I'm getting about 1, 1 and a half hours of spare time these days. I still use my laptop a lot- I'll have msn running in the background while studying history and the like- but really, in terms of things I could do with the time I have, shooting the breeze at this place- pleasant as that sometimes is- doesn't come high on the list. Maybe in November that'll change and you'll all be justified in letting out a chorus of "Why did TDL return?" groans, but considering how violently some people want me away from here and the fact I was never exactly planning on it anyway, I don't think you need to worry too much.

Seriously. I'm a bigger man. And moving onto better things.
But I love her. Because she moves in her own way...
